method: Built by the CMC/Module 3 lane on 2026-10-04 from a multi-agent research run: one researcher per authority group (ICH; FDA; EU; UK and Switzerland; Japan and Korea; China; Canada and Australia; Brazil, India, Singapore, WHO and PIC/S), each re-verified by an independent agent that re-searched every source and corrected or deleted unsupported entries, plus four academic deep dives citing peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/PMC) and industry white papers. Regulator websites could not be fetched from the build environment, so facts rest on corroborating search results and literature; each entry carries its confidence and what could not be established. Check a draft or low-confidence entry against the authority before relying on it.

sources.code: Food and Drug Regulations, C.R.C., c. 870, Part C, Division 5 (ss. C.05.001 et seq.)
sources.title: Food and Drug Regulations, Part C, Division 5: Drugs for Clinical Trials Involving Human Subjects
sources.scope: The legal basis for Canadian clinical trial applications for drugs, including biologics. The researcher maps the following provisions (not re-verified): C.05.005 application content, including chemistry and manufacturing information for drugs with no DIN or NOC; C.05.006 30-day default authorization; C.05.008 and related sections for amendments and notifications; C.05.010 sponsor obligations, including GCP and manufacture, handling and storage under applicable GMP; C.05.012 record keeping, with 15-year retention. Independently corroborated: Division 5 governs trials of drugs and biologics. A CTA is needed for drugs not authorized for sale in Canada, or used outside their marketed parameters. Review runs 30 days from receipt of a complete application, and Health Canada answers with a No Objection Letter (NOL) or a Not Satisfactory Notice (NSN).
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: Core facts are corroborated by two retrieved peer-reviewed full texts. PMID 40303377 (2025, co-authored by Health Canada BRDD staff) confirms Division 5 as the legal basis, the 30-day review of a complete application, and the NOL/NSN responses. PMID 30984761 (2019) confirms the 30-day default review, NOL, NSN, and that CTAs cover clinical and quality review for Phase I-III. NOT re-verified, because the web search budget was exhausted and regulator sites were blocked: the 2001 coming-into-force date, the individual section numbers, the 15-year retention period, and the page-65 URL (Justice Laws consolidation page numbers change, so link the section pages). Division 5 is in force; its proposed replacement was not re-verified.
sources.supersededBy: hc-proposed-ct-regs-2025 (proposed; not in force as of 2026-10-04; pre-publication not re-verified)

sources.scope: Process and format guidance for CTAs, CTA amendments (CTA-A) and notifications (CTA-N). Covers the three-module CTA structure, the 30-day default review, the 7-day administrative target for comparative bioavailability and some Phase I healthy-volunteer trials, the Phase IV exemption, and electronic filing.
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: NOT re-verified; the web search budget was exhausted and canada.ca was blocked. The 30-day review and the NOL/NSN outcomes are corroborated by PMIDs 40303377 and 30984761, but this document's identity and dates are not. The researcher's own uncertainty stands: the dates (adoption 2003-06-25, revision 2011-11-07, effective 2013-05-29) came from one Open Government summary; a 2016-03-17 revision was reported by a secondary source only; the current 'date modified' is unknown. A draft replacement dated 2025-12-20 was reported but not re-verified.

sources.code: Canada Gazette, Part I, Vol. 159, No. 51 (2025-12-20): Clinical Trials Regulations (proposed)
sources.title: Clinical Trials Regulations (proposed); with Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Relating to Clinical Trials
sources.scope: Proposed stand-alone framework for clinical trials of human drugs, intended to replace FDR Part C Division 5 with risk-based lifecycle oversight. Health Canada's modernization proposals, as described by Health Canada co-authors in 2025, are: a proportional risk-based approach; single authorization of a multi-arm trial, with partial suspension or cancellation; agile lifecycle terms and conditions; enabling decentralized trials; and new registration and results-reporting policy.
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: NOT re-verified, so downgraded from high. The policy direction is corroborated by PMID 40303377 (2025), but the Canada Gazette I pre-publication (date, volume and issue), the consultation dates (2025-12-20 to 2026-04-19) and the projections (Canada Gazette II spring 2027; in force spring 2028) were not. Whether the regulations remain unpublished in Canada Gazette II as of 2026-10-04 was not established.

sources.code: Australian clinical trial handbook (TGA guidance; reported Version 2.0 2018-03-15; web 'Guidance' edition updated 2024-10-03)
sources.title: Australian clinical trial handbook: Guidance on conducting clinical trials in Australia using 'unapproved' therapeutic goods
sources.scope: Describes the CTN and CTA schemes and their legal basis. Covers sponsor responsibility for investigational product quality and GMP, including overseas manufacture; the Schedule 7 manufacturing exemption for first-in-human studies; licensing of other Australian IMP manufacture; mandatory CTA for Class 4 biologicals; the HREC role; and the data evaluated under CTA.
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: The version history (2006-03; v2.0 2018-03-15; v2.4 2021-08-01; web migration 2024-10-03) was NOT re-verified. Several scheme facts the handbook is cited for are corroborated by PMID 40303377: the sponsor and then the HREC choose CTN or CTA; CTA is mandatory for Class 4 biologicals with stated exceptions; there is no TGA data evaluation under CTN. The GMP and Schedule 7 content was not corroborated.

sources.title: Recommendations for Regulating the Environmental Risk of Shedding for Gene Therapy and Oncolytic Viruses in Canada (Bubela T, Boch R, Viswanathan S; Front Med 2019;6:58)
sources.scope: Full text verified. Viral vectors (including non-replicating ones, as 'virus-like or sub-viral particles') and oncolytic viruses are regulated as micro-organisms under CEPA 1999 and NSNR(O), with a 120-day statutory ECCC review once the information package is complete, independent of Health Canada's 30-day CTA review. CTAs are required for all Phase I-III trials for clinical and quality review. Health Canada issues an NOL, seeks clarification by 'Clarifax' with a 2-day response expectation, and may issue an NSN. A Health Canada cell therapy CTA guidance exists. As of 2019 there was no approved ECCC guidance for vectors, only a draft.
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: Bibliographic data and full text re-verified. The content reflects the 2018-2019 situation; whether the recommended reforms were adopted is unknown.

sources.title: Comparison of regulatory framework of clinical trial with genetically modified organism-containing vaccines in the Europe, Australia, and Switzerland (Jose J, Pai S; Clin Exp Vaccine Res 2021;10(2):93-105)
sources.scope: Comparative review of GMO-containing vaccine trial regulation, including Australia's Gene Technology Act 2000. Background for the parallel gene-technology requirements for GMO investigational products in Australia.
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: Bibliographic data re-verified in PubMed. This is a secondary review; no official OGTR source was retrieved, so no requirement is anchored on it.

sources.title: Requirements and special considerations for drug trials with children across six jurisdictions: 1. Clinical trial application review in the regulatory approval process (Stewart B, Lepola P, Egger GF, et al.; Front Med (Lausanne) 2025;12:1542408)
sources.scope: Full text verified. Canada: FDR Part C Division 5 governs drug and biologic trials. A CTA is needed for drugs not authorized in Canada and for marketed drugs used outside their authorized parameters (indication, population, route, dosage regimen), and not for NOC drugs used within them or for observational studies. Pharmaceuticals go to PDD; biologics, radiopharmaceuticals and cell and gene therapies go to BRDD. CTAs and CTA amendments are reviewed in 30 days from receipt of a complete application, with an NOL or NSN response. The modernization proposals are risk-based. Australia: the TGA administers the CTN and CTA schemes for unapproved goods (not on the ARTG, or used beyond their marketing conditions). The choice of scheme lies first with the sponsor and then with the HREC, depending on the HREC's expertise. CTA is mandatory for Class 4 biologicals with exceptions. CTN involves no TGA data evaluation and is processed in about 5 days; CTA involves TGA evaluation of safety aspects, with a 50-day target timeframe. The TGA inspects trial sites, and a National One Stop Shop is in development.
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: Added by the verifier and retrieved in full via PMC. Survey responses date from 2020-21, re-polled in 2024. It does not cover CMC dossier content and does not say whether the 50-day TGA target is in working or calendar days.

sources.title: Requirements and special considerations for drug trials with children across six jurisdictions: 2. Ethics review in the regulatory approval process (Stewart B, Lepola P, Egger GF, et al.; Front Med (Lausanne) 2025;12:1539787)
sources.scope: Full text verified. Australian trials of unapproved goods must comply with the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989, the National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research, GCP and other legislation. HRECs must be registered. A National One Stop Shop is under development.
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER 2026-10-05: Added by the verifier and retrieved in full via PMC. It focuses on ethics review, not CMC.

sources.title: Navigating ICH Q2(R2) compliance in analytical method validation: A gap analysis toolkit to streamline risk assessment and change management (Cassidy B, Bloomingdale T, Carmody J; J Pharm Sci 2025;114(6):103749)
sources.scope: States that ICH officially adopted Q2(R2) and Q14 as harmonised guidelines on 2023-11-01, and identifies 56 differences between Q2(R1) and Q2(R2).

sources.code: Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (2019 revision)
sources.title: Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (中华人民共和国药品管理法), revised 2019
sources.scope: National statute. The date field is the effective date (2019-12-01). Corroborated content: makes the marketing authorization holder (MAH) system nationwide, separating marketing authorization from manufacturing authorization; incorporates sponsor-regulator communication mechanisms and the 60-working-day silent (implied) approval of clinical trial applications. Content from researcher recollection, not corroborated here: review of chemical APIs together with the drug product and joint review of excipients and direct-contact packaging; approval of the quality standard, manufacturing process, label and package insert at marketing approval; ChP and NMPA drug standards as national drug standards; GMP compliance for manufacturing.
sources.uncertainty: Checked through PubMed only. WebSearch was exhausted (200/200) and no official-domain snippet was retrieved. Corroborated: the 2019 revision took effect 2019-12-01 (PMID 39307761; PMID 41994443; PMID 36561995). The MAH system became nationwide under this law (PMID 40918402; PMID 42776789). The DAL and DRR incorporate the 60-working-day silent IND approval and the communication mechanisms (PMID 36561995, single source). NOT corroborated: the adoption date 2019-08-26 (12th session of the 13th NPC Standing Committee), Presidential Order No. 31, and all article numbers (for example Art. 19 and Art. 25). PMID 42678023 wrongly calls this the '2020 revision'. The URL is the NPC homepage; no deep link was verified.
supersedes: Drug Administration Law of the PRC (promulgated 1984, revised 2001, as subsequently amended)

sources.code: SAMR Order No. 27 (国家市场监督管理总局令第27号)
sources.title: Provisions for Drug Registration (药品注册管理办法)
sources.scope: Implementing regulation for drug registration. Promulgated 2020-01-22, published March 2020, effective 2020-07-01. Covers clinical trial applications (60-working-day silent approval), marketing authorization, associated review of APIs, excipients and packaging, registration testing, and risk-based on-site inspection with in-parallel review. Expedited pathways: breakthrough therapy (new in this revision), conditional approval, priority review and special approval. Also covers post-approval changes and renewal. Time limits are counted in working days: standard marketing-application review 200 working days, priority review 130. Recollected but not corroborated: changes during trials, supplementary applications and DSUR provisions, and lapse of clinical trial approval if no subject is enrolled within 3 years.
sources.uncertainty: Checked through PubMed only. Corroborated: SAMR is the issuer (PMID 32656769; PMID 42453401). Order No. 27 of 2020 is confirmed by PMID 42453401 and PMID 42776789 (the latter wrongly calls it an 'NMPA Order'). Promulgation on 2020-01-22 rests on PMID 42453401 alone. Public release in March 2020 is from PMID 32656769. Effect from 2020-07-01 is confirmed by PMIDs 32656769, 36561995 and 42678023. The 200 and 130 working-day review limits are confirmed by PMIDs 41075154 and 42776789. Breakthrough therapy, in-parallel review and risk-based on-site inspection are from PMID 36561995. NOT corroborated: the 3-year lapse rule, the DSUR and supplementary-application provisions, and every article number. The URL is the SAMR homepage. Repo defect confirmed: shared/regulatory/global-document-registry.ts line 167 reads 'NMPA Order 2019 No. 27' and '60-day tacit approval'. The corroborated values are SAMR Order No. 27 (2020) and 60 working days.
supersedes: Provisions for Drug Registration, 2007 revision (SFDA Order No. 28; the order number is unverified)

sources.code: SAMR Order No. 28 (国家市场监督管理总局令第28号)
sources.title: Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Drug Manufacturing (药品生产监督管理办法)
sources.scope: Manufacturing licensing, GMP compliance inspections (including the pre-approval GMP compliance inspection linked to registration) and MAH manufacturing obligations. Effective 2020-07-01 (recollection).
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated: PubMed searches found nothing and WebSearch was unavailable. The order number, the promulgation date (believed to be the same day as Order No. 27) and the 2020-07-01 effective date are model recollections. The URL is the SAMR homepage.

sources.code: NMPA Announcement 2018 No. 50 (国家药品监督管理局关于调整药物临床试验审评审批程序的公告)
sources.title: Announcement on Adjusting the Review and Approval Procedures for Drug Clinical Trials
sources.scope: Introduced implied (silent) approval of clinical trial applications and the pre-IND communication meeting in 2018. Both were later codified in the 2019 DAL and the 2020 Provisions for Drug Registration.
sources.uncertainty: The announcement number and date are not corroborated. PMID 36561995 says only that the 60-working-day silent IND approval was a 'time-tested' practice before it was incorporated into the DAL/DRR. It does not name this announcement. Unverified recollection: the 2018 text may have set '60 days' rather than '60 working days'. The 60-working-day limit is the DAL/DRR rule. Whether this announcement was formally repealed is not established, so status is 'unknown'. The URL is the NMPA homepage.

sources.code: NMPA Notice 2020 No. 44 (国家药监局关于发布《化学药品注册分类及申报资料要求》的通告)
sources.title: Registration Classification and Application Dossier Requirements for Chemical Drugs (化学药品注册分类及申报资料要求)
sources.scope: Defines chemical drug registration categories (1 innovative; 2 improved new; 3-5 generic or imported) and requires dossiers in ICH M4 CTD structure: CN Module 1, Module 2 summaries (2.3 QOS), Module 3 quality, and Modules 4-5. Applies to clinical trial and marketing applications from 2020-07-01 (recollection).
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The notice number and the 2020-06-30 date are model recollections. PMID 41075154 says only that chemical classification was reformed in March 2016 and that 'new registration classification rules for biologics and Chinese medicines' came in March 2020, probably meaning the DRR published that month. It does not confirm this notice's number or date. The Module 1 content list and phase-specific allowances for clinical trial applications are unverified.
supersedes: cn-cfda-2016-80-chem-ctd

sources.code: NMPA Notice 2020 No. 43 (国家药监局关于发布《生物制品注册分类及申报资料要求》的通告)
sources.title: Registration Classification and Application Dossier Requirements for Biological Products (生物制品注册分类及申报资料要求)
sources.scope: Defines registration categories for preventive biologics (vaccines), therapeutic biologics (including cell and gene therapy products) and IVD reagents regulated as drugs. Requires CTD-structured dossiers (CN Module 1 plus ICH M4 Modules 2-5) for therapeutic and preventive biologics.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated: the number and date are model recollections. PMID 41075154 dates new biologics classification rules to 'March 2020', which conflicts with the 2020-06-30 date if it refers to this notice. It more likely refers to the DRR. PMID 42776789 confirms that CGTs are regulated as a sub-category of biological products. Whether IVD reagents use a full CTD Module 3 is unverified.

sources.code: CFDA Notice 2016 No. 80 (总局关于发布化学药品新注册分类申报资料要求（试行）的通告)
sources.title: Application Dossier Requirements for the New Registration Classification of Chemical Drugs (Trial) (化学药品新注册分类申报资料要求（试行）)
sources.scope: Issued after the March 2016 chemical drug registration classification reform. Required CTD-format pharmaceutical (药学) data for the new chemical drug categories.
sources.uncertainty: PMID 41075154 corroborates only the March 2016 classification reform, not this notice's number, date or content. Supersession by NMPA 2020 No. 44 is inferred, not confirmed.

sources.title: Notice on Matters Concerning Preparing Chemical Drug Registration Dossiers in CTD Format (关于按CTD格式撰写化学药品注册申报资料有关事项的通知)
sources.scope: First introduction of CTD-format pharmaceutical (Module 3-equivalent) dossiers for chemical drug registration in China.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The document number and date are model recollections. Whether the format was voluntary or mandatory, and for which categories, is unverified. Supersession by the 2016 and 2020 dossier requirements is inferred. Historical only; do not cite for current submissions.

sources.code: CFDA Announcement 2018 No. 10 (总局关于适用国际人用药品注册技术协调会二级指导原则的公告)
sources.title: Announcement on Applying ICH Level-2 Guidelines (including M4 CTD)
sources.scope: First post-accession adoption of ICH guidelines, including M4 (CTD). Applied M4 to defined new-drug categories (chemical category 1 and 5.1; therapeutic and preventive biologics category 1) from 2018-02-01 (recollection).
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The announcement number, the date, the list of guidelines adopted (believed to be M4, E2A, E2D, M1 and E2B(R3)) and the 2018-02-01 start date for M4 are model recollections.

sources.code: ICH Assembly decision, 2017 (CFDA, now NMPA, admitted as ICH Regulatory Member)
sources.title: ICH Members & Observers - China NMPA (formerly CFDA) Regulatory Member
sources.scope: CFDA (renamed NMPA in 2018) became an ICH Regulatory Member in 2017. It was elected to the ICH Management Committee in 2018 and re-elected in 2021 and 2024. Most ICH guidelines have been implemented since accession. ICH publishes implementation status per member and per guideline. The ICH website began showing ChP's ICH Q4B implementation status in 2020.
sources.uncertainty: Five independent PubMed sources confirm 2017 Regulatory Membership: PMIDs 41075154, 40150438, 36561995, 34513116 and 42776789. The month (June 2017, Montreal Assembly) is not corroborated, so the date is given to the year. Management Committee election in 2018, 2021 and 2024 rests on PMID 42776789 alone. PMID 41075154 says 'most' ICH guidelines are implemented. NMPA's status for each Q guideline (for example Q2(R2)/Q14, Q12, Q13, Q1 revision, Q3E, M4Q(R2)) was NOT established. Check the ICH implementation tables before citing a specific guideline as in force in China.

sources.code: CFDA Announcement 2017 No. 146 (总局关于调整原料药、药用辅料和药包材审评审批事项的公告)
sources.title: Announcement on Adjusting Review and Approval Matters for APIs, Pharmaceutical Excipients and Packaging Materials
sources.scope: Ended separate approval of APIs, excipients and packaging materials. Introduced registration on a CDE platform with associated review (关联审评审批) alongside the drug product application.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated: PubMed has no coverage of the associated-review system. The number and date are model recollections. Believed to be refined by NMPA 2019 No. 56; formal supersession status is not established.

sources.code: NMPA Announcement 2019 No. 56 (国家药监局关于进一步完善药品关联审评审批和监管工作有关事宜的公告)
sources.title: Announcement on Further Improving Associated Review, Approval and Supervision of Drugs (APIs, excipients, packaging materials)
sources.scope: Operating rules for the CDE registration platform for chemical APIs, excipients and direct-contact packaging materials, China's DMF-like system. Covers platform registration by the manufacturer, registration numbers, public status flags (recollected as A = associated with an approved product or independently approved, I = not yet approved), letters of authorization to drug product applicants, associated review with the drug product, independent review of chemical APIs, and MAH responsibility for supplier quality.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. Unverified: the number and date (about 2019-07-15/16), the A/I status convention, the Y/F/B registration-number prefixes, and whether a clinical trial application may carry API/excipient/packaging data directly instead of citing a platform registration. The URL is the CDE homepage.

sources.code: CFDA Notice 2018 No. 16 (总局关于发布新药Ⅰ期临床试验申请技术指南的通告)
sources.title: Technical Guide for Phase I Clinical Trial Applications of New Drugs (新药I期临床试验申请技术指南)
sources.scope: Content of a first-in-human (Phase I) clinical trial application, as recollected. The pharmaceutical (药学) section covers, for the drug substance: basic information, manufacturer, manufacturing process, characterization, quality control (specification, methods, batch analyses) and stability. For the drug product: dosage form and composition (including placebo), manufacturer, manufacturing process, quality control and stability. Emphasis is on CMC factors relevant to subject safety.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The guide's existence and content outline are model recollections, and the notice number and date are uncertain. Not established: whether it has been revised or replaced by the CTD-structured requirements of NMPA 2020 No. 44/43.

sources.title: Guidance on Pharmaceutical Research Information for Phase III Clinical Trials of Innovative Drugs (Chemical Drugs) (创新药（化学药）III期临床试验药学研究信息指南)
sources.scope: CMC (药学) information expected when an innovative chemical drug enters pivotal Phase III, as recollected.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The title is recalled from model knowledge; the issuing number, exact date and current status are not established. Do not cite to customers until verified against cde.org.cn.

sources.title: Technical Guideline on Pharmaceutical Changes During Clinical Trials of Innovative Drugs (Chemical Drugs) (Trial) (创新药（化学药）临床试验期间药学变更技术指导原则（试行）)
sources.scope: How sponsors assess CMC changes during clinical development (process, site, scale, formulation, specifications, analytical methods, stability) for impact on subject safety. Separates changes that need a supplementary application from those reported in the DSUR, as recollected.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The title and year are recollections, and the notice number and date are unconfirmed. For cell therapy products, see cn-cde-cell-therapy-change-draft-2025.

sources.title: Administrative Measures for Communication on Drug Development and Technical Review (药物研发与技术审评沟通交流管理办法)
sources.scope: Meeting types (recollected as Type I/II/III) between sponsors and CDE at key milestones: pre-IND, end of Phase II / pre-Phase III, and pre-NDA. CMC questions can be raised at these meetings.
sources.uncertainty: The mechanism is corroborated: communication with CDE at pre-IND, post-Phase II, pre-Phase III and pre-NDA (PMID 42453401), and communication mechanisms written into the DAL/DRR (PMID 36561995). This document's identifier, the 2020 revision date and the meeting-category assignments are NOT corroborated.

sources.code: ChP 2025 (Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China, 2025 edition); promulgation announcement number not confirmed
sources.title: Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China, 2025 Edition (中华人民共和国药典 2025年版)
sources.scope: The current national drug standard, in force as of 2026. Four volumes: I traditional Chinese medicines; II chemical drugs; III biological products; IV general chapters, guidelines and excipient monographs. The 2025 bacterial endotoxin chapter converges further with ICH Q4B while keeping some China-specific requirements. The date field is the effective date (unverified).
sources.uncertainty: Corroborated: ChP 2025 is implemented and in use as the current standard. NIFDC authors call it 'the newly implemented 2025 edition' (PMID 41620123, Jan 2026), and 2025-2026 papers apply ChP 2025 limits (PMIDs 42079722, 42543304). NOT corroborated: the 2025-10-01 effective date, the March 2025 promulgation and the announcement number (possibly 2025 No. 29), the transition rules for approved products and pending applications, and the four-volume structure for 2025. Confidence stays low because the date is unverified.
supersedes: cn-chp-2020

sources.code: ChP 2020 (Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China, 2020 edition)
sources.title: Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China, 2020 Edition (中华人民共和国药典 2020年版)
sources.scope: Previous edition, approved by NMPA and NHC in July 2020 and implemented 2020-12-30 (the date field is the implementation date). It is a statutory technical specification for drug development, production, use and regulation, with 360 general chapters. ICH-aligned general chapters: 9001 stability testing of drug substances and preparations (revised per ICH Q1A); 9101 analytical method validation (per ICH Q2); 9102 impurity analysis (ICH Q3A/Q3B thresholds and decision tree); 0861 residual solvents (per ICH Q3C); 9306 genotoxic impurity control (per ICH M7); 1101 sterility and 0931 dissolution updated per ICH Q4B annexes.
sources.uncertainty: Rests on a single source, PMID 34513116 (PMC8424356), written by staff of the Chinese Pharmacopoeia Commission, the issuing body. It confirms the July 2020 approval, the 2020-12-30 implementation and the chapter content. Supersession by ChP 2025 is supported by PMID 41620123. Chapter numbers are confirmed for the 2020 edition only; check them in ChP 2025.

sources.title: Administrative Measures for Drug Standards (药品标准管理办法)
sources.scope: Management of national drug standards (ChP and NMPA-issued standards) and registered standards (药品注册标准), as recollected. Registered standards should not be lower than the ChP and must be updated when the ChP changes. The date field is the effective date (unverified).
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The title, the announcement number, the issue date (believed mid-2023) and the 2024-01-01 effective date are model recollections.

sources.code: MOH Order No. 79 (卫生部令第79号)
sources.title: Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs (2010 Revision) (药品生产质量管理规范（2010年修订）)
sources.scope: Base GMP for drug manufacturing in China, with NMPA-issued annexes (sterile products, APIs, biologics, blood products, computerized systems, qualification and validation, clinical trial drugs, among others). Effective 2011-03-01 (recollection).
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The order number, promulgation date and 2011-03-01 effective date are recollections. Not established: whether a further GMP revision was finalized by 2026-10.

sources.code: NMPA Announcement 2022 No. 43 (国家药监局关于发布《药品生产质量管理规范—临床试验用药品附录（试行）》的公告)
sources.title: GMP Annex: Drugs for Clinical Trials (Trial) (药品生产质量管理规范—临床试验用药品附录（试行）)
sources.scope: GMP annex for preparing investigational drugs (test drugs, comparators, placebos), as recollected. Covers the quality system, personnel, facilities, documentation (including product files), preparation, blinding and randomization, labelling, quality control, retention samples, release, shipment, recall, return and destruction. Effective 2022-07-01 (recollection).
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated: PubMed had no coverage. The announcement number, date, effective date and clause-level content (including release roles) are recollections.

sources.title: Good Clinical Practice for Drug Clinical Trials (药物临床试验质量管理规范)
sources.scope: GCP, as recollected. Sponsor obligations for investigational products: manufacture under GMP, packaging and labelling (including blinding), storage and transport conditions, release documentation and accountability. Effective 2020-07-01 (recollection).
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated. The announcement number, date and effective date are recollections; clause numbers were not checked. PMID 36561995 mentions only the original 1999 GCP.

sources.code: NMPA announcement on implementing eCTD submission (2021) - number not confirmed
sources.title: Announcement on Implementing Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Submission for Drugs (关于实施药品电子通用技术文档申报的公告), with the NMPA eCTD technical specification and validation criteria
sources.scope: Introduced eCTD submission in China for a defined scope of applications, together with the NMPA eCTD technical specification (CN regional Module 1 backbone) and validation criteria, as recollected.
sources.uncertainty: NOT corroborated: PubMed 'eCTD China' returned only false positives. The number (possibly 2021 No. 119), the dates (start about 2021-12-29), the initial scope (innovative chemical category 1/5.1 and biologics category 1) and any later expansion or mandatory phase-in up to 2026-10 are NOT established. The repo's server/services/ectd/ectd-regional-rules.ts (lines 223-257) cites 'NMPA eCTD技术规范 V1.0 (2019)' and 'NMPA M4 Module 1 (2019 No. 17)'; both are unverified.

sources.title: Measures for the Administration of Post-Approval Changes of Drugs (Trial) (药品上市后变更管理办法（试行）)
sources.scope: Classifies post-approval changes (manufacturing site, process, specifications, packaging and similar) as major (prior-approval supplementary application), moderate (filing) or minor (annual report), and covers MAH change management, as recollected. Supported by CDE technical guidelines on pharmaceutical changes to approved chemical drugs and biologics.
sources.uncertainty: The number and date are not corroborated. PMID 37680352 (CDE and NIFDC co-authors) only partly corroborates the scheme: it describes a 'major post-approval change' to a China-approved biosimilar that needed comparability studies, and states the generic ICH Q5E/Q12 major/moderate/minor categorization. It does not cite this document. Not established: whether the measures have left 'trial' status by 2026-10.

sources.title: Technical Guideline for Stability Studies of Chemical Drugs (APIs and Preparations) (Revised) (化学药物（原料药和制剂）稳定性研究技术指导原则（修订）)
sources.scope: China stability-study guideline aligned with ICH Q1A(R2)/Q1B conditions (long-term, accelerated, stress, photostability), including commitments. Complements ChP general chapter 9001.
sources.uncertainty: This guideline's number and date are NOT corroborated. The companion ChP general chapter 9001 (stability testing of drug substances and preparations, revised per ICH Q1A in ChP 2020) IS corroborated by PMID 34513116. Status relative to NMPA's implementation of ICH Q1A-Q1E and the consolidated ICH Q1 revision is not established.

sources.code: Vaccine Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (2019)
sources.title: Vaccine Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (中华人民共和国疫苗管理法)
sources.scope: Vaccine-specific statute passed by the NPC Standing Committee on 2019-06-29 and in force from 2019-12-01. Eleven chapters and 100 articles covering the whole vaccine life cycle. Introduces a vaccine MAH system and whole-process electronic traceability. Requires lot release (批签发) on a lot-by-lot basis, examining materials and inspecting samples (Art. 29), with inspection items and frequency adjusted by risk assessment. Vaccine MAHs report annually to NMPA on production, circulation, post-marketing research and risk management.
sources.uncertainty: The 2019-06-29 passage date and 2019-12-01 effective date rest on PMID 34373122 alone. PMIDs 37608980 and 35339307 confirm a 2019 enactment. Art. 29 lot-by-lot release is from PMID 36834145, and risk-based adjustment of lot-release testing from PMID 34373122. Presidential Order No. 30 is NOT corroborated.

sources.title: Administrative Measures for Lot Release of Biological Products (生物制品批签发管理办法)
sources.scope: Lot release (批签发) by designated institutions (NIFDC or provincial institutes) of vaccines and other NMPA-designated biologics before marketing or import, as recollected. Effective 2021-03-01 (recollection).
sources.uncertainty: This 2020 SAMR order is NOT corroborated (number, dates and product scope beyond vaccines). PMID 36834145 (2023) confirms the predecessor regime: lot release for biological products since 2004; CFDA 'Measures for the Administration of Lot Release of Biological Products (2017)'; NIFDC sample inspection of every vaccine lot marketed or imported; full-item testing against registration standards for a newly approved product's first three lots. It does not mention a 2020 replacement, so the supersession below is inferred.
supersedes: Measures for the Administration of Lot Release of Biological Products (CFDA, 2017)

sources.code: CDE draft guideline for public comment, July 2025 - identifier not confirmed
sources.title: Draft technical guideline on pharmaceutical (CMC) change research and evaluation for cell therapy products (English description from a secondary source; the official Chinese title is not confirmed)
sources.scope: Draft CDE guidance on CMC changes to cell therapy products. Introduces a three-tier risk classification of manufacturing changes and cites ICH Q5E, the FDA 2023 CGT comparability draft guidance and the EMA ATMP Q&A as benchmarks. The same source reports earlier CDE CMC guidance (2022) for in vivo gene therapy products and for gene-manipulation systems used in ex vivo gene therapy manufacturing.
sources.uncertainty: Rests on one peer-reviewed narrative review (PMID 42776789, PMC13600107, current to June 2026). The official title, document number and exact release date are not confirmed. Not established: whether the draft was finalized by 2026-10-04.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 April 2014 on clinical trials on medicinal products for human use, and repealing Directive 2001/20/EC
sources.scope: EU/EEA clinical trial authorisation. Annex I sets the content of the application dossier: GMP compliance documentation for the IMP, the IMPD (quality, non-clinical, clinical), the simplified IMPD (Annex I Table 1) and labelling (Annex VI). Article 61 covers the manufacturing/import authorisation for IMPs (Article 61(5) lists processes that need no such authorisation, including hospital preparation of diagnostic radiopharmaceutical IMPs). Article 62 sets QP responsibilities and Article 63 GMP for IMPs. It also sets GMP expectations for auxiliary medicinal products. Applicable since 31 January 2022; mandatory for new initial applications since 31 January 2023; the transition from Directive 2001/20/EC ended 30 January 2025.
supersedes: Directive 2001/20/EC (repealed by the CTR; still applied to transitional trials until 30 January 2025)
sources.uncertainty: Verifier (2026-10-05) could not reopen EUR-Lex or legislation.gov.uk: the WebSearch budget was exhausted and the proxy blocks regulator hosts. Peer-reviewed papers by AIFA (Italian Medicines Agency) authors corroborate the key dates (application 31 Jan 2022; CTIS sole route for new trials from 31 Jan 2023; transition 31 Jan 2022 to 30 Jan 2025): PMID 42403710 / PMC13327920 and PMID 40949130 / PMC12425750. PMC12567058 (PMID 41155591) corroborates the Article 61(5)(b) diagnostic radiopharmaceutical exemption. PMC13017528 (PMID 41360073) corroborates the GMP-or-equivalent standard for unauthorised auxiliary medicinal products. Annex I point numbers (32, 38-40) rest only on the researcher's reading of the legislation.gov.uk copy. PMC13327920 reports a European Commission 'Biotech Act' proposal (December 2025) aimed at faster trials. Whether it amends Regulation 536/2014, and its status as of 2026-10-04, were not established.

sources.code: EMA news item and CTIS newsflash of 11 February 2025
sources.title: Clinical trials' transition to new EU system - one year left (EMA news) / CTIS newsflash - 11 February 2025
sources.scope: EMA communications on CTR/CTIS timelines. CTIS has been mandatory for new initial CTAs since 31 January 2023. Trials running beyond 30 January 2025 had to be transitioned to CTIS (transitioning applications submitted between 31 January 2022 and 30 January 2025). After that date only the CTR and its implementing acts apply.
sources.uncertainty: The timeline dates are corroborated independently by two AIFA-authored peer-reviewed papers (PMC13327920; PMC12425750). The verifier could not reopen the EMA pages. The 11 February 2025 newsflash date and the publication date of the 'one year left' news item (believed around January 2024) are unconfirmed. Two claims were removed from the scope as unverifiable: the 5,088 transitioned-trials figure attributed to EMA's 2025 annual report, and the detail on the 'Transitional trial' checkbox.

sources.code: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers (EudraLex Volume 10); version 7.2 reported, current version not confirmed
sources.title: Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Questions & Answers
sources.scope: Living Commission/CTCG Q&A on how the CTR is implemented: the application dossier, Part I/Part II, substantial modifications, transition and CTIS practice.
supersedes: Earlier versions of the CTR Q&A (e.g. versions 6.x)
sources.uncertainty: The version number (7.2), its Q1 2026 endorsement and the revised Q&A items (1.24, 2.12, Chapter III, 3.6) come from one search-result summary in the research pass. The verifier could not re-check them, and no peer-reviewed source mentions them. A later version may exist as of 2026-10-04. No CMC-specific Q&A text was verified. Cite the current version from EudraLex Volume 10.

sources.title: Guideline on the requirements to the chemical and pharmaceutical quality documentation concerning investigational medicinal products in clinical trials - Revision 2
sources.scope: Quality documentation in the IMPD for chemically defined drug substances, synthetic peptides, herbal substances and preparations, and chemically defined radioactive/radiolabelled substances (radiopharmaceuticals), submitted to competent authorities before a clinical trial in humans. Revised to implement Regulation (EU) No 536/2014. Legal effective date 31 January 2022.
supersedes: CHMP/QWP/185401/2004 final (original guideline)
Revision 1 of this guideline (reference number not confirmed)
sources.uncertainty: The verifier could not reopen EMA pages. The researcher's search confirmed the 31/01/2022 effective date; the verifier did not re-confirm it. Peer-reviewed IMPD papers (PMC9268543; PMC12567058) corroborate that the EMA chemical/pharmaceutical IMP quality guideline covers radiopharmaceuticals and that the IMPD has drug-substance and IMP parts. They cite the guideline without its code. The CHMP adoption date and the Rev. 1 reference are unconfirmed. Section-level phase-scaling content used in 'low' requirements is unverified against the PDF.

sources.title: Guideline on the requirements for quality documentation concerning biological investigational medicinal products in clinical trials - Revision 2
sources.scope: Documentation requirements on the biological, chemical and pharmaceutical quality of IMPs containing biological/biotechnology-derived substances, where no simplified IMPD is submitted. Prepared by the BWP under a Commission mandate to implement Regulation (EU) No 536/2014. Reported as adopted by CHMP on 27 January 2022 and effective 31 January 2022.
supersedes: EMA/CHMP/BWP/534898/2008 Rev. 1
EMA/CHMP/BWP/534898/2008 (first version)
sources.uncertainty: The identifier 'EMA/CHMP/BWP/534898/2008 Revision 2' is independently confirmed: J Infect Dis 2026 (PMID 41360073, PMC13017528) used it to build a product dossier. The verifier did not re-confirm the adoption and effective dates (researcher's search only). The dates of Rev. 1 and the first version are unconfirmed. Section-level content in 'low' requirements is unverified.

sources.title: Guideline on quality, non-clinical and clinical requirements for investigational advanced therapy medicinal products in clinical trials
sources.scope: Multidisciplinary guideline on the structure and data requirements of CTAs for exploratory and confirmatory trials with investigational ATMPs (gene therapy, somatic cell therapy, tissue-engineered and combined ATMPs). Covers development, manufacturing and quality control plus non-clinical and clinical aspects. Takes a risk-based approach with risk-appropriate flexibility in CTA data requirements. Reported as adopted by CAT on 6 December 2024 and by CHMP on 20 January 2025, in effect since 1 July 2025.
supersedes: Draft versions released for public consultation (first draft 2018-2019; a second version for a second public consultation)
Guideline on the minimum quality and non-clinical data for certification of ATMPs (not relevant to CTAs; listed only to separate the two)
sources.uncertainty: Code, title and risk-based CTA data approach are independently confirmed by Front Med 2026 (PMID 42311903, PMC13270379). The verifier did not re-confirm the CAT/CHMP adoption dates or the 1 July 2025 effective date (researcher's four secondary sources only). The 2019 date in the task brief belongs to the draft. The second 'supersedes' entry is not a supersession and is kept only as a disambiguation note.

sources.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 of 23 May 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council by specifying principles of and guidelines for good manufacturing practice for investigational medicinal products for human use and arrangements for inspections
sources.scope: Legally binding GMP principles for IMPs and arrangements for inspections under Article 63 of the CTR. Aims at consistency between batches of the same IMP used in the same or different trials, and at documenting and justifying changes during development. Aligned as far as possible with GMP for authorised products, with added attention to cross-contamination, randomisation and blinding.
sources.uncertainty: The verifier found no peer-reviewed article citing the Delegated Regulation by number and could not reopen EUR-Lex. Identity and date rest on the researcher's search results. That it applies from the CTR application date (31 January 2022) is model knowledge. Article-level content beyond the recitals was not verified.

sources.title: Detailed Commission guidelines on good manufacturing practice for investigational medicinal products for human use, pursuant to the second subparagraph of Article 63(1) of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014
sources.scope: Detailed GMP for IMP manufacture, import, QP certification, labelling, blinding and comparators. Applies from the date of application of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 (31 January 2022). Replaced the earlier Annex 13 for CTR trials. Investigational ATMPs follow EudraLex Volume 4 Part IV instead.
supersedes: eu-eudralex-v4-annex13-2010
sources.uncertainty: The C(2017) 8179 number and the 8.12.2017 date come from the researcher's reading of the official download title. The verifier could not re-open it, and no peer-reviewed source citing it was retrieved. Section-level content (product specification file, certification steps) is unverified.

sources.title: EudraLex Volume 4 - Annex 13: Manufacture of Investigational Medicinal Products (Directive 2001/20/EC era)
sources.scope: GMP annex for IMPs under Directive 2001/20/EC and Directive 2003/94/EC. It stayed applicable to trials authorised under the Directive during the CTR transition. Since the transition ended (30 January 2025) it has no remaining application to EU/EEA trials.
sources.uncertainty: Downgraded from medium. The February 2010 date (in operation 31 July 2010) and the ENTR reference are model knowledge, confirmed by neither the researcher nor the verifier. The 'no remaining application' status is inferred from the end of the CTR transition; no formal notice was seen. The UK applies its own retained version, which is outside EU scope.

sources.code: EudraLex Volume 10 template (no separate reference number confirmed)
sources.title: Template for the qualified person's declaration of equivalence to EU GMP for investigational medicinal products manufactured in third countries
sources.scope: Certification by an EU/EEA QP that an IMP made outside the EU/EEA was manufactured under GMP at least equivalent to EU GMP, as the CTR requires. Part A gives the manufacturing sites and activities. Part B gives the basis of the declaration (preferably an audit, with auditing party and date) and the declaration itself. The template identifies the EU CT number, the IMP name(s) and the MIA number of the importing site.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified by the verifier: no peer-reviewed source was found and regulator sites were blocked. The template structure rests on the researcher's secondary sources (ECA, SUKL, CCMO) and the official download URL. Publication/version date not established. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: Commission guideline on sponsor responsibilities for handling and shipping of IMPs (reference number not confirmed)
sources.title: Guideline on the responsibilities of the sponsor with regard to handling and shipping of investigational medicinal products for human use in accordance with Good Clinical Practice and Good Manufacturing Practice
sources.scope: Sponsor responsibilities for handling and shipping IMPs under the CTR, including release of QP-certified IMP to trial sites.
sources.uncertainty: The researcher's search results confirm existence and URL. The date is inferred from the URL path (2022-12). The C-number is unconfirmed. The two-step release content is model knowledge. The verifier found no corroboration.

sources.title: EU Guidelines for Good Manufacturing Practice for Medicinal Products for Human and Veterinary Use - Annex 16: Certification by a Qualified Person and Batch Release
sources.scope: QP certification and batch release of medicinal products in the EU/EEA, including imported batches. QP certification of IMPs follows the CTR and the detailed GMP-IMP guideline.
sources.uncertainty: The October 2015 date is inferred from the official file name. The 15 April 2016 effective date is model knowledge. Whether Annex 16 was revised by 2026-10 was not checked. The verifier found no peer-reviewed source citing Annex 16.

sources.title: EudraLex - Volume 4 - Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) guidelines (Parts I-IV and Annexes)
sources.scope: The EU GMP Guide: Part I (medicinal products), Part II (active substances), Part III (GMP-related documents), Part IV (GMP specific to ATMPs, risk-based) and the Annexes (including Annex 1 sterile, the Annex 13 heading for the IMP guideline, and Annex 16 QP certification). EMA has published a concept paper (EMA/INS/GMP/48771/2025) on revising the ATMP GMP guidelines (Part IV).
sources.uncertainty: A living collection; individual part and annex versions were not verified. Front Med 2026 (PMC13270379) confirms that the ATMP-specific GMP guideline (Part IV) is risk-based and that a revision concept paper exists. Methods Mol Biol 2021 (DOI 10.1007/7651_2020_286) confirms that Part IV is titled 'Guidelines on Good Manufacturing Practice specific to Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products'. Part IV's C-number (believed C(2017) 7694 of 22 November 2017, applicable 22 May 2018) is unconfirmed. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: Directive 2001/83/EC, Annex I (as replaced by Commission Directive 2003/63/EC and amended by Directive 2009/120/EC)
sources.title: Directive 2001/83/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 November 2001 on the Community code relating to medicinal products for human use - Annex I: Analytical, pharmacotoxicological and clinical standards and protocols in respect of the testing of medicinal products
sources.scope: Legal basis for MAA content (Article 8(3) full application; other legal bases such as Article 10a well-established use) and for the CTD-format dossier in Annex I. Annex I Part I Module 3 covers chemical, pharmaceutical and biological information; Part IV covers ATMPs. Also contains the MIA/QP provisions (Articles 40-52) that CTR Article 61 cross-references. Applies to national, MRP/DCP and (with Regulation 726/2004) centralised MAAs.
sources.uncertainty: Upgraded from low. J Clin Med 2025 (PMID 41226917, PMC12609620), by Paul-Ehrlich-Institut authors, confirms that the Directive defines MA data requirements in Annex I and the Article 8(3) and Article 10a legal bases. The amending-directive history (2003/63/EC, 2009/120/EC) and the EUR-Lex ELI URL were not verified. To be replaced by the pharmaceutical reform once adopted and applicable (see eu-pharma-reform-2023).

sources.title: Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 laying down Union procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use and establishing a European Medicines Agency
sources.scope: Centralised procedure (CHMP opinion, Commission decision). Mandatory for biotechnology products, ATMPs, oncology medicines and certain other categories. Dossier content follows Directive 2001/83/EC Annex I.
sources.uncertainty: Onkologie 2013 (PMID 23549032) corroborates its role as the legal basis of the centralised procedure, e.g. for oncology medicines. The 31 March 2004 date, the full list of mandatory-scope categories and the URL were not verified. Proposed for replacement by the pharmaceutical reform Regulation (procedure 2023/0131(COD)).

sources.code: EudraLex Volume 2B - Notice to Applicants (CTD presentation and content of the dossier)
sources.title: Notice to Applicants, Volume 2B: Presentation and format of the dossier - Common Technical Document (CTD), including EU Module 1 and EU-specific Module 3 regional information
sources.scope: EU presentation of the CTD. EU 3.2.R regional information includes the drug product process validation scheme, medical device information, certificate(s) of suitability, and information on materials of animal/human origin (TSE).
sources.uncertainty: Not verified by the researcher or the verifier. The URL follows the confirmed pattern of the EudraLex Volume 4/10 pages. The current NtA 2B version date and the exact 3.2.R headings are model knowledge. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: Certification of Suitability to the Monographs of the European Pharmacopoeia (CEP) procedure
sources.title: Certification of Suitability to the Monographs of the European Pharmacopoeia (CEP)
sources.scope: An EDQM CEP confirms that the quality of an active substance (or of a material, for TSE risk) is suitably controlled by the Ph. Eur. monograph. In EU MAAs a CEP can replace the corresponding Module 3.2.S data.
sources.uncertainty: EDQM is outside the EU institutional scope, but CEPs are used in EU dossiers. The governing resolution, current version and URL were not verified. Ther Innov Regul Sci 2025 (PMID 40389795) confirms that switching an approved manufacturer from an ASMF to a CEP across 38 EEA MAs took four variations, with one authority requesting a fifth. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: Guideline on Active Substance Master File Procedure
sources.scope: ASMF procedure: the active substance manufacturer submits an Applicant's Part (shared with the applicant/MAH) and a Restricted Part (confidential, sent directly to the authorities) in place of full 3.2.S data, with a letter of access.
sources.uncertainty: The reference-number revision, date and URL were not verified. Procedure details are model knowledge. PMID 40389795 confirms only that the ASMF route is used in EEA MAs. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: Guideline on process validation for finished products - information and data to be provided in regulatory submissions
sources.scope: Process validation data for finished products in MAAs and variations: traditional, continuous or hybrid verification. For standard processes, a process validation scheme (EU 3.2.R), completed before commercial release, may stand in for validation data at submission.
sources.uncertainty: PMC12609620 (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut authors) confirms that an EMA 'Guideline on process validation for finished products' exists and that a matrix approach is a justified deviation from it. The reference number, revision, date and URL are model knowledge and were not verified.

sources.code: EMA QP declaration template (reference number not confirmed)
sources.title: Template for the qualified person's (QP) declaration concerning good manufacturing practice compliance of active substance manufacture - 'The QP declaration template'
sources.scope: Template for the QP declaration that active substance manufacture complies with EU GMP. Submitted with MAAs and with variations that introduce active substance manufacturers.
sources.uncertainty: The researcher's search confirmed the page URL and title; the verifier did not re-check them. The reference number, current version and legal basis (Directive 2001/83/EC Articles 8(3)(ha) and 46(f)) are model knowledge. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices - Article 117 (amendment to Annex I of Directive 2001/83/EC)
sources.scope: For integral drug-device combinations (iDDCs), the medicinal product framework governs the product, but the device part must meet the relevant MDR Annex I general safety and performance requirements (GSPRs). Article 117 made notified bodies responsible for assessing the integral device's GSPR compliance; the MAA includes the corresponding conformity evidence (EU declaration of conformity, notified body certificate or notified body opinion). The MDR has applied since 26 May 2021.
sources.uncertainty: Upgraded from low. Ther Innov Regul Sci 2026 (PMID 42542469), by EMA authors, confirms the Article 117 notified-body role, the GSPR standard and the 26 May 2021 date of effect. The 5 April 2017 adoption date and the 'amends Annex I of Directive 2001/83/EC' framing are model knowledge, not re-confirmed. EMA's Article 117 Q&A was not retrieved.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008 of 24 November 2008 concerning the examination of variations to the terms of marketing authorisations for medicinal products for human use and veterinary medicinal products
sources.scope: The EU Variations Regulation. Classifies post-approval changes as Type IA/IAIN, Type IB, Type II or extension (Type II: a change that may have a significant impact on quality, safety or efficacy) and sets the procedures, grouping and worksharing. Amended by Regulation (EU) No 712/2012 and by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701.
sources.uncertainty: Upgraded from low. Its role and variation categories are corroborated by PMC12609620 (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut authors, 2025), Pharmaceut Med 2020 (PMID 32048215: four categories and the Type II definition) and Ther Innov Regul Sci 2025 (PMID 40389795: the same change approved as IA, IB or II in different EEA countries). The 24 November 2008 date (in the title) and the 712/2012 amendment were not separately re-confirmed. Verify the consolidated text on EUR-Lex.

sources.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701 amending Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008 as regards the examination of variations to the terms of marketing authorisations for medicinal products for human use
sources.scope: 2024 revision of the Variations Regulation: modernises the classification and procedures and supports lifecycle management tools.
sources.uncertainty: Not verified by the researcher (budget exhausted) or the verifier (no search; no peer-reviewed source retrieved). Model knowledge only: adoption 11 March 2024, OJ publication June 2024, application from 1 January 2025. Confirm against the OJ before citing any date.

sources.code: Commission Guidelines on the details of the various categories of variations (revision following Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701; OJ C reference not confirmed)
sources.title: Guidelines on the details of the various categories of variations, on the operation of the procedures laid down in Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008, and on the documentation to be submitted (revised following Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701)
sources.scope: Variations classification guideline implementing Delegated Regulation 2024/1701. Gives classification codes, the conditions and documentation for each change category, and procedural details.
supersedes: Guidelines on the details of the various categories of variations, 2013/C 223/01 (OJ C 223, 2.8.2013)
sources.uncertainty: Not verified by the researcher or the verifier. Model knowledge only: publication in 2025 and application from 15 January 2026. The OJ C reference is unconfirmed. The URL is the EudraLex Volume 2 landing page, not the document.

sources.title: Questions and answers for marketing authorisation holders/applicants on the CHMP Opinion for the Article 5(3) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 referral on nitrosamine impurities in human medicinal products
sources.scope: Nitrosamine risk evaluation, confirmatory testing and risk mitigation for MAHs/applicants, and acceptable intake (AI) limits, including an appendix of established limits. Revision 16 (2023) introduced the Carcinogenic Potency Categorization Approach (CPCA) for nitrosamine drug-substance-related impurities (NDSRIs), assigning 1 of 5 potency categories with AIs of 18 ng/day (category 1), 100 ng/day (2), 400 ng/day (3) and 1500 ng/day (4 and 5).
sources.uncertainty: Peer-reviewed papers corroborate the content: J Pharm Sci 2023 (PMID 37805074) on CPCA in revision 16 with 18/100/1500 ng/day; Regul Toxicol Pharmacol 2024 (PMID 38754805, EMA/BfArM/FDA co-authors) on 5 categories and international adoption; Biomed Chromatogr 2026 (PMID 41795220) on category 3 = 400 ng/day; Front Pharmacol 2024 (PMC11288830) on authorities requiring MAHs to assess all chemically manufactured DS/DP. The verifier did not confirm the reference number, the PDF URL (recalled) or the current revision as of 2026-10. Step deadlines are unverified and removed from requirements. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: COM(2023) 192 final (Directive, procedure 2023/0132(COD)); COM(2023) 193 final (Regulation, procedure 2023/0131(COD))
sources.title: Proposals for a Directive on the Union code relating to medicinal products for human use and a Regulation laying down Union procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human use and governing the rules for the European Medicines Agency (EU pharmaceutical legislation reform)
sources.scope: Reform package to repeal and replace Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation (EC) No 726/2004. Includes a platform technology approach, a regulatory sandbox, and a restructuring of EMA committees (e.g. CAT's remit integrated into other bodies).
sources.uncertainty: Corroborated: the Commission proposal (April 2023) and the European Parliament's position (April 2024), with the process not completed as of mid-2025 (Health Policy 2025, PMID 40829473); procedure numbers 2023/0131 and 2023/0132 (Cytotherapy 2025, PMID 41217312). A Drug Discovery Today article (PMID 42462853, July 2026) still calls the revised legislation 'upcoming'. Not established: whether it was adopted or published in the OJ by 2026-10-04, its application dates, and any provisional political agreement. The landing-page URL is recalled, not verified.

sources.code: EudraLex Volume 4, Annex 1: Manufacture of Sterile Medicinal Products (2022 revision)
sources.title: EU Guidelines to Good Manufacturing Practice - Annex 1: Manufacture of Sterile Medicinal Products (revised 2022)
sources.scope: GMP for sterile medicinal products: a lifecycle contamination control strategy (CCS) under ICH Q9 quality risk management, aseptic processing, environmental monitoring and sterilisation. Section 8.87 expects pre-use post-sterilisation integrity testing (PUPSIT) of sterilised filter assemblies, with a documented risk-based justification where it is not feasible. PIC/S has adopted the revision.
supersedes: Previous EU GMP Annex 1 (2008 revision; date not verified)
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. Three peer-reviewed papers corroborate the 2022 revision year, the CCS framework and the section 8.87 PUPSIT text: Appl Microbiol Biotechnol 2026 (PMC13134992); PDA J Pharm Sci Technol 2026 (PMID 42731872, PMID 42225407). Not verified: the exact publication date and C-number (believed 25 August 2022), the application date (believed 25 August 2023, with a later date for one lyophiliser provision) and the URL (EudraLex Volume 4 landing page). The extent to which Annex 1 applies to sterile IMPs, via the GMP-IMP guideline, was not verified.

sources.title: Concept paper on the revision of the guidelines on good manufacturing practice specific to advanced therapy medicinal products (EudraLex Volume 4 Part IV)
sources.scope: Concept paper launching a revision of the ATMP-specific GMP guidelines. It aims to reduce inconsistencies, to apply quality risk management more systematically and to accommodate innovative manufacturing approaches.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. Its only source is Front Med 2026 (PMID 42311903, PMC13270379), which cites the identifier and summarises its aims. The exact title is paraphrased from that article. No official URL, publication date or consultation status was confirmed. Whether a revised Part IV was adopted by 2026-10-04 is unknown.

sources.title: IND content and format
sources.scope: Required content of an IND for human drugs and biologics. Paragraph (a)(7) sets the phase-graded CMC section (drug substance, drug product, placebo, labeling, environmental analysis).
sources.uncertainty: Regulatory text was confirmed from eCFR, Cornell LII and govinfo snippets. The FR citation for the 1987 rewrite and the dates of later amendments were not verified, so cite the current eCFR text. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Labeling of an investigational new drug
sources.scope: Sets the caution statement for the immediate package and bans false or misleading statements and claims of safety or effectiveness on investigational drug labels.
sources.uncertainty: Amendment history was not verified. It includes a Strategic National Stockpile exception in 312.6(c). Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Information amendments
sources.scope: Information amendments to an active IND, including new chemistry, manufacturing and control information.
sources.uncertainty: None material to content. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Annual reports
sources.scope: IND annual progress report, which includes a summary of significant manufacturing or microbiological changes.
sources.uncertainty: None material to content. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Applicability of current good manufacturing practice regulations - exemption of most Phase 1 investigational drugs from 21 CFR Part 211 (final rule: Current Good Manufacturing Practice and Investigational New Drugs Intended for Use in Clinical Trials)
sources.scope: Exempts most Phase 1 investigational drugs, including biological drugs, from Part 211. Statutory CGMP under FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B) still applies. The exemption does not cover a drug already made available for Phase 2/3 or lawfully marketed.
supersedes: Direct final rule of 2006-01-17 (FR Doc 06-353) proposing the same exemption
sources.uncertainty: Search results did not detail how the 2006 direct final rule was handled before the 2008 final rule. Cite the 2008 final rule and the current eCFR. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Human drugs and biologics - categorical exclusions (National Environmental Policy Act)
sources.scope: Categorical exclusions from environmental assessment, including action on an IND (25.31(e)), unless extraordinary circumstances apply.
sources.uncertainty: The 25.31(e) IND exclusion was confirmed through secondary and FDA guidance snippets, not the eCFR page itself. Amendment dates were not verified. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Content and format of an NDA
sources.scope: Required NDA content. (d)(1) is the CMC section for drug substance and drug product. (e) covers samples, which FDA may request so agency laboratories can validate the applicant's analytical procedures.
sources.uncertainty: Exact subparagraph numbering below (d)(1)(i)/(ii) was not verified. In particular, the paragraph holding the environmental assessment and categorical exclusion claim was not confirmed. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Drug master files
sources.scope: An IND, NDA, ANDA, amendment or supplement may incorporate a DMF by reference when the holder authorizes it in writing. The DMF must list every person authorized to reference it.
sources.uncertainty: None material to content. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Applications for biologics licenses; procedures for filing
sources.scope: BLA content under PHS Act section 351, including a full description of manufacturing methods, stability data through the dating period, samples, lot test summaries, labels and the address of each manufacturing location. Applicable GMP: parts 210, 211, 600, 606 and 820.
sources.uncertainty: None material to content. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Biologics License Applications and Master Files
sources.scope: A BLA may not incorporate drug substance, drug substance intermediate or drug product information by reference to a master file; other information may be referenced. INDs for PHS Act products may incorporate any master file information. Transition (deemed-BLA) products keep references existing at approval. The rule also covers combination-product constituent parts.
supersedes: Proposed rule 'Biologics License Applications and Master Files' (FR Doc 2019-13753, 2019-06-28)
sources.uncertainty: None material to content. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Supplements and other changes to an approved NDA
sources.scope: Reporting categories for post-approval CMC changes. 314.70(e) covers protocols (comparability protocols) that set the tests, studies and acceptance criteria showing no adverse effect of a specified change.
sources.uncertainty: None material to content. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Changes to an approved application (biologics)
sources.scope: Reporting of manufacturing changes to approved BLAs, including comparability protocols under 601.12(e).
sources.uncertainty: The exact 601.12(e) wording was not retrieved. Search results paraphrased it as parallel to 314.70(e). Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Content and Format of Investigational New Drug Applications (INDs) for Phase 1 Studies of Drugs, Including Well-Characterized, Therapeutic, Biotechnology-derived Products
sources.scope: Content and format of Phase 1 INDs, including a phase-appropriate CMC section: risk signals, link between clinical and toxicology material, and limited stability, validation and specification expectations.
sources.uncertainty: A companion Questions and Answers document (media/72284) is listed as issued October 2000. Its content was not reviewed. FDA's 2026 FIH Phase 1 clarifications supplement this guidance but do not formally supersede it. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, May 2003 (FR Doc 03-12545, 2003-05-20)
sources.title: INDs for Phase 2 and Phase 3 Studies: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Information
sources.scope: CMC information for Phase 2 and 3 INDs, split into CMC safety information (information amendments) and corroborating information (annual reports). It does not apply to botanicals, protein drugs from natural sources or biotechnology, or other biologics.
supersedes: Draft guidance of February 1999 (same topic)
sources.uncertainty: The February 1999 draft is named only in secondary results. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, July 2008 (FR Doc E8-16002; Docket FDA-2005-D-0157)
sources.title: Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Phase 1 Investigational Drugs
sources.scope: How to apply statutory CGMP (FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B)) to manufacture of most Phase 1 investigational drugs, including biological drugs, that are exempt from Part 211. It does not apply to HCT/Ps regulated solely under PHS Act section 361.
supersedes: Draft guidance 'INDs - Approaches to Complying with CGMP During Phase 1' (January 2006)
sources.uncertainty: None material. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, investigators, and reviewers, January 2006 (FR Doc 06-354)
sources.title: Exploratory IND Studies
sources.scope: Preclinical, clinical and CMC approaches for exploratory studies early in Phase 1 with very limited human exposure and no therapeutic or diagnostic intent (for example microdose studies).
sources.uncertainty: The detailed CMC recommendations in the guidance body were not retrieved. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA clarification document posted via the Phase 1 IND Navigator (fda.gov/media/193163)
sources.title: Regulatory Flexibilities and Clarifications: Chemistry, Manufacturing and Control (CMC) Information for Original First in Human (FIH) Phase 1 INDs - CDER-Regulated Small Molecule Drug Products
sources.scope: Sets the minimum CMC information for original FIH Phase 1 INDs (CDER small molecules) and what can be deferred, such as clinical-lot stability, full-duration stability, method validation and non-safety process controls. FDA estimates IND preparation time can drop by up to 12 months.
sources.uncertainty: The posting date was not confirmed. The document ties to HHS Operation TrialBlazer, announced 2026-06-22. The title string and the mapping of media/193163 (small molecule) versus media/193164 (recombinant) come from search snippets; a third PDF, media/192065, also exists. It does not appear to be a numbered Good Guidance Practice guidance, so treat it as FDA clarification of 21 CFR 312.23 expectations. Content was verified from snippets only, not the PDF. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA clarification document posted via the Phase 1 IND Navigator (fda.gov/media/193164)
sources.title: Regulatory Flexibilities and Clarifications: Chemistry, Manufacturing and Control (CMC) Information for Original First in Human (FIH) Phase 1 INDs - CDER-Regulated Recombinant Biological Products
sources.scope: Sets the minimum CMC information for original FIH Phase 1 INDs (CDER recombinant biologics), covering characterization depth, viral clearance, potency assay and process controls, and what can be deferred.
sources.uncertainty: Same date and title caveats as the small-molecule document. The viral clearance item ('product-specific viral clearance study ... not needed at FIH Phase 1') comes from a snippet with ambiguous wording about an accompanying risk assessment. Verify the exact text in the PDF before quoting. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, January 2020 (FR Doc 2020-01701, 2020-01-30)
sources.title: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Control (CMC) Information for Human Gene Therapy Investigational New Drug Applications (INDs)
sources.scope: CMC information for human gene therapy INDs, organized by CTD Module 3, to assure safety, identity, quality, purity and strength (including potency).
supersedes: Guidance for FDA Reviewers and Sponsors: Content and Review of CMC Information for Human Gene Therapy INDs (April 2008)
sources.uncertainty: None material. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: Guidance for FDA reviewers and sponsors, April 2008 (FR Doc E8-7588, 2008-04-10)
sources.title: Content and Review of Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Control (CMC) Information for Human Somatic Cell Therapy Investigational New Drug Applications (INDs)
sources.scope: CMC information to include in an original IND for human somatic cell therapy, plus reviewer instructions.
supersedes: Draft 'Guidance for Reviewers: Instructions and Template for CMC Reviewers of Human Somatic Cell Therapy INDs' (August 2003)
sources.uncertainty: I could not confirm that this guidance is still current as of 2026-10 beyond its listing on the FDA site. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry (Level 2, issued directly as final), May 2026 (fda.gov/media/192321)
sources.title: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Flexibilities for Developing Human Cellular and Gene Therapy Products for a Biologics License Application
sources.scope: Risk-based CMC flexibilities for cell and gene therapy products, in four groups: clinical development (phase-appropriate CGMP, permissive early release criteria, risk-based comparability), process validation (PPQ batch number scientifically justified), commercial specifications, and other areas (stability, alternative analytics). Full statutory and regulatory compliance is still required.
sources.uncertainty: Two secondary sources confirm the issue date. Content details come from secondary summaries, not the guidance text. FDA had announced a 'flexible approach' webpage on 2026-01-11, before the guidance. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, January 2011 (FR Doc 2011-3462, 2011-02-16)
sources.title: Potency Tests for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products
sources.scope: Developing potency tests to support cell and gene therapy INDs and BLAs.
sources.supersededBy: Intended to be replaced by 'Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products' once that guidance is final (draft December 2023)
sources.uncertainty: If the Potency Assurance guidance was finalized in 2026 (it is on CBER's 2026 agenda), this guidance may already be superseded. Finalization was not confirmed. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA draft guidance for industry, December 2023 (FR Doc 2023-28596, 2023-12-28)
sources.title: Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products
sources.scope: Science- and risk-based potency assurance strategy for cell and gene therapy products, covering process design, process control, material control, in-process testing and potency lot-release assays.
sources.uncertainty: Status as of 2026-10-04 is unclear. The draft is listed for finalization on CBER's 2026 guidance agenda, but a final version was not confirmed. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA draft guidance for industry, July 2023 (FR Doc 2023-14917, 2023-07-14)
sources.title: Manufacturing Changes and Comparability for Human Cellular and Gene Therapy Products
sources.scope: Lifecycle management and reporting of manufacturing changes for cell and gene therapy products, and design of comparability studies.
sources.uncertainty: Still a draft based on available results. The May 2026 CGT flexibilities guidance covers overlapping ground on comparability during development. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, June 2016 revision (FR Doc 2016-15664, 2016-07-01); original February 2012 (FR Doc 2012-3957)
sources.title: Early Clinical Trials With Live Biotherapeutic Products: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Control Information
sources.scope: CMC information for IND submissions for early clinical trials with live biotherapeutic products. The 2016 update covers when a commercially available product's label may satisfy CMC requirements.
supersedes: February 2012 version of the same guidance (draft October 2010)
sources.uncertainty: The June 2016 document month comes from secondary summaries; the FR notice is dated 2016-07-01. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, Revision 8 (original final guidance May 2015, FR Doc 2015-10539); implements FD&C Act section 745A(a)
sources.title: Providing Regulatory Submissions in Electronic Format - Certain Human Pharmaceutical Product Applications and Related Submissions Using the eCTD Specifications
sources.scope: Mandatory eCTD format for NDAs, ANDAs, certain BLAs, commercial INDs and master files, with exemptions (noncommercial INDs, section 561 expanded access) and waivers. Revision 8 adds eCTD v4.0 language and short-term waiver criteria (section III.E).
supersedes: Revision 7 of the same guidance
sources.uncertainty: Revision number and month (September 2024) come from search summaries. Results disagree on the Revision 7 date (2019 vs February 2020). No later revision was found, but one issued after 2024 cannot be ruled out. The eCTD requirement dates (NDA/ANDA/BLA 2017-05-05; commercial INDs and master files 2018-05-05) are well corroborated. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA draft guidance for industry, October 2019 (FR Doc 2019-22821, 2019-10-21)
sources.title: Drug Master Files
sources.scope: Preparing and submitting DMFs (Types II, III, IV, V), letters of authorization, and holder obligations.
sources.uncertainty: No final version was found as of 2026-10 searches. When final it is expected to replace the September 1989 'Guideline for Drug Master Files', which FDA still posts. LOA content items come from FDA guideline snippets. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: ICH M4Q (R1); FDA guidance 'M4Q: The CTD - Quality', August 2001
