sources.supersededBy: ICH M4Q(R2) once final (FDA draft January 2026)
sources.uncertainty: The FDA document is dated August 2001; ICH's R1 renumbering came later. The exact FDA revision label was not verified. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: M4: The CTD - Quality Questions and Answers/Location Issues
sources.scope: Which CTD-Quality section each type of information belongs in, and how linked sections relate.
sources.uncertainty: Specific location answers were not retrieved. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: ICH M4Q(R2) Step 2; FDA draft guidance, January 2026 (FR Doc 2026-01073, 2026-01-21; Docket FDA-2025-D-2275)
sources.title: M4Q(R2) The Common Technical Document for the Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use: Quality
sources.scope: Proposed restructure of Module 2.3 and Module 3 to improve registration and lifecycle efficiency, support digitalization and knowledge management, and accommodate emerging technologies. ICH Step 2 was endorsed May 2025.
sources.uncertainty: The FDA comment period closed around 2026-03-23 (secondary source). The ICH Step 4 date and FDA implementation timing were not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA eCTD 'The Comprehensive Table of Contents Headings and Hierarchy' (version 2.3.3 at fda.gov/media/76444)
sources.title: The Comprehensive Table of Contents Headings and Hierarchy
sources.scope: FDA heading hierarchy for eCTD submissions, including US 3.2.R regional subheadings (executed batch records, comparability protocols, methods validation package).
sources.uncertainty: The 3.2.R subsection numbers and contents were corroborated through FDA's 'ANDA Submissions - Content and Format' guidance (snippets). Version and date of the TOC document were not verified. For NDAs/BLAs, confirm with the current FDA eCTD specifications or v4.0 controlled vocabularies. Adoption date not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, July 2015 (FR Doc 2015-18270, 2015-07-27)
sources.title: Analytical Procedures and Methods Validation for Drugs and Biologics
sources.scope: Submitting analytical procedures and methods validation data to document identity, strength, quality, purity and potency in NDAs, ANDAs, BLAs and supplements.
supersedes: Draft guidance of 2014-02-19 (same title)
2000 draft 'Analytical Procedures and Methods Validation'
1987 'Guideline for Submitting Samples and Analytical Data for Methods Validation'
sources.uncertainty: The docket number was inconsistent across results and is omitted. How this guidance interacts with the March 2024 Q2(R2)/Q14 guidances was not established. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, October 2022 (FR Doc 2022-22334, 2022-10-14)
sources.title: Comparability Protocols for Postapproval Changes to the Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Information in an NDA, ANDA, or BLA
sources.scope: Using comparability protocols in an original application or a prior approval supplement to plan and implement post-approval CMC changes, often at a reduced reporting category.
supersedes: Draft 'Comparability Protocols for Human Drugs and Biologics: CMC Information' (2016-04-20)
Draft 'Comparability Protocols - Protein Drug Products and Biological Products - CMC Information' (September 2003; withdrawn 2015-05-06)
sources.uncertainty: Placement of the protocol in 3.2.R is stated in the 2016 draft (snippet). Its carry-over into the 2022 final was not confirmed verbatim. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, January 2011, Revision 1 (FR Doc 2011-1437, 2011-01-25)
sources.title: Process Validation: General Principles and Practices
sources.scope: Lifecycle process validation for human and animal drugs and biologics, including APIs: Stage 1 process design, Stage 2 process qualification/PPQ, Stage 3 continued process verification.
supersedes: Guideline on General Principles of Process Validation (May 1987)
sources.uncertainty: None material. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, September 2024, Revision 2
sources.title: Control of Nitrosamine Impurities in Human Drugs
sources.scope: Three-step mitigation (risk assessment, confirmatory testing, reporting changes) for small-molecule nitrosamines and NDSRIs in APIs and drug products: marketed, under approved or pending applications, and in development. Revision 2 adds an NDSRI section on root causes and mitigation.
supersedes: Earlier versions of the same guidance (original September 2020; Revision 1)
sources.uncertainty: The Revision 1 date (believed February 2021) was not verified. Applicability to products under IND is stated as advice to assess risk early so it is resolved before the NDA. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA guidance for industry, August 2023 (FR Doc 2023-16814, 2023-08-07) plus 'CDER Nitrosamine Impurity Acceptable Intake Limits' webpage (updated 2025-06-23)
sources.title: Recommended Acceptable Intake Limits for Nitrosamine Drug Substance-Related Impurities
sources.scope: Predicted carcinogenic potency categorization approach for NDSRI acceptable intake (AI) limits. FDA's AI webpage lists recommended and interim limits. A June 2025 update allows progress reports when NDSRI mitigation for approved or marketed products is incomplete by 2025-08-01.
sources.uncertainty: It is not established whether the June 2025 change revised the guidance PDF or only the webpage (sources differ). The AI tables change over time, so cite the live webpage with an access date. Not independently re-verified.

sources.scope: Control of elemental impurities in human drug products marketed in the US, consistent with ICH Q3D implementation.
supersedes: Draft guidance of 2016-07-01 (same title)
sources.uncertainty: None material. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Q3D(R2) - Guideline for Elemental Impurities

supersedes: Q3D(R1) Elemental Impurities (FDA guidance, March 2020)
sources.uncertainty: None material. Not independently re-verified.

supersedes: M7(R1) (FDA guidance issued 2018-03-14)
sources.uncertainty: None material. Not independently re-verified.

Excludes drug discovery and operational-efficiency uses.
sources.uncertainty: No final version was found as of 2026-10, based on secondary sources. CMC relevance is limited to AI models whose output supports product-quality or manufacturing decisions. Not independently re-verified.

sources.code: FDA strategy document under PDUFA VII (FR Doc 2026-14898, 91 FR 46443, 2026-07-23)
sources.title: FDA's Strategy Document on Facilitating Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Readiness for Products With Accelerated Clinical Development
sources.scope: FDA actions and FY2026-2027 plans to support CMC readiness for products with accelerated clinical timelines, including the CMC Development and Readiness Pilot (CDRP), which has run since April 2023 and continues through FY2027.
sources.uncertainty: This is a policy and strategy document, not a requirement. Not independently re-verified.

sources.title: Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products
sources.scope: Core stability data package for registration applications for new drug substances and products in the ICH regions: batch selection, storage conditions, testing frequency, stability commitments, evaluation and labelling. The R2 revision incorporated the relevant recommendations of Q1F. It remains the applicable ICH stability standard until the consolidated ICH Q1 reaches Step 4.
supersedes: Q1A (original)
Q1A(R1) (FDA published it as 'Q1A(R)', FR 7 Nov 2001)
sources.uncertainty: The verifier could not re-fetch the ICH URL or the day-level Step 4 date (6 Feb 2003). FDA announced Q1A(R2), revised to incorporate Q1F recommendations, in the Federal Register of 21 Nov 2003 (68 FR 65717; PubMed 14631936), which is consistent with an early-2003 ICH adoption. ICH dates for the original Q1A and Q1A(R1) were not verified. The consolidated Q1 will supersede this guideline at Step 4. Step 4 had not been reached by mid-2026; the status between June and 4 Oct 2026 is UNCONFIRMED.

sources.title: Photostability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products
sources.scope: Annex to Q1A(R2) setting out the basic photostability testing protocol: forced degradation and confirmatory testing of drug substance and drug product, light sources and minimum exposure. When the consolidated Q1 reaches Step 4, it will supersede Q1B.
sources.uncertainty: Date is month-level only (November 1996); the day was not confirmed. The verifier did not re-verify this entry: no PubMed or Federal Register record of the Q1B availability notice was retrieved.

sources.title: Stability Testing for New Dosage Forms
sources.scope: Annex to the parent stability guideline. Covers the stability data the original applicant should submit for a new dosage form after the original submission for the new drug substance and product. When the consolidated Q1 reaches Step 4, it will supersede Q1C.
sources.uncertainty: Month-level date only. The verifier did not independently corroborate this entry.

sources.title: Bracketing and Matrixing Designs for Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products
sources.scope: How to apply reduced bracketing and matrixing designs to formal stability studies run under Q1A(R2). When the consolidated Q1 reaches Step 4, it will supersede Q1D.
sources.uncertainty: Month-level date (February 2002). FDA's availability notice of 16 Jan 2003 (68 FR 2339; PubMed 12532979) confirms the title and describes Q1D as an annex to Q1A(R), consistent with a 2002 ICH adoption.

sources.title: Evaluation for Stability Data
sources.scope: How to evaluate stability data to propose a re-test period or shelf life, including statistical approaches and limits on extrapolating beyond the period covered by long-term data. When the consolidated Q1 reaches Step 4, it will supersede Q1E.
sources.uncertainty: The Step 4 month (February 2003; the day is believed to be 6 Feb) is not confirmed at day level. FDA's availability notice of 8 Jun 2004 (69 FR 32010; PubMed 15185712) confirms the title and that Q1E supplements Q1A(R2).

sources.title: Stability Data Package for Registration Applications in Climatic Zones III and IV
sources.scope: Withdrawn. Q1F was adopted in 2003 as an annex to Q1A(R2), defining how to use Q1A more broadly for territories in Climatic Zones III and IV. The ICH Steering Committee endorsed its withdrawal in June 2006 (Yokohama) and left storage conditions for Zones III and IV to the regions and WHO.
sources.supersededBy: Regional and WHO climatic-zone stability requirements (no ICH successor)
sources.uncertainty: The date field records the withdrawal (June 2006), which comes from the researcher's ICH snippet and was not re-verified. FDA's notice of 21 Nov 2003 (PubMed 14631936) confirms that Q1F existed and was issued as an annex to Q1A. The day of Q1F's original Step 4 adoption (believed to be February 2003) was not verified.

sources.code: Q1 (Step 2b draft; consolidated revision of Q1A(R2), Q1B, Q1C, Q1D, Q1E and Q5C)
sources.title: Stability Testing of Drug Substances and Drug Products
sources.scope: Consolidated draft that would replace Q1A(R2), Q1B, Q1C, Q1D, Q1E and Q5C with a single guideline, reported as 18 sections and 3 annexes. It extends scope to synthetic and biological drug substances and products and aligns post-approval stability lifecycle management with Q12. Step 2b was reached on 11 April 2025. The ICH work plan targets Step 3 and Step 4 for November 2026.
sources.uncertainty: The verifier could not re-fetch the ICH, EMA or Federal Register pages. The IQ Consortium paper (AAPS J 2021; PMID 34529169; doi 10.1208/s12248-021-00641-6) confirms that ICH's Quality Discussion Group recommended revising Q1A-Q1E and Q5C together. The researcher's report that the June 2026 Assembly in Rio de Janeiro noted progress only, and the absence of Step 4 as of 2026-10-04, are UNCONFIRMED; check ich.org before calling this a draft in customer-facing text. Q1F was withdrawn in 2006 and is not part of this consolidation, so the earlier code 'Q1A-Q1F' was corrected. Extension of scope to vaccines, ATMPs and combination products is unconfirmed.

sources.title: Validation of Analytical Procedures
sources.scope: Validation of new or revised analytical procedures used for release and stability testing of commercial chemical and biological drug substances and products. With a risk-based approach, it may also be applied to other procedures in the control strategy. It covers multivariate procedures and real-time release testing, is paired with Q14, and replaced Q2(R1).
sources.uncertainty: Cassidy et al., J Pharm Sci 2025 (PMID 40154788; doi 10.1016/j.xphs.2025.103749) corroborate that ICH adopted Q2(R2) and Q14 on 1 November 2023. The ICH PDF file name carries 2023-11-30. The 2025 training modules were not re-verified.

sources.title: Impurities in New Drug Substances
sources.scope: Reporting, identification and qualification of impurities in new drug substances made by chemical synthesis, for registration applications. It is not intended to apply during the clinical research stage of development.
supersedes: Q3A (original; FDA guidance of 4 Jan 1996)
Q3A(R1) (FDA published it as 'Q3A(R)', FR 11 Feb 2003)
sources.uncertainty: The day-level date (25 Oct 2006) was not re-verified. The revision chain is corroborated by FDA's Q3A(R) notice (PubMed 12583358). Kenyon et al., Regul Toxicol Pharmacol 2024 (PMID 38761968) corroborate that Q3A/B are not intended for the clinical research phase.

sources.title: Impurities in New Drug Products
sources.scope: Degradation products in new drug products made from chemically synthesised new drug substances: reporting, identification and qualification thresholds based on maximum daily dose. Complements Q3A(R2).
supersedes: Q3B (original; FDA guidance of 19 May 1997)
Q3B(R1) (FDA published it as 'Q3B(R)', FR 14 Nov 2003)
sources.uncertainty: The day-level date (2 Jun 2006) was not re-verified. The revision chain is corroborated by FDA's Q3B(R) notice (PubMed 14619944).

sources.title: Impurities: Guideline for Residual Solvents
sources.scope: Current revision. Sets toxicologically acceptable limits (PDEs) for residual solvents in drug substances, excipients and drug products, and classifies solvents as Class 1, 2 or 3. PDEs are maintained through ICH maintenance revisions. R9 is described as a minor revision to Section 3.4 (analytical procedures) on solvent volatility; this content was not verified. The scope excludes products used during clinical research stages and existing marketed products.
supersedes: Q3C(R8)
sources.uncertainty: Confidence lowered from high: the verifier could not corroborate the Step 4 day, what R9 changed, or the unusual PDF file name. A July 2024 review (Crit Rev Anal Chem; PMID 39058576) cites Q3C(R9) as current. FDA notices on the NMP/THF PDE revision (2003; PubMed 14619948) and the cumene PDE revision (2012; PubMed 22379689) confirm the maintenance-revision mechanism. Q3C(R10) is in development; see ich-q3c-r10-wip.

sources.title: Impurities: Guideline for Residual Solvents - Revision 10 (revised PDEs for N,N-dimethylformamide, dichloromethane and ethylene glycol; monographs restructured into a separate document)
sources.scope: Maintenance revision. The concept paper is dated 26 November 2024 and was reported endorsed by the Management Committee in January 2025. The revision re-examines the PDEs for DMF (after IARC reclassification), DCM and ethylene glycol, and moves compound monographs into a separate document.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified by the verifier. Work plans scheduled Step 2 first for October 2025 and later for January 2026, with Step 4 around December 2026; no published Step 2 draft could be confirmed. Q3C(R9) PDEs apply until R10 is adopted.

sources.title: Guideline for Elemental Impurities
sources.scope: Risk-based assessment and control of elemental impurities in new drug products against route-specific PDEs: oral, parenteral and inhalation, plus cutaneous/transcutaneous, which R2 added. The control threshold is 30% of the PDE. R2 also corrected the PDEs/monographs for gold, silver and nickel. Q3D does not apply to drug products used during clinical research stages of development.
supersedes: Q3D(R1)
Q3D
sources.uncertainty: Corrected: the researcher wrote that R2 'added gold and silver monographs'. Gold and silver were among the elements with monographs in the original Q3D; R2 corrected their PDEs (with nickel's). The exact R2 changes were not verified against official text. The cutaneous route under Q3D(R2) is corroborated by Jurowski & Krosniak 2023 (PMID 36768068), and the 30%-of-PDE threshold and component/finished-product approaches by Ann Pharm Fr 2025 (PMID 40378920). A Q3D(R3) maintenance EWG exists, with no Step 2 or Step 4 found. Placement in 3.2.P.5.5/3.2.P.5.6 is convention.

sources.title: Guideline for Extractables and Leachables (with Supporting Documentation: Class 3 Leachable Monographs)
sources.scope: First harmonised ICH framework for assessing and controlling extractables and leachables from manufacturing components and systems, packaging, and delivery-device components. It builds on Q3A-Q3D, M7 and Q9. It defines a safety concern threshold (the lowest of the M7 TTC, a route- and duration-specific qualification threshold and, where relevant, a local-toxicity threshold) and three leachable classes: Class 1 to be avoided, Class 2 to be limited, and Class 3 of low toxicity, which has supporting monographs. Safety assessment of elemental leachables stays under Q3D. FDA published it as a draft guidance (docket FDA-2025-D-4678).
sources.uncertainty: Draft, not in force. Confidence lowered from high: the Step 2b day conflicts with the file date (1 Aug 2025 vs 2025-07-04), and the EU comment deadline and FDA draft date (1 Dec 2025) were not re-verified. Draft status and the class/SCT/QT content are corroborated by Kuzmic et al., Toxics 2026 (PMID 41600641) and Liu & Liu, Regul Toxicol Pharmacol 2026 (PMID 41905433). No Step 4 is known; the status in Oct 2026 is unconfirmed. The CTD section mapping is inferred.

sources.title: Evaluation and Recommendation of Pharmacopoeial Texts for Use in the ICH Regions
sources.scope: Process for evaluating harmonised pharmacopoeial texts so that regulators can recognise them as interchangeable in the ICH regions. Each favourable evaluation is issued as a topic-specific annex stating the conditions, implementation and regional considerations, so that industry avoids redundant testing.
sources.uncertainty: FDA published the core guideline on 21 Feb 2008 (73 FR 9575; PubMed 18677819), consistent with ICH Step 4 in November 2007. The verifier retrieved FDA notices for these annexes: 1 (residue on ignition/sulphated ash), 2 (extractable volume of parenterals), 3 (subvisible particles), 4A/4B/4C (microbiological examination of non-sterile products), 5 (disintegration), 6 (uniformity of dosage units), 7 (dissolution), 8 (sterility), 9 (tablet friability), 10 (PAGE), 12 (analytical sieving), 13 (bulk and tapped density) and 14 (bacterial endotoxins). Annex 11 and the current implementation status of each annex in each region were not verified.

sources.title: Viral Safety Evaluation of Biotechnology Products Derived from Cell Lines of Human or Animal Origin
sources.scope: Viral safety of biotechnology products: testing of cell lines and raw materials, viral clearance and testing, and the data to submit in marketing applications. R2 adds next-generation sequencing as an alternative to traditional in vivo, in vitro and PCR adventitious-virus tests (Section 3.2.5.2), use of prior and platform knowledge for viral clearance, newer product types, and continuous-manufacturing considerations.
supersedes: Q5A(R1)
sources.uncertainty: Adoption in November 2023 is corroborated by Alston et al., Biologicals 2025 (PMID 40179635) and Anderson et al., PDA J Pharm Sci Technol 2025 (PMID 40300811). The day (1 Nov 2023) was not re-verified. The direct ICH PDF URL was not captured. FDA published the original Q5A in 1998 (PubMed 10185809). The extent of Q5A data expected at clinical-trial stage is set by regional CTA/IND guidance.

sources.title: Quality of Biotechnological Products: Analysis of the Expression Construct in Cells Used for Production of r-DNA Derived Protein Products
sources.scope: Characterising the expression construct and confirming the coding sequence and genetic stability in production cells for recombinant-DNA-derived proteins.
sources.uncertainty: The verifier did not independently corroborate this entry; no PubMed or Federal Register record was retrieved.

sources.title: Quality of Biotechnological Products: Stability Testing of Biotechnological/Biological Products
sources.scope: Stability testing for products whose active components are proteins or polypeptides, augmenting Q1A. In scope are cytokines, erythropoietins, plasminogen activators, plasma factors, growth hormones, insulins, monoclonal antibodies and vaccines made of well-characterised proteins. When the consolidated Q1 reaches Step 4, it will supersede Q5C.
sources.uncertainty: Pending supersession by the consolidated Q1, which had not reached Step 4 by mid-2026; status in Oct 2026 unconfirmed. PMID 34529169 confirms that Q5C is within the stability-series revision.

sources.title: Derivation and Characterisation of Cell Substrates Used for Production of Biotechnological/Biological Products
sources.scope: Origin and history of cell substrates (human, animal and microbial), generation of the production cell line, Master and Working Cell Bank systems, and characterisation for identity, purity and stability through the proposed in vitro cell age.
sources.uncertainty: FDA's notice of 21 Sep 1998 (63 FR 50244; PubMed 12269373) confirms the title and that the guideline recommends information for marketing applications. The day-level ICH date was not re-verified.

sources.title: Comparability of Biotechnological/Biological Products Subject to Changes in Their Manufacturing Process
sources.scope: Principles for assessing whether a biotechnological/biological product is comparable before and after a manufacturing process change, during development or after approval. The exercise is quality-led and may be supplemented by nonclinical or clinical bridging.
sources.uncertainty: FDA's notice of 30 Jun 2005 (70 FR 37861; PubMed 15988855) confirms the title and purpose. A Q5E Annex on ATMP comparability is in development: the concept-paper date (reported May 2025) is low confidence and no draft was confirmed.

sources.title: Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria for New Drug Substances and New Drug Products: Chemical Substances
sources.scope: Setting and justifying acceptance criteria and selecting test procedures for new synthetic drug substances, and the drug products made from them, not previously registered. Covers universal and specific tests and decision trees. A unified Q6(R1) revision is in development.
sources.uncertainty: FDA's notice of 29 Dec 2000 (65 FR 83041; PubMed 12356095) confirms the title and scope. Q6(R1) will supersede Q6A; its Step 4 target (June 2027) is unverified.

sources.title: Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria for Biotechnological/Biological Products
sources.scope: Characterisation and specifications (identity, purity and impurities, potency, quantity) for biotechnological/biological proteins and polypeptides and their products. A unified Q6(R1) revision is in development.
sources.uncertainty: FDA's final notice of 18 Aug 1999 (PubMed 12356094) and draft notice of June 1998 (PubMed 10180131) confirm the title and that the guideline supports new marketing applications. The Q6(R1) Step 4 target (June 2027) is unverified.

sources.title: Revision of the Specification Guidelines ICH Q6A and Q6B
sources.scope: A single revised specification guideline. It keeps shared principles plus separate chemical and biological sections and extends scope to modalities such as cell and gene therapies and to the commercial lifecycle. It aligns with Q8-Q14 and covers reference standards/materials and the role of pharmacopoeias. The concept paper is dated 25 June 2024 (MC endorsement reported 18 July 2024).
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified by the verifier. The researcher reports work-plan targets of Step 2 in November 2026 and Step 4 in June 2027. No draft was known as of mid-2026; status in Oct 2026 unconfirmed.

sources.title: Good Manufacturing Practice Guide for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients
sources.scope: GMP for API manufacture, starting from the introduction of the API starting material. Section 19 covers APIs for use in clinical trials, with controls consistent with the stage of development. FDA originally published it as 'Q7A'.
sources.uncertainty: FDA's notice of 25 Sep 2001 (66 FR 49028; PubMed 12358036) published it as 'Q7A Good Manufacturing Practice Guidance for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients'; ICH now designates it Q7. The day-level ICH date was not re-verified.

sources.title: Questions and Answers: Good Manufacturing Practice Guide for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients
sources.scope: ICH Implementation Working Group Q&As clarifying how to interpret Q7.
sources.uncertainty: The verifier did not independently corroborate this entry. The researcher's illustrative topic list (starting materials, validation, contract manufacturers, clinical-trial APIs) was removed from scope because it was not individually verified.

sources.title: Pharmaceutical Development
sources.scope: Suggested content for CTD section 3.2.P.2 (Pharmaceutical Development): QbD elements (QTPP, CQAs, risk assessment, design space, control strategy, lifecycle). Consolidates the original Q8 parent guideline and the Q8 Annex.
supersedes: Q8 (parent; ICH Step 4 Nov 2005; FDA FR 22 May 2006)
Q8(R1) (parent plus Annex; FDA FR 9 Jun 2009)
sources.uncertainty: Date is month-level (August 2009). FDA notices confirm the parent Q8 (PubMed 16749216) and the parent-plus-Annex version that FDA called 'Q8(R1)' (PubMed 19588572).

sources.title: Quality Risk Management
sources.scope: Principles of quality risk management and examples of tools across the product lifecycle. R1 added sections on formality, managing subjectivity, risk-based decision-making and product-availability risks, and renamed 'risk identification' to 'hazard identification'.
supersedes: Q9 (2005; FDA FR 2 Jun 2006)
sources.uncertainty: The day-level date (18 Jan 2023) comes from the researcher's ICH snippet and was not re-verified. PDA J Pharm Sci Technol 2024 (PMID 38942476) corroborates the recent issuance of Q9(R1) and the ICH training material. The 'hazard identification' rename was not re-verified against the text.

sources.title: Pharmaceutical Quality System
sources.scope: A pharmaceutical quality system model based on ISO concepts that includes applicable GMP and complements Q8 and Q9 across the lifecycle (development, technology transfer, commercial manufacturing, discontinuation), for drug substances and drug products including biotechnology and biological products.
sources.uncertainty: FDA's notice of 8 Apr 2009 (74 FR 15990; PubMed 19507321) corroborates the scope. The day-level ICH date was not re-verified.

sources.title: Development and Manufacture of Drug Substances (Chemical Entities and Biotechnological/Biological Entities)
sources.scope: Approaches to developing and understanding the drug substance manufacturing process, and what to provide in CTD sections 3.2.S.2.2-3.2.S.2.6: process description, starting-material selection, control strategy, process validation/evaluation and lifecycle. Applies to drug substance manufacture only.
sources.uncertainty: FDA's notice of 20 Nov 2012 (77 FR 69634; PubMed 23227566) corroborates the title and scope. The day-level ICH date was not re-verified.

sources.title: Questions and Answers: Selection and Justification of Starting Materials for the Manufacture of Drug Substances
sources.scope: Implementation Working Group Q&As clarifying Q11 Section 5 on selecting and justifying starting materials, focused on chemical entities: information to submit, impurity fate and purge, commercially available versus custom-synthesised materials, and convergent syntheses.
sources.uncertainty: The Step 4 date of 23 Aug 2017 rests on one search result plus ICH training material; the verifier did not re-verify it. The exact official title wording may differ.

sources.title: Technical and Regulatory Considerations for Pharmaceutical Product Lifecycle Management
sources.scope: Core guideline plus annexes defining Established Conditions (ECs), risk-based reporting categories, Post-Approval Change Management Protocols (PACMPs), the Product Lifecycle Management (PLCM) document, and the links to the PQS.
sources.uncertainty: FDA issued Q12 as guidance in May 2021, and the definition of ECs is corroborated by Tran et al. 2024 (PMC10966141). Uptake of ECs, PACMPs and the PLCM document is limited and differs by region (Deavin et al., TIRS 2024, PMID 39179719; Nakayama et al., TIRS 2025, PMID 40839206). The PLCM location (3.2.R or Module 1) was not confirmed from official text.

sources.title: Continuous Manufacturing of Drug Substances and Drug Products
sources.scope: Scientific and regulatory considerations for continuous manufacturing of chemical entities and therapeutic proteins, for new products and for converting batch processes. Covers control strategy, process dynamics and residence time distribution, material traceability and diversion, batch definition, process models and lifecycle.
sources.uncertainty: Q13's emphasis on material traceability, diversion and RTD is corroborated by Chen et al., J Chromatogr A 2026 (PMID 41687211). The day-level date was not re-verified beyond the file name.

sources.title: Analytical Procedure Development
sources.scope: Science- and risk-based development and lifecycle management of analytical procedures under minimal and enhanced approaches: analytical target profile, analytical procedure control strategy, ECs for procedures, change management and submission content. Paired with Q2(R2).
sources.uncertainty: Adoption on 1 Nov 2023 is corroborated by PMID 40154788. The Q12/Q14 link for analytical ECs is corroborated by FDA authors in AAPS J 2025 (PMID 40087229) and J Pharm Sci 2024 (PMID 39111548).

sources.title: Organisation of the Common Technical Document for the Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use
sources.scope: The agreed common format for the CTD: Module 1 is region-specific and Modules 2-5 are common to all regions. Includes the Granularity Annex.
sources.uncertainty: 15 June 2016 is the date the Assembly approved corrections to the revised Granularity Annex, per a researcher snippet; the R4 revision itself may carry another 2016 date. FDA's notice of 16 Oct 2001 (PubMed 12358037) corroborates the M4 CTD's four-part structure (organisation, quality, safety, efficacy). Verify the R4 day against ICH document history before citing it.

sources.title: The Common Technical Document for the Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use: Quality - M4Q(R1); Quality Overall Summary of Module 2; Module 3: Quality
sources.scope: Current harmonised structure and content headings for the Quality Overall Summary (Module 2.3) and the Module 3 body of data: 3.2.S drug substance, 3.2.P drug product, 3.2.A appendices, 3.2.R regional information and 3.3 literature references. M4Q(R2) will supersede it at Step 4.
sources.uncertainty: The day-level date was not re-verified. Tran et al. 2024 (PMC10966141) corroborate that M4Q(R1) is the current CTD quality guideline and that it is under revision as M4Q(R2).

sources.title: M4: The CTD - Quality: Questions and Answers / Location Issues
sources.scope: Implementation Q&As that clarify how to prepare the quality parts of a CTD. They address the relationship between linked sections for certain parameters (e.g., polymorphism and particle size) and the section in which to place requested information.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. The date is FDA's Federal Register availability date (9 Jun 2004; 69 FR 32358; PubMed 15188781); the ICH adoption date of the R1 Q&As was not verified. The ICH URL and the '(R1)' designation come from the researcher's corroborating list and were not re-fetched.

sources.title: The Common Technical Document for the Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use: Quality - M4Q(R2)
sources.scope: Draft restructuring of Module 2.3 and Module 3. Module 2.3 becomes the primary basis for assessment, built from modular components: 2.3.1 General Information, 2.3.2 Overall Development and Control Strategy, 2.3.3 Core Quality Information, development summaries/justifications, optional 2.3.5 Product Lifecycle Management and 2.3.6 Product Quality Benefit-Risk. Module 3 becomes the repository of supporting data. The revision aims to specify where lifecycle-management elements go and to align with Q8-Q14. Scope extends to biologicals and complex multiconstituent products, including device-containing products and ATMPs.
sources.uncertainty: Confidence lowered from high: snippets give the Step 2 sign-off as both 13 and 14 May 2025, the 2.3.x numbering is from the draft and may change (the heading of 2.3.4 is unconfirmed), and the consultation dates, mock example and mapping document were not re-verified. Tran et al. 2024 (PMC10966141) corroborate the revision's aims. The work plan targets Step 4 for June 2027. Not in force; M4Q(R1) applies.

sources.title: Assessment and Control of DNA Reactive (Mutagenic) Impurities in Pharmaceuticals to Limit Potential Carcinogenic Risk
sources.scope: Hazard assessment (database/literature search, two complementary (Q)SAR methodologies with expert review, Ames test), five-class categorisation, acceptable intakes (TTC 1.5 µg/day and less-than-lifetime limits) and control options for mutagenic impurities in new drug substances and products, during clinical development and for marketing applications. Not applicable to products for advanced cancer as defined in ICH S9, or to previously used excipients, flavourings, colourants and fragrances; applies to marketed products only when changes are made. R2 moved HIV treatment from the '>1-10 years' to the '>10 years to lifetime' clinical-use category.
supersedes: M7(R1) (March 2017)
M7 (June 2014)
sources.uncertainty: Honma, Genes Environ 2025 (PMC12723853) corroborates: the revision dates (M7 June 2014, R1 March 2017, R2 April 2023); the HIV category change; the scope exclusions; and that LTL acceptable intakes apply during clinical trials. The day (3 Apr 2023) was not re-verified. Other scope exclusions (e.g., biologics, peptides, oligonucleotides) were not re-verified. An N-nitrosamine addendum (future M7(R3)) is in development.

sources.title: Addendum to ICH M7(R2): Application of the Principles of the ICH M7 Guideline to Calculation of Compound-Specific Acceptable Intakes
sources.scope: Compound-specific acceptable intakes (AIs) or PDEs for mutagenic carcinogens common in pharmaceutical manufacturing or illustrative of the derivation principles (e.g., acrylonitrile, aniline, benzyl chloride, formaldehyde). The R1 addendum (March 2017) covered 14 compounds; R2 (April 2023) added seven more. It also covers higher AIs where background human exposure (endogenous or dietary) greatly exceeds pharmaceutical exposure.
sources.uncertainty: The count (14 compounds in R1, +7 in R2) is confirmed by Honma 2025 (PMC12723853). The individual monographs added in R2 were not listed or verified.

sources.title: M7(R2) Questions and Answers: Assessment and Control of DNA Reactive (Mutagenic) Impurities in Pharmaceuticals to Limit Potential Carcinogenic Risk
sources.scope: 25 implementation Q&As clarifying M7 and the information to provide during development, in marketing applications and in Master Files.
sources.uncertainty: Raised from low: Honma 2025 (PMC12723853) states the Q&A was officially adopted in May 2022 and contains 25 Q&As. The day remains unconfirmed: snippets say 24 May 2022, while the ICH file name carries 2022-04-07. The Q&As were published together with M7(R2) in April 2023.

sources.code: M7 Addendum on N-nitrosamines (future M7(R3); in development)
sources.title: Addendum to ICH M7: Risk Assessment and Control of N-Nitrosamine Impurities (working title)
sources.scope: An M7 sub-group/EWG is developing general principles for setting acceptable intakes for N-nitrosamines, including approaches based on structural characteristics, and a quality risk-management framework for assessing and controlling them. Once final, it will be incorporated as M7(R3). The topic was adopted at the ICH meeting in Fukuoka in June 2024, after an M7(R3) maintenance work plan issued in February 2024.
sources.uncertainty: Raised from low for the topic's existence and its June 2024 adoption, both corroborated by Honma 2025 (PMC12723853), which contradicts the alternative 'May 2025' date. The Step 2a/b target of April 2027 comes only from the researcher's reading of the 2026 work plan and was not verified. The title is a working title. No draft was known as of mid-2026; status in Oct 2026 unconfirmed. Nitrosamine AIs currently come from regional authorities (e.g., CPCA as adopted by EMA, FDA and MHLW).

sources.code: 昭和35年法律第145号 (Act No. 145 of 1960), as amended
sources.title: 医薬品、医療機器等の品質、有効性及び安全性の確保等に関する法律 (Act on Securing Quality, Efficacy and Safety of Products Including Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices, the 'PMD Act'; formerly 薬事法, Pharmaceutical Affairs Act)
sources.scope: Japan's primary pharmaceutical statute. Two facts are CORROBORATED by four independent peer-reviewed sources, three with PMDA authors: (1) the Act took effect in its current form, as the PMD Act, in November 2014; (2) from then it defines cell and gene therapy products as a separate category, regenerative medical products (再生医療等製品), which can receive conditional, time-limited approval. NOT VERIFIED, recalled article numbers: Art. 13-3 (accreditation of foreign manufacturers); Art. 14 (manufacturing/marketing approval, partial change approval, minor change notification, GMP conformity inspection); Art. 14-7-2 (confirmation of change plans for approved matters, i.e. PACMP, added by the 2019 amendment); Art. 41 (Japanese Pharmacopoeia); Art. 56 (sale of a JP drug that does not conform to the JP is prohibited); Art. 80-2 (clinical trial notification, including the 30-day wait after a first CTN); Art. 80-6 (Master File, 原薬等登録原簿).
sources.uncertainty: Corroborated: the PMD Act form in force from November 2014, and the regenerative-medical-product category with conditional, time-limited approval (PMIDs 37526847, 26374217, 26482927, 42776789). Not verified: the 1960-08-10 promulgation date, all article and paragraph numbers (including the post-2019 renumbering of Art. 14), and the effective date of Art. 14-7-2. The e-Gov URL follows the law-ID pattern and could not be opened (egress to laws.e-gov.go.jp is blocked).

sources.code: 令和元年法律第63号 (Act No. 63 of 2019)
sources.title: 医薬品、医療機器等の品質、有効性及び安全性の確保等に関する法律等の一部を改正する法律 (Act Partially Amending the PMD Act, etc.)
sources.scope: Amending act. Recalled as introducing, for CMC: the change-plan confirmation system for approved matters (変更計画の確認, Japan's statutory PACMP, Art. 14-7-2) and statutory import confirmation (輸入確認). Also recalled as introducing conditional approval and SAKIGAKE designation for drugs. Provisions took effect in phases.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED; no corroborating search result was found. Unverified: the act number, the 2019-12-04 promulgation date, the phase dates (recalled as 2020-09-01, 2021-08-01 and 2022-12-01) and which phase brought in PACMP. PMID 40839206 confirms only that Japan implemented ICH Q12, including PACMP as part of the PLCM concept, from 2021; it does not cite this Act. The URL is the MHLW landing page.

sources.code: 昭和36年厚生省令第1号 (MHW Ordinance No. 1 of 1961), as amended
sources.title: 医薬品、医療機器等の品質、有効性及び安全性の確保等に関する法律施行規則 (Ordinance for Enforcement of the PMD Act)
sources.scope: Implementing ordinance. CORROBORATED by PMID 40839206: Art. 47 sets the scope of changes that may be handled by minor change notification, and changes to ICH Q12 established conditions reported that way must still comply with it. NOT VERIFIED, recalled: what the approval application form must contain; the CTN content, change, termination and discontinuation provisions (recalled as around Arts. 268-270); MF registration particulars.
sources.uncertainty: Only Art. 47's role as the minor-change scope rule is corroborated, by one secondary source (PMID 40839206). Not verified: the CTN article numbers, the exact wording of Art. 47, the ordinance number and date. The URL follows the e-Gov law-ID pattern and was not opened.

sources.code: 平成9年厚生省令第28号 (MHW Ordinance No. 28 of 1997), as amended
sources.title: 医薬品の臨床試験の実施の基準に関する省令 (Ministerial Ordinance on Good Clinical Practice for Drugs, J-GCP)
sources.scope: Japanese GCP. CORROBORATED by PMID 40445582: J-GCP is one of the three rule sets governing clinical trials in Japan. NOT VERIFIED, recalled CMC-relevant articles: Art. 5 (quality, toxicity and pharmacology studies must be completed before requesting a trial); Art. 8 (investigator's brochure contents); Art. 16 (IMP labelling in Japanese and prohibited label items); Art. 17 (supply of IMP from sites with appropriate manufacturing and quality control).
sources.uncertainty: Only the existence of J-GCP and its role are corroborated. Not verified: the article numbers and their content, the ordinance number and date, and whether an amendment implementing ICH E6(R3) was made in 2025-2026.

sources.code: 薬生薬審発0831第10号 (2020-08-31) — identifier not verified
sources.title: 治験の依頼をしようとする者による薬物に係る治験の計画の届出等に関する取扱いについて (Handling of Clinical Trial Notifications for Drugs by Persons Intending to Request Clinical Trials)
sources.scope: Operating rules for the CTN (治験計画届). Recalled content: form entries (IMP code/name, ingredients and quantities, dosage form, route, manufacturing site(s), planned supply quantity); attachments (reasons the trial is judged scientifically justified, protocol, IB, informed-consent materials, CRF template); notifications of change, completion and discontinuation. CORROBORATED by PMC12771677: PMDA's review and any document amendments for a first CTN are completed exactly 30 calendar days after submission, so sites can be contracted on day 31.
supersedes: 薬食審査発0531第8号 (2013-05-31), same title — not verified
sources.uncertainty: Only the first-CTN 30-day review is corroborated, by one secondary source (Novartis authors, Clin Transl Sci 2026). Not verified: the identifier, the date, the superseded notification, the form and attachment list, and any later partial revisions (e.g. 2023-2025 drug-loss measures allowing English IB/protocol). Current status as of 2026-10-04 could not be established. The URL is a landing page.

sources.title: 治験薬の製造管理、品質管理等に関する基準（治験薬GMP）について (Standards for Manufacturing Control and Quality Control of Investigational Products — Investigational Product GMP)
sources.scope: Japanese GMP for investigational drugs (治験薬GMP), recalled as a PFSB Director-General notification. Recalled content: organisation and QA; manufacturing and QC records; retention samples; validation or verification built up as development progresses; equivalent standard for IMPs made outside Japan. PMID 26234351 corroborates only that hospital sites in Japan run IMP manufacture under 'GMP for INDs'.
supersedes: 薬発第480号 (1997-03-31), the earlier 治験薬GMP notification — not verified
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED. The identifier, date, effective date (believed 2009-04-01), superseded notification and content are all recalled. Not established as of 2026-10-04: whether a revision aligning with PIC/S Annex 13 or the newer EU IMP GMP has been issued. The deep URL is unknown.

sources.code: 平成16年厚生労働省令第179号 (MHLW Ordinance No. 179 of 2004), as amended by 令和3年厚生労働省令第90号
sources.title: 医薬品及び医薬部外品の製造管理及び品質管理の基準に関する省令 (GMP Ministerial Ordinance for Drugs and Quasi-drugs)
sources.scope: GMP for commercial drug products and drug substances. Recalled: the 2021 amendment (promulgated 2021-04-28, effective 2021-08-01) added a pharmaceutical quality system, a QA unit, supplier management and data-reliability provisions in alignment with PIC/S. Compliance is confirmed by GMP conformity inspection. Regenerative medical products fall under a separate ordinance (GCTP), which was not researched.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED; no corroborating search result was found. Ordinance numbers and dates are recalled. Modalities narrowed from 'all' because regenerative medical (CGT) products are covered by a separate GCTP ordinance, whose existence is recalled and not verified. The URL follows the e-Gov pattern and was not opened.

sources.title: 医薬品の承認申請について (On Applications for Approval of Drugs)
sources.scope: Defines application categories, such as new active ingredient, and the attached data (イ–ト) each needs. ロ = manufacturing method, specifications and test methods (structure determination, physicochemical properties, manufacturing, specifications and test methods). ハ = stability (long-term, stress/severe, accelerated).
supersedes: 薬食発第0331015号 (2005-03-31) — not verified
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED; no corroborating search result was found. Unverified: the identifier, date, data-category lettering and later partial amendments. The deep URL is unknown.

sources.code: 医薬審発第899号 (2001-06-21), as amended
sources.title: 新医薬品の製造又は輸入の承認申請に際し承認申請書に添付すべき資料の作成要領について (Guidelines for Preparing Data to be Attached to Applications for Approval of New Drugs — Japanese CTD implementation)
sources.scope: Recalled as implementing ICH M4 CTD in Japan and defining the Japanese Module 1. Recalled language rule: application form, Module 1 and Module 2 in Japanese; Modules 3–5 may be in English. CTD format recalled as mandatory for new drug applications from 2003-07-01.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED; no corroborating search result was found. The status as the current CTD notification is uncertain: it may have been replaced or amended (e.g. for M4 revisions or Japanese eCTD v4.0). Not verified: Module 1 numbering, the language rule, the 2003-07-01 mandatory date and the eCTD v4.0 timeline.

sources.title: 改正薬事法に基づく医薬品等の製造販売承認申請書記載事項に関する指針について (Guideline on Particulars to be Described in Marketing Approval Application Forms under the Revised Pharmaceutical Affairs Law)
sources.scope: Explains how to complete the 製造方法 field (sites, process flow, parameters, in-process controls, critical steps) and the 規格及び試験方法 field. CORROBORATED by PMID 40839206: Notification No. 0210001 of 2005-02-10, issued by the Director of the Evaluation and Licensing Division, PFSB, introduced in 2005 the system of symbols/annotations on approved matters. These fix at approval whether a later change goes by partial change application or minor change notification, and the examples in it are illustrative, with classification decided case by case. MHLW treats these annotated approved matters as equivalent to ICH Q12 established conditions.
sources.uncertainty: The identifier, date, English title and annotation function are corroborated by one peer-reviewed source (JPMA Regulatory Affairs Committee, Ther Innov Regul Sci 2025). By the task rule, a single non-official source leaves confidence 'low'. The symbols themselves are deliberately not recorded. Later Q&As and amendments are not verified. The deep URL is unknown.

sources.code: Notification of 2021-07-30, No. 6, Director of the Pharmaceutical Evaluation Division, PSEHB — as cited in PMID 40839206; full Japanese identifier not verified
sources.title: Entries in the Specifications and Test Methods Column of Applications for Approval of Pharmaceuticals, etc., and Their Changes (English title as given in PMID 40839206; Japanese title not verified)
sources.scope: MHLW notification on how the 規格及び試験方法 (specifications and test methods) column of the approval application is written, and how changes to it are handled. PMID 40839206 cites it alongside notification 0210001 and Enforcement Regulations Art. 47 as governing how ICH Q12 established conditions map onto Japanese approved matters.
sources.uncertainty: ADDED BY VERIFIER from one secondary source, whose citation text is partly garbled. Not verified: the exact identifier (possibly of the form 薬生薬審発0730第6号), the Japanese title, the content and the current status. Do not quote to customers until checked against the MHLW/PMDA database.

sources.title: 原薬等登録原簿の利用に関する指針について (Guideline on the Use of the Master File System)
sources.scope: Japanese Master File (MF, 原薬等登録原簿). Recalled content: registration of drug substances, intermediates, excipients and container/closure materials; the MF number cited in product applications; the holder–applicant contract; the in-country caretaker (原薬等国内管理人) for foreign registrants; MF change registrations and minor change notifications; the holder's duty to inform users. PMID 27518176, by PMDA authors, corroborates only that PMDA runs an ASMF/DMF (MF) procedure.
supersedes: 薬食審査発第0210004号 (2005-02-10) — not verified
sources.uncertainty: Not verified: the identifier, date, superseded notification and all content. Only the existence of a PMDA MF procedure is corroborated. The deep URL is unknown.

sources.code: JP18 — 令和3年厚生労働省告示第220号 (MHLW Ministerial Notification No. 220 of 2021)
sources.title: 第十八改正日本薬局方 (The Japanese Pharmacopoeia, Eighteenth Edition)
sources.scope: Official Japanese compendium: General Notices, General Tests, Processes and Apparatus, monographs and General Information. Peer-reviewed articles published January–May 2026 (PMIDs 41638652, 41943023, 42107610) still cite JP18 as the edition in use, e.g. the JP18 sterility test 4.06, harmonised with USP <71> and Ph. Eur. 2.6.1. Supplement I was recalled as 2022-12 and Supplement II as 2024-06.
supersedes: JP17 (2016-03) — not verified
sources.uncertainty: JP18 being in use into mid-2026 is corroborated by literature. Not verified: the 2021-06-07 date, Notification No. 220, the Supplement I/II dates and numbers. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether JP19 was promulgated between mid-2026 and 2026-10-04 and superseded JP18. The previous 'supersededBy' value was removed because no successor is established.

sources.code: JP19 (第十九改正日本薬局方) — no notification number established
sources.title: The Japanese Pharmacopoeia, Nineteenth Edition
sources.scope: Next full JP revision. CORROBORATED by PMID 36858562 (NIHS authors, 2023): the JP is fully revised every five years and partially revised in between, and 'basic principles for the preparation of the JP 19th edition' exist, including internationalisation of test methods. That implies a JP19 date of about 2026, but this is inference only.
supersedes: jp-jp18 (only if promulgated — not established)
sources.uncertainty: Not established: whether JP19 was promulgated as of 2026-10-04, and its MHLW notification number, effective date and transition period. Do not cite JP19 to customers until verified. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: 平成15年厚生労働省告示第210号 (MHLW Ministerial Notification No. 210 of 2003), as revised
sources.title: 生物由来原料基準 (Standard for Biological Ingredients)
sources.scope: Requirements for raw materials of human or animal origin used in manufacture (e.g. serum, cell substrates, ruminant/TSE-relevant materials): origin, donor screening, inactivation/removal and records. PMC13600107 (2026) notes, in general terms, that PMDA imposes additional TSE qualification obligations on raw materials for CGT products; it does not name this standard.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED: the notification number, date and revision history (recalled as 2014 and 2018). The researcher's statement that compliance is checked for IMPs at the CTN 30-day review was REMOVED from scope as unsupported.

sources.code: 平成15年法律第97号 (Act No. 97 of 2003)
sources.title: 遺伝子組換え生物等の使用等の規制による生物の多様性の確保に関する法律 (Act on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Biological Diversity through Regulations on the Use of Living Modified Organisms — 'Cartagena Act')
sources.scope: Living modified organisms need one of two clearances before use: approval of Type 1 use regulations (open use), or confirmation of Type 2 containment measures. This covers viral-vector gene therapy products and live recombinant vaccines, including clinical-trial IMPs.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED: PubMed searches returned no relevant corroboration. The act number, date and Type 1/Type 2 mechanism are recalled. The URL follows the e-Gov pattern and was not opened.

sources.code: Notification No. 0709-2 (as cited in PMC13600107); recalled as 薬生機審発0709第2号 — full identifier and year not verified
sources.title: 遺伝子治療用製品等の品質及び安全性の確保について (Ensuring the Quality and Safety of Gene Therapy Products, etc.) — Japanese title recalled; English subject as given in PMC13600107
sources.scope: Japanese quality and safety expectations for gene therapy products. PMC13600107 cites it for: adventitious-agent controls, controls on human-derived materials, qualification of biological raw materials used in potency assay systems, and biodistribution expectations.
sources.uncertainty: ADDED BY VERIFIER from one secondary narrative review, which gives no year and calls it a 'PMDA Notification'. Not verified: the bureau prefix, date, Japanese title, issuing body (MHLW vs PMDA) and current status. Note that '0709' also appears in the unrelated 治験薬GMP identifier 0709002 (2008); check that they are not confused. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: PMDA 対面助言 (face-to-face consultation) implementing outline — identifier not verified
sources.title: PMDA Consultation Services for Drugs (e.g. 医薬品品質相談 quality consultation, 医薬品第I相試験開始前相談 pre-Phase 1 consultation, 申請前相談 pre-application consultation)
sources.scope: Scientific and regulatory consultations with PMDA, including quality (CMC) consultations and consultations before Phase 1 and before application. CORROBORATED: PMDA consultations exist across development stages; more consultations, and prior-assessment consultations, are associated with shorter later NDA review times (PMID 29714577); evidentiary questions for regenerative products are settled through face-to-face consultation with PMDA (PMC13600107).
sources.uncertainty: Only the existence and general use of PMDA consultations is corroborated. Not verified: fees, the current consultation menu names, the issuing of official minutes, the implementing notification and the deep URL. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: PIC/S Members (Participating Authorities)
sources.scope: Recorded for one fact: Japan (MHLW, PMDA and prefectures) and Korea (MFDS) are recalled as becoming PIC/S Participating Authorities effective 2014-07-01. CORROBORATED by PMID 25707200 (NIHS, 2014): Japan applied for PIC/S membership in March 2012 and had to meet PIC/S requirements, including an inspectorate quality system and OMCL access under ISO 17025.
sources.uncertainty: Japan's March 2012 application is corroborated. The 2014-07-01 accession date for Japan and Korea is NOT verified.

sources.title: ICH Members and Observers
sources.scope: Recorded for two facts. (1) MHLW is a founding ICH member and Japan an original ICH region; corroborated by PMC13010624 and PMID 40839206. (2) MFDS (Korea) was admitted as an ICH Regulatory Member in November 2016, alongside ANVISA, in the first cohort of new Regulatory Members after the 2015 reform; corroborated by PMC13600107 only.
sources.uncertainty: The MHLW founding role has two independent secondary corroborations. MFDS's November 2016 admission has one secondary source, so the entry stays low. The ich.org page was not opened.

sources.code: 약사법 — 법률 제300호 (Act No. 300, 1953-12-18), as amended
sources.title: 약사법 (Pharmaceutical Affairs Act)
sources.scope: Korea's primary pharmaceutical statute. CORROBORATED by PMID 26374218 (MFDS-context review, 2015): MFDS regulates medicinal products, including gene and cell therapy products as biologics, under the PAA, with approval for clinical-trial use and for marketing. Also corroborated by PMC9597240: clinical trials of advanced biopharmaceuticals still follow the existing pharmaceutical law. NOT VERIFIED, recalled: Art. 31 (manufacturing business licence and product approval, 품목허가) and Art. 34 (approval of clinical trial plans).
sources.uncertainty: The Act's role is corroborated. Not verified: the article numbers and the original act number and date. The law.go.kr name-based URL was not opened (egress blocked).

sources.code: 의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙 (Prime Ministerial Ordinance), as amended
sources.title: 의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙 (Regulations on Safety of Pharmaceuticals, etc.)
sources.scope: Implementing rules of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. Recalled content: Art. 24 (documents for clinical trial plan approval); annexes setting KGCP and KGMP standards, including investigational-product provisions; documents for product approval.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED; no corroborating search result was found. Not verified: the ordinance number, the date, Art. 24, and which annex (별표) holds KGCP and the IMP GMP standard. The URL was not opened.

sources.code: 식품의약품안전처 고시 — 의약품 임상시험 계획 승인에 관한 규정
sources.title: 의약품 임상시험 계획 승인에 관한 규정 (Regulation on Approval of Clinical Trial Plans for Pharmaceuticals; cited in PMC7921003 as 'Guideline for Approving Clinical Study Plans on Drugs')
sources.scope: MFDS notification giving the detailed IND submission data, review procedure and changes to approved plans. CORROBORATED by PMC7921003 (Integr Med Res 2020; legislation reviewed to 2020-04-20): Korea introduced the IND in December 2002, and the IND package lists protocol, IB, manufacturing and quality data, nonclinical data, prior clinical experience, institution/investigator/CRO data, ICF, compensation rules, GMP compliance documents and a development plan. Art. 7(2) of the regulation exempts certain herbal investigator INDs from nonclinical data; that provision was implemented in 2009.
sources.uncertainty: The existence of the regulation and the 2020 content are corroborated by one peer-reviewed source. Not established: the notification number, latest revision date and current item list as of 2026-10-04. The URL was not opened. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: 식품의약품안전처 고시 — 의약품 제조 및 품질관리에 관한 규정
sources.title: 의약품 제조 및 품질관리에 관한 규정 (Regulation on Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Quality Control — KGMP detailed rules)
sources.scope: Detailed KGMP rules, recalled as aligned with PIC/S, including GMP evaluation and inspection procedures for domestic and overseas sites.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED; no corroborating search result was found. Not established: whether this regulation or the Regulations on Safety holds the IMP GMP annex, its revision number and its date. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: 의약품의 품목허가·신고·심사 규정 (Regulation on Approval, Notification and Review of Pharmaceuticals)
sources.scope: MFDS notification recalled as setting data requirements and format for product approval, including the CTD format for new drugs. PMID 27518176 corroborates that MFDS operates a DMF procedure; its link to this regulation is not verified.
sources.uncertainty: NOT VERIFIED. Not established: the notification number, latest revision, the date CTD became mandatory for new drugs, and the Korean DMF legal basis. The URL is a landing page. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: 첨단재생의료 및 첨단바이오의약품 안전 및 지원에 관한 법률 — act number not verified
sources.title: 첨단재생의료 및 첨단바이오의약품 안전 및 지원에 관한 법률 (Act on the Safety of and Support for Advanced Regenerative Medicine and Advanced Biological Products — 'Advanced Regenerative Bio Act', ARMAB)
sources.scope: ADDED BY VERIFIER. Passed by the National Assembly plenary on 2019-08-02, enacted August 2019, implemented 2020 (August 2020 per PMC13600107). It covers advanced biopharmaceuticals (cell therapy, gene therapy, tissue-engineered and advanced bio-convergence products) and advanced regenerative medicine. Content per PMC9597240: MFDS licensing of manufacturers and importers (Arts. 23–27), with quality-control obligations from cell collection through testing, processing and storage, and a mandatory record-management room; MFDS licence for businesses handling human cells as raw materials, with mandatory donor suitability assessment (Arts. 28–29); long-term follow-up of designated products (Art. 30); expedited review designation (Art. 36). Clinical trials of advanced biopharmaceuticals follow the existing Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. Subordinate rules (2020) include 'Regulations on approval and safety of human cells, etc. and Advanced Biopharmaceuticals'.
sources.uncertainty: The enactment month (2019-08) and implementation (2020) have two independent peer-reviewed corroborations. Not verified: the act number, exact promulgation and effective dates, and current article numbering, which is taken from a 2022 review and may have changed through later amendments. The law.go.kr URL follows the name pattern and was not opened.

sources.title: Reimagining Early-Phase Clinical Development in Japan: From Regulatory Obligation to Global Acceleration
sources.scope: Corroborates the Japanese CTN process: PMDA's review and document amendments for a first CTN are completed exactly 30 calendar days after submission, and sites can be contracted on day 31. Clinical holds are described as unlikely in Japan. About half of first-in-Japan studies at one site started within 70 days of CTN submission. Also reports a 2023 MHLW notification relaxing the expectation of a Japanese Phase 1 before joining MRCTs (clinical, not CMC).
sources.uncertainty: Retrieved in full text. This is a secondary industry-authored source; it corroborates but does not replace the CTN legal instruments.

sources.title: Implementation of Established Conditions and Use of Quality by Design Principles during Drug Development: Status in the US, EU, and Japan. Data from a Survey Conducted by the Japan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association (JPMA)
sources.scope: Corroborates five points. (1) Since 2005, notification 0210001 (2005-02-10) has required symbols/annotations on approved matters fixing at approval whether a later change goes by partial change application or minor change notification. (2) Enforcement Regulations Art. 47 governs minor change notifications. (3) ICH Q12 has applied in Japan since 2021; ECs equal the approved matters stated in the application form, and the PLCM includes the PACMP. (4) Japan has no separate post-approval change classification guideline like those of the US and EU. (5) A notification of 2024-09-30 allowing risk-based changes was issued, but its guidelines were not yet published. Also: 64 of 191 Japanese NDAs from 2019 to 2024 defined ECs, and over 70% of Japanese new-drug approvals have used QbD elements since 2021.
sources.uncertainty: Retrieved in full text. A secondary source; its citations of MHLW notifications are partly garbled, e.g. the 2021-07-30 notification and the 2024-09-30 notification lack full identifiers.

sources.title: Regulation and status of herbal medicine clinical trials in Korea: a narrative review
sources.scope: Reviews Korean IND legislation updated to 2020-04-20. Points: Korean IND introduced December 2002; MFDS approval plus IRB approval and KGCP required; trials of approved drugs within approved indications exempt from IND; 30 working days from submission to the first supplementary notice; IND and IRB review may run in parallel. IND contents: protocol, IB, manufacturing and quality data (active ingredient and amount, manufacturing method, manufacturer, standard test methods, QC results), nonclinical data (toxicology and safety pharmacology in GLP facilities), prior clinical experience, institution/investigator/CRO data, ICF, compensation rules, GMP compliance documents and a development plan. Trials run at MFDS-designated institutions.
sources.uncertainty: Retrieved in full text. A 2020 snapshot from a herbal-medicine perspective; MFDS rules may have been revised since.

sources.title: Impact and challenges of enactment for advanced regenerative medicine in South Korea
sources.scope: Describes Korea's ARMAB Act: enacted August 2019 (plenary passage 2019-08-02) and implemented 2020, with 2020 subordinate regulations. Article-level content covers MFDS manufacturer/importer licensing, quality control from cell collection onward, human-cell management licensing with donor suitability assessment, long-term follow-up, and expedited review (customised review, priority review, conditional approval on Phase 2 data). Clinical trials follow the existing pharmaceutical law.
sources.uncertainty: Retrieved in full text. Secondary source; article numbering as of 2022.

sources.title: Regulatory Convergence in Cell and Gene Therapy: Harmonizing Quality, CMC, and Approval Pathways Across the FDA, EMA, PMDA, and Emerging Markets
sources.scope: Narrative review current to June 2026. Japan: the PMD Act and Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine took effect November 2014; conditional, time-limited approval for regenerative products; PMDA gene therapy quality expectations cited as 'Notification No. 0709-2'; additional raw-material TSE qualification. Korea: ARMAB enacted August 2019 and implemented August 2020; MFDS admitted as ICH Regulatory Member in November 2016 alongside ANVISA.
sources.uncertainty: Retrieved in full text. A two-author narrative review; some regulatory citations lack full identifiers, so use only as corroboration.

sources.title: Regulatory Aspects of Cell and Gene Therapy Products: The Japanese Perspective
sources.scope: PMDA Office of Cellular and Tissue-Based Products authors. In November 2014 the Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine and the PMD Act came into effect; the PMD Act provides conditional, time-limited approval for CGT products.
sources.uncertainty: Abstract retrieved only; full text is not open access.

sources.title: Regulatory Frameworks for Gene and Cell Therapies in Japan
sources.scope: PMDA authors. The PMD Act and the Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine were enacted in November 2014. The PMD Act defines regenerative medical products for the first time and introduces conditional, time-limited marketing authorisation for them.
sources.uncertainty: Abstract retrieved only.

sources.title: [Accession to the PIC/S and pharmaceutical quality system in Japan]
sources.scope: Japan applied for PIC/S membership in March 2012. Accession required a GMP-inspectorate quality system and access to ISO 17025-accredited OMCLs.
sources.uncertainty: Abstract only, in Japanese with an English abstract. Does not state the accession date.

sources.title: Similarities and Differences of International Practices and Procedures for the Regulation for Active Substance Master Files/Drug Master Files of Human Use: Moving Toward Regulatory Convergence
sources.scope: A gap-analysis survey of ASMF/DMF procedures among 12 regulators, including PMDA (Japan) and MFDS (Korea). Corroborates that both operate ASMF/DMF (MF) procedures covering submission, assessment, changes and API GMP inspection.
sources.uncertainty: Abstract only; jurisdiction-specific details not retrieved.

sources.title: Regulatory Oversight of Gene Therapy and Cell Therapy Products in Korea
sources.scope: MFDS regulates gene and cell therapy products as biological products under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. They are subject to clinical-trial approval, marketing authorisation and post-market surveillance.
sources.uncertainty: Abstract only; predates the 2019 ARMAB Act.

sources.title: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada RDC nº 945/2024: diretrizes e procedimentos para a realização de ensaios clínicos com medicamentos (sintéticos e semissintéticos, fitoterápicos, radiofármacos, biológicos e biossimilares) com todo ou parte do desenvolvimento clínico no Brasil para fins de registro
sources.scope: Brazil's clinical-trial regulation for medicines (synthetic and semi-synthetic, herbal, radiopharmaceutical, biological and biosimilar) where all or part of the clinical development is in Brazil for registration purposes. Defines the DDCM (Dossiê de Desenvolvimento Clínico de Medicamento) and the DEEC (Dossiê Específico de Ensaio Clínico). Art. 28, as summarised but not read verbatim, requires the Dossiê do Produto sob Investigação (DPI) or an IMPD with quality data on the active substance and on the investigational medicine. Reported to exempt phase IV and non-interventional trials from Anvisa review, to allow continuous submission of partial data before the definitive DDCM, and to allow reliance-based optimized review under IN 338/2024. Published in the DOU 2024-12-02; reported in force 2025-01-01. Replaced RDC 9/2015.
sources.uncertainty: Identity, date and DOU publication rest on the DOU, gov.br and two law-firm alerts the researcher cited. The verifier could not re-search them: this session's WebSearch budget was already used up, and WebFetch to regulator domains is egress-blocked. Not read verbatim: the Art. 28 item list, the 90-working-day review period with release by lapse of time, and the 15-working-day DEEC deadline. The researcher's claim that RDC 945 also revoked RDC 449/2020 could not be confirmed and was removed from the scope.
supersedes: anvisa-rdc-9-2015

sources.title: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada RDC nº 9/2015: regulamento para a realização de ensaios clínicos com medicamentos no Brasil
sources.scope: The previous Brazilian clinical-trial regulation. It introduced the DDCM/DEEC structure and the investigational-product dossier. Superseded by RDC 945/2024, reported effective 2025-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: Supersession by RDC 945/2024 rests on several law-firm alerts. PMID 42594328 (JCO Glob Oncol 2026), which the verifier retrieved, confirms RDC 09/2015 (with RDC 10/2015) as the regime that changed Anvisa review in 2015.

sources.title: Instrução Normativa IN nº 338/2024: estabelece a lista de Autoridades Reguladoras Estrangeiras Equivalentes (AREE) e critérios para adoção do procedimento otimizado de análise (reliance e avaliação de risco e complexidade) de petições de DDCM, DEEC, modificações substanciais ao produto sob investigação e emendas substanciais ao protocolo
sources.scope: Lists the Autoridades Reguladoras Estrangeiras Equivalentes (AREE) and sets criteria for optimized review, by reliance or by risk and complexity assessment, of DDCM and DEEC petitions, substantial modifications to the investigational product, and substantial protocol amendments. Amended by IN 345/2025.
sources.uncertainty: Identity and date rest on the researcher's gov.br news item and a state health-department copy of the text; the verifier could not re-check them. The AREE list was removed from the scope. A secondary summary named EMA, Health Canada, WHO, EDQM, Swissmedic, MHRA, US FDA and TGA. WHO and EDQM do not authorise clinical trials, so the summary probably merges this list with a different reliance list. Read the consolidated text (as amended by IN 345/2025) for the current AREE list.

sources.title: Instrução Normativa IN nº 345/2025: altera a Instrução Normativa nº 338, de 29 de novembro de 2024
sources.scope: Amends IN 338/2024. Under reliance, the DPI/IMPD version submitted to Anvisa must be the same as the one approved by at least one AREE. For products registered in Brazil or by an AREE, products modified for the trial, and fixed-dose combinations, only the DPI/IMPD information on the modifications is analysed. States that Anvisa will issue a further normative act or guidance on the quality requirements of RDC 945/2024 Art. 28.
sources.uncertainty: Content comes from search-result summaries of the official text, and the verifier could not re-check it. The snippet named EMA, Health Canada and Swissmedic for DPI reliance and may be truncated. Whether the promised quality-requirements act had been published by 2026-10-04 was not established.

sources.code: Manual para Submissão de DDCM e DEEC (4ª edição, 2025)
sources.title: Manual de Submissão de Dossiê de Desenvolvimento Clínico de Medicamento (DDCM) e Dossiê Específico de Ensaio Clínico (DEEC)
sources.scope: Procedural manual on assembling DDCM and DEEC petitions under RDC 945/2024, IN 338/2024 and IN 345/2025.
sources.uncertainty: The edition (4th) and date were inferred from the file name (24-02-25) and the NIH ClinRegs listing. A later 2026 edition was neither confirmed nor ruled out. The verifier could not re-check it, because clinregs.niaid.nih.gov is also egress-blocked.

sources.code: Perguntas e Respostas – RDC 945/2024 e IN 338/2024, Ed. 3 (26/12/2025)
sources.title: Perguntas e Respostas sobre a RDC nº 945/2024 e a Instrução Normativa nº 338/2024 – 3ª edição
sources.scope: Non-binding Q&A on primary DDCM and DEEC petitions, substantial protocol amendments, and substantial modifications to the investigational product. States that DPI/IMPD information should follow a logical structure and recommends the CTD Module 3 format (ICH M4).
sources.uncertainty: A trade-association item (Sincofarma, 2026-08-13) reports a further Q&A update focused on fixed-dose combinations. Its edition and date were not confirmed, so Ed. 3 may no longer be current. The edition and date come from the official URL path; the verifier did not re-check them.

sources.code: Manual de Submissão dos Requisitos de Qualidade – Medicamentos Sintéticos e Semissintéticos, 3ª edição
sources.title: Manual de Submissão dos Requisitos de Qualidade referente aos Produtos sob Investigação Utilizados em Ensaios Clínicos – Medicamentos Sintéticos e Semissintéticos (3ª edição)
sources.scope: Guidance on the quality data for synthetic and semi-synthetic investigational medicines in the investigational-medicine dossier within the DDCM, written under RDC 9/2015.
sources.uncertainty: The 2019 year comes from a single search summary. The manual was written under RDC 9/2015. Whether Anvisa still applies it under RDC 945/2024, or has replaced it with the act promised in IN 345/2025, was not established.

sources.code: Manual de Submissão dos Requisitos de Qualidade – Produtos Biológicos, 3ª edição
sources.title: Manual de submissão dos dados de qualidade referente aos produtos sob investigação utilizados em ensaios clínicos: produtos biológicos (3ª edição)
sources.scope: Guidance on the quality data for biological investigational products in the DDCM, written under RDC 9/2015.
sources.uncertainty: The publication date was not found. Its status under RDC 945/2024 is unknown. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada RDC nº 658/2022: Diretrizes Gerais de Boas Práticas de Fabricação de Medicamentos
sources.scope: General GMP for medicines in Brazil, aligned with PIC/S. Applies across the lifecycle, including the manufacture of investigational medicines. A manufacturing authorization holder must make medicines that meet their registration or their authorization for use in a clinical trial. Replaced RDC 301/2019.
sources.uncertainty: Replacement of RDC 301/2019 rests on a secondary source only. The verifier did not re-check it.

sources.title: Instrução Normativa IN nº 136/2022: Boas Práticas de Fabricação complementares a Medicamentos Experimentais
sources.scope: Adopts the PIC/S GMP guideline for investigational (experimental) medicines as requirements complementary to RDC 658/2022. Applies to companies that manufacture investigational medicines. Includes definitions for blinding, randomization codes, comparators and similar terms.
sources.uncertainty: Not established whether IN 136/2022 follows the PIC/S Annex 13 revision that entered into force on 2022-02-01 or the earlier text. Not re-checked by the verifier.

sources.title: Guia para Organização do Documento Técnico Comum (CTD) para o Registro e Pós-registro de Medicamentos – versão 1
sources.scope: Non-binding guide to organizing registration and post-registration dossiers in CTD format (five modules) for new, innovative, biological, generic, similar, radiopharmaceutical, specific and herbal medicines. Adopting the CTD format was optional.
sources.uncertainty: Superseded status depends on Guia 24 v2 (2026), which the verifier could not independently confirm.

sources.title: Guia para Organização do Documento Técnico Comum (CTD) para o Registro e Pós-registro de Medicamentos – versão 2
sources.scope: Version 2 of the CTD organization guide. Published 2026-05-04 and in effect, with public contributions open until 2026-11-04. Reported changes: full integration of the CADIFA flow into the CTD format, and electronic filing of registration and post-registration requests.
sources.uncertainty: Not confirmed whether v2 makes CTD mandatory or keeps it recommended. Open for comment until 2026-11-04 and may be revised. The verifier could not re-check it, and it post-dates the verifier's reference knowledge.
supersedes: anvisa-guia-24-2019-v1

sources.title: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada RDC nº 753/2022: registro de medicamentos de uso humano com princípios ativos sintéticos e semissintéticos, classificados como novos, inovadores, genéricos e similares
sources.scope: Registration of synthetic and semi-synthetic medicines. Revoked RDC 200/2017. Includes a section on technical quality documentation. The CTD format is recommended through Guia 24.
sources.uncertainty: The entry-into-force date is unverified; one secondary snippet says 2022-11-01. Later amendments, for example by RDC 948/2024, were not mapped.

sources.title: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada RDC nº 948/2024: requisitos gerais para a regularização sanitária de medicamentos de uso humano
sources.scope: General framework for regularizing medicines, either by registration (prior review of the technical file) or by notification. Covers categorization, required documents, validity periods and minimum quality, safety and efficacy parameters in the technical file. In force 2025-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: How it interacts with the product-specific RDCs (753/2022, 55/2010) was not mapped in detail. Not re-checked by the verifier.

sources.title: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada RDC nº 359/2020: institui o Dossiê de Insumo Farmacêutico Ativo (DIFA) e a Carta de Adequação de Dossiê de Insumo Farmacêutico Ativo (CADIFA)
sources.scope: Brazil's API dossier (DIFA) and adequacy letter (CADIFA) for APIs used in new, innovative, generic and similar medicines. Published in the DOU 2020-04-01; in force 2020-08-03.
sources.uncertainty: Publication and in-force dates come from search summaries. Later amendments and any phase-in of mandatory CADIFA were not mapped.

sources.title: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada RDC nº 55/2010: registro de produtos biológicos novos e produtos biológicos
sources.scope: Brazil's registration rule for biological products. Reported as still in force, complemented or amended in 2024 (e.g., RDC 875/2024).
sources.uncertainty: The scope of the 2024 amendments (RDC 875/2024, 876/2024, 914/2024, 915/2024) was not verified. Whether any part of RDC 55/2010 was revoked by them is unknown. There is only one secondary source.

sources.title: Anvisa international position: ICH membership (observer December 2015; regulatory member November 2016)
sources.scope: ANVISA became an ICH observer in December 2015 and a regulatory member in November 2016. It takes part in ICH working groups.
sources.uncertainty: The researcher's claim that the ICH Assembly met in Rio de Janeiro on 2–3 June 2026 was removed from the scope. It was unverifiable and not material to CMC.

sources.code: PIC/S news: Brazil / ANVISA joins PIC/S
