sources.title: Brazil / ANVISA joins PIC/S (54th Participating Authority as of 1 January 2021)
sources.scope: The PIC/S Committee decided by written procedure, completed 2020-11-27, to admit ANVISA. ANVISA has been a Participating Authority since 2021-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: None material. Consistent with the verifier's reference knowledge; not re-searched.

sources.code: G.S.R. 227(E), 19 March 2019 – New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
sources.title: The New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
sources.scope: India's rules for clinical trials and new-drug approval, made under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. They replaced the Schedule Y framework for new drugs and clinical trials. Clinical-trial application on Form CT-04 and permission on Form CT-06. Manufacture of new drugs/INDs for trials: application on Form CT-10, permission on CT-11 (valid 3 years). Import application on Form CT-16. New-drug marketing: applications on Forms CT-18 (import) and CT-21 (manufacture), with permissions on CT-19/CT-20 and CT-23. The Second Schedule sets the data requirements, including chemical and pharmaceutical information and stability.
sources.uncertainty: The Second Schedule chemical and pharmaceutical items and stability conditions come from summaries of the official PDF, not a verbatim read. Item and table numbers are not quoted. Deemed approval on silence applies, on the verifier's reading, only to the 30-working-day route for drugs discovered or developed in India and to be made and marketed there (rule 23), not to the general 90-working-day route (rule 22); confirm against the verbatim text. PMID 39140018 (Perspect Clin Res 2024), retrieved by the verifier, dates the rules to 19 March 2019. Amended in 2026 (see india-ndct-amendment-2026); other amendments were not mapped.

sources.code: G.S.R. 46(E), 20 January 2026 – New Drugs and Clinical Trials (Amendment) Rules, 2026
sources.title: New Drugs and Clinical Trials (Amendment) Rules, 2026
sources.scope: Replaces the test licence for non-commercial manufacture (analytical and non-clinical testing) with a prior-intimation mechanism. Excluded high-risk categories, which still need permission: sex hormones, cytotoxics, beta-lactams, biologics with live microorganisms, narcotics and psychotropics. Cuts the statutory timelines for permissions under rules 53 and 60 from 90 to 45 working days. Exempts certain low-risk BA/BE studies from prior permission. Reported in force 45 days after Gazette publication. A Second Amendment Rules, 2026 was also reported.
sources.uncertainty: The Gazette text was not read. The G.S.R. number and date come from consultancy and newsletter sources plus the PIB release; the verifier did not re-check them. The content and G.S.R. number of the Second Amendment Rules, 2026 were not established. The RAPS headline ('CDSCO halves clinical…') may refer to clinical-trial timelines, so whether the CT-04 (rule 22) timeline itself changed remains open.

sources.title: Schedule M (revised): Good Manufacturing Practices and Requirements of Premises, Plant and Equipment for Pharmaceutical Products (Drugs Rules, 1945)
sources.scope: Revised, WHO-aligned Indian GMP. Introduces a pharmaceutical quality system, quality risk management, product quality review, and equipment qualification and validation. Includes a part on manufacturing investigational pharmaceutical products for clinical trials in humans (part number not verified). Applied to large manufacturers (turnover above Rs 250 crore) from 2024-06-28, and to all manufacturers from 2026-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: The URL is a third-party copy of the Gazette notification; no official CDSCO or egazette URL was found. 'Part VII' for the investigational-products part comes from two secondary summaries only. PMID 42237438 (Indian J Med Ethics 2026), retrieved by the verifier, confirms the December 2023 GMP/QRM amendments and compliance by all manufacturers, small and large, from 2026-01-01.

sources.title: Notification on conditional extension of the timeline for implementation of revised Schedule M for small and medium manufacturers
sources.scope: Conditionally extended revised Schedule M compliance for manufacturers with turnover of Rs 250 crore or less to 2025-12-31, on application in Form A with an upgrade plan. The extension has now lapsed: all manufacturers have had to comply since 2026-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: The G.S.R. number comes from a secondary listing of CDSCO notifications. PMID 42237438 corroborates that compliance became universal from 2026-01-01, so no further general extension is evident.

sources.code: CDSCO Guidelines on Common Technical Document (28.10.2010)
sources.title: Guidelines on Common Technical Document (CTD)
sources.scope: CDSCO guidance, based on ICH M4, on the five-module submission format. Module 3 covers quality information for chemical, pharmaceutical and biological products. The CTD sets the format, not the content.
sources.uncertainty: Its current status after the NDCT Rules 2019 was not confirmed, nor whether CTD is mandatory for all new-drug applications. No second independent source was found.

sources.title: Guidance for Industry: Submission of Clinical Trial Application for Evaluating Safety and Efficacy; Requirements for Permission of New Drugs Approval; Post-approval Changes in Biological Products; Preparation of the Quality Information for Drug Submission for New Drug Approval: Biotechnological/Biological Products
sources.scope: CDSCO guidance on clinical-trial applications and on quality information for new-drug approval of biotechnological and biological products.
sources.uncertainty: The 2008 date comes from a search summary. The document predates the NDCT Rules 2019, and its current status is unknown. CDSCO posted a draft revised Guidance for Industry for comment at an undetermined date.

sources.title: Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2016
sources.scope: Regulates clinical trials of therapeutic products and, since the 2021 CTGTP framework, Class 2 CTGTPs. Covers quality and safety of investigational products, sponsor and investigator duties, GCP, consent and safety reporting. Sets the CTA and CTN routes. Gazetted 2016-07-15; in operation 2016-11-01.
sources.uncertainty: Later amendments, including those bringing Class 2 CTGTPs in from 2021-03-01 and the 2023-12-11 consolidation shown on SSO, were not mapped item by item.

sources.code: S 332/2016 – Health Products (Clinical Research Materials) Regulations 2016
sources.title: Health Products (Clinical Research Materials) Regulations 2016
sources.scope: Controls on importing, supplying, labelling, record-keeping and disposing of clinical research materials. A CRM notification is required before import, unless the material is locally registered and the importer is its licensed importer. Notifications are valid one year.
sources.uncertainty: The date is the gazette date inferred from the WTO file name. Commencement was not confirmed and is presumed to be 2016-11-01, like S 331/2016.

sources.title: Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2016
sources.scope: Governs clinical trials of medicinal products, as distinct from therapeutic products under the Health Products Act, through the Clinical Trial Certificate (CTC) route. Before 2021-03-01, high-risk cell- and tissue-based products and gene therapy products were regulated as medicinal products under the Medicines Act, with trials under a CTC (PMID 26374220). From 2021-03-01 they moved to the Health Products Act CTGTP framework (PMID 37526849).
sources.uncertainty: Exact gazette and commencement dates were not confirmed. Which products remain under the CTC route after the 2021 CTGTP transfer was not mapped.

sources.title: Clinical Trials Guidance: Regulatory Requirements for New Applications and Subsequent Submissions
sources.scope: Documents for CTA, CTN and CTC: protocol, consent form, investigator's brochure for unregistered products, GMP certificates (finished-product manufacturer for unregistered investigational and auxiliary products; also the drug-substance manufacturer for biologics and Class 2 CTGTPs), certificates of analysis for study batches, and CMC information when requested. Also covers subsequent submissions. Revision history: GN-CTB-2-003A-001 (2016-11-01), -002 (2017-05-02), Rev. 003 (2021-03-01), Rev. 004 (2021-04-28).
sources.uncertainty: Rev. 004 (2021) is the latest revision confirmed. A later revision may exist; the file.go.gov.sg link may host a newer version. Not re-checked by the verifier.

sources.title: Clinical Trials Guidance: Labelling of Investigational and Auxiliary Products in Clinical Trials
sources.scope: Labelling principles for investigational and auxiliary products: participant protection and traceability, identification of product and trial, correct use and storage, and data reliability. Covers therapeutic products, CTGTPs and medicinal products.
sources.uncertainty: The revision number and date come from a single search summary. The URL is HSA's guidance index page, not the PDF.

sources.title: Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls Requirements for Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTP) for Clinical Trials and Product Registration
sources.scope: CMC dossier expectations for Class 2 CTGTPs in clinical trials and registration: origin of starting materials, quality of reagents, manufacturing process and controls, analytical methods, and stability.
sources.uncertainty: 2026-06-23 is the date HSA's guidance page reports as last updated. The file name says only '23 Jun', and the year of Ver 2 itself was not confirmed.

sources.code: Guidance on Therapeutic Product Registration in Singapore (updated 1 April 2026)
sources.title: Guidance on Therapeutic Product Registration in Singapore – Application Dossier (ICH CTD / ACTD; eCTD)
sources.scope: Registration dossiers must be in English and in ICH CTD format (quality in Module 3) or ASEAN CTD format (quality in Part II). The format cannot change after submission. eCTD (ICH v3.2.2 with SG-HSA regional spec v1.1) has been accepted voluntarily since 2026-04-01. Updates effective 2026-01-16 include an option to ask HSA to inspect overseas drug-substance sites lacking GMP evidence for NCE/NBE applications. From 2026-06-01, a declaration is reported to be required that the CMC dossier has no known quality defects needing update.
sources.uncertainty: The CMC-declaration requirement (from 2026-06-01) comes from search summaries of secondary sources. The guidance's own document code and revision number were not captured. Not re-checked by the verifier.

sources.code: Health Products (Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products) Regulations 2021 (in force 1 March 2021)
sources.title: Health Products (Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products) Regulations 2021 and related subsidiary legislation under the Health Products Act
sources.scope: HSA's risk-based CTGTP framework, implemented on 1 March 2021 through 11 pieces of subsidiary legislation gazetted under the Health Products Act. CTGTPs are classed as lower-risk Class 1 or moderate- to higher-risk Class 2, based on degree of manipulation, intended use, and whether they are combined or used with therapeutic products or medical devices. Regulatory controls, including clinical-trial and quality requirements, are calibrated to the class.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. The source is a peer-reviewed chapter by an HSA Advanced Therapy Products Branch author (PMID 37526849, 2023), retrieved via PubMed. The SSO citation (S numbers) of the 11 instruments was not established, so the URL is HSA's CTGTP guidance index rather than the legislation itself.

sources.title: HSA – International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) membership
sources.scope: HSA became an ICH Regulatory Member in November 2017 (Geneva Assembly). It has participated in PIC/S since 2000, the first Asian authority to do so.
sources.uncertainty: None material. Consistent with the verifier's reference knowledge; not re-searched.

sources.title: WHO good manufacturing practices for investigational products
sources.scope: WHO GMP for investigational pharmaceutical products. They must be manufactured, packaged, tested, handled, stored and distributed under an effective quality management system, applicable good-practice guidelines and this guideline. Revises the 1996 supplementary guidelines (TRS 863, Annex 7). WHO PQ inspection services raised the revision urgently after inspecting COVID-19 therapeutics.
sources.uncertainty: The exact month of the WHO web posting is unconfirmed (one result says August 2022). The annex number and the TRS 863 Annex 7 predecessor agree with the verifier's reference knowledge.
supersedes: WHO TRS No. 863 (1996), Annex 7

sources.title: IAEA/WHO guideline on good manufacturing practices for investigational radiopharmaceutical products
sources.scope: Minimum GMP standards for preparing novel radiopharmaceuticals without marketing authorization for phase I–III clinical investigations.
sources.uncertainty: Downgraded from high. The researcher's academic corroboration (PMC11325260 = PMID 38821100, Lancet Oncol 2024) was retrieved in full text by the verifier. It does not mention this guideline, only that the IAEA has addressed regulatory frameworks for radiopharmaceuticals, so it was removed. The WHO PDF file name reads 'good-manufacturing-practices-for-radiopharmaceutical-products' without 'investigational'. WHO also has a separate IAEA/WHO GMP guideline for (non-investigational) radiopharmaceutical products, so confirm the Annex 3 title on the PDF cover before citing.

sources.title: Stability testing of active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished pharmaceutical products
sources.scope: Core stability data package for registering APIs and FPPs. Long-term conditions depend on climatic zone, including 30 °C/65% RH for zone IVa and 30 °C/75% RH for zone IVb. Includes a table of long-term conditions notified by WHO Member States. Replaced TRS 953 Annex 2 (2009). ICH hosts it as the reference after ICH Q1F was withdrawn.
sources.uncertainty: No newer ECSPP-adopted WHO stability guideline was found as of 2026-10-04. Whether the ICH Q1 consolidated revision (Step 2 draft, April 2025) reached Step 4 by 2026-10-04 was not established. PMID 29354559 (2017), retrieved by the verifier, applies WHO zone IVb storage as 30 ± 2 °C / 75 ± 5% RH. Zone I–III conditions were not quoted from a verified snippet.
supersedes: WHO TRS No. 953 (2009), Annex 2

sources.title: Guidelines on submission of documentation for a multisource (generic) finished pharmaceutical product for the WHO Prequalification of Medicines Programme: quality part
sources.scope: Quality-part dossier requirements for WHO prequalification of generic FPPs, organized per ICH M4Q (CTD-Quality), including the Quality Overall Summary (Module 2.3) and Module 3.
sources.uncertainty: Not confirmed whether WHO PQ has issued a newer quality-part guideline that supersedes TRS 970 Annex 4.

sources.title: Guidelines on submission of documentation for a multisource (generic) finished pharmaceutical product: quality part
sources.scope: Version of the PQ quality-part guideline intended for national medicines regulatory authorities. Structured per ICH M4Q, using WHO terms (API, FPP, product dossier).
sources.uncertainty: None material.

sources.code: WHO TRS No. 961 (2011) – Procedure for prequalification of pharmaceutical products (annex number believed to be Annex 10)
sources.title: Procedure for prequalification of pharmaceutical products (WHO Expert Committee on Specifications for Pharmaceutical Preparations, TRS 961, 2011)
sources.scope: The 2011 ECSPP report (TRS 961) adopted a procedure for prequalification of pharmaceutical products, together with a guide on submission of documentation for prequalification of innovator FPPs approved by stringent regulatory authorities, and guidelines on preparing multisource product dossiers in CTD format. Presumed predecessor of the TRS 1067 Annex 4 procedure.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. PubMed record PMID 21699061 (World Health Organ Tech Rep Ser 2011;(961):1-428) confirms that TRS 961 adopted a 'procedure for prequalification of pharmaceutical products'. The annex number (10) comes from the verifier's reference knowledge, not the PubMed abstract. Supersession by TRS 1067 Annex 4 is inferred from the identical title and the researcher's report of a 2025–2026 revision; it was not confirmed from a WHO document. No official who.int URL was confirmed.

sources.title: Procedure for prequalification of pharmaceutical products
sources.scope: Current WHO procedure for prequalifying pharmaceutical products for UN procurement. Published in the 59th ECSPP report (meeting October 2025; report published 2026-06-09). Revised from draft QAS/25.974 (March 2025).
sources.uncertainty: 2026-06-09 is the publication date of the TRS 1067 report. The predecessor is presumed to be the TRS 961 (2011) procedure (who-trs961-pq-procedure-2011, low confidence). The verifier did not re-check it, and it post-dates the verifier's reference knowledge.
supersedes: who-trs961-pq-procedure-2011

sources.code: PIC/S GMP Guide (PE 009) Annex 13 – revised (entered into force with PE 009-16, 1 Feb 2022)
sources.title: PIC/S Guide to Good Manufacturing Practice for Medicinal Products, Annex 13: Manufacture of Investigational Medicinal Products
sources.scope: PIC/S revised Annex 13 on the basis of the EU framework under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, which replaced EU Annex 13. The Committee adopted it with the new Annex 16 (Certification by the Authorised Person and Batch Release) by written procedure on 2022-01-26, in force 2022-02-01 in PE 009-16. Carried unchanged into PE 009-17 (in force 2023-08-25) and PE 009-18 (in force 2026-09-24). Requires a Product Specification File. ANVISA adopts the PIC/S IMP GMP guideline through IN 136/2022.
sources.uncertainty: The 2022-02-01 entry into force and PE 009-17's 2023-08-25 date agree with the verifier's reference knowledge. The 2022-01-26 adoption date and the PE 009-18 carry-over were not re-checked. PIC/S-specific deviations from the EU 2017 Detailed Commission guideline were not itemized. Whether Annex 13 says applicable PSF sections must exist before the first batch was not verified verbatim.

sources.title: PIC/S Guide to Good Manufacturing Practice for Medicinal Products (PE 009-18)
sources.scope: Current PIC/S GMP Guide. Adopted by written procedure on 2026-09-22; in force 2026-09-24. The only change is a revised Annex 19 (reference and retention samples, Section 9 on parallel-traded products). Part I, Part II and all other annexes, including Annex 13, are unchanged from PE 009-17.
sources.uncertainty: The verifier could not re-check it: picscheme.org is egress-blocked and the search budget was used up. It is about 10 days old as of 2026-10-04 and post-dates the verifier's reference knowledge. Confidence rests on the researcher's official-domain (picscheme.org) news item plus one secondary source.

sources.title: Detailed Commission guideline of 8 December 2017 on good manufacturing practice for investigational medicinal products for human use, pursuant to the second subparagraph of Article 63(1) of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014
sources.scope: EU detailed IMP GMP guideline. It replaced EudraLex Volume 4 Annex 13 for trials under the CTR and is the basis for the revised PIC/S Annex 13.
sources.uncertainty: The CTR transition for Directive 2001/20/EC trials ended 2025-01-30, so all EU trials now fall under the CTR and this guideline. The status of the old EU Annex 13 page on EudraLex was not re-checked.

sources.title: Decade of Progress: Ethical and Regulatory Approval Timelines for Cancer Clinical Trials in Brazil (JCO Global Oncology, 2026;12(8):e2600138)
sources.scope: Retrospective analysis of 196 oncology trials (2013–2023). ANVISA mean final approval time fell from 341 days (2013) to 90 days (2023). Covers the periods before and after RDC 09/2015 and 10/2015. Notes that recent legislation introducing centralized ethical review and mandatory response deadlines is expected to improve this further. Corroborates the RDC 9/2015 history.
sources.uncertainty: Peer-reviewed secondary source; metadata and abstract retrieved and confirmed by the verifier. It does not cover how RDC 945/2024 has performed.

sources.title: Systematic Review on Clinical Trial Regulations: Perspectives from India, USA, and Europe (Rev Recent Clin Trials, 2026;21(2))
sources.scope: Systematic review noting that India replaced Schedule Y with the NDCT Rules, under CDSCO oversight. Corroborates the NDCT framework.
sources.uncertainty: Corroborates at abstract level only, with no CMC detail. Metadata confirmed by the verifier.

sources.title: Regulatory and operational challenges in conducting Asian International Academic Trial for expanding the indications of cancer drugs (Clin Transl Sci, 2021;14(3):1015-1025)
sources.scope: Multi-country academic registration trial in Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Singapore. Reports regional differences in GMP-related documents and in investigational-product labelling, import and export. Corroborates jurisdiction-specific IMP GMP documentation, including HSA's.
sources.uncertainty: Predates several HSA guidance revisions. Metadata confirmed by the verifier.

sources.title: Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme: An Overview (Cureus, 2024;16(9):e69043)
sources.scope: Review of PIC/S's role in harmonizing GMP standards and in exchanging inspection reports among participating authorities.
sources.uncertainty: General overview; it does not discuss Annex 13 specifically. Metadata confirmed by the verifier.

sources.title: Regulatory Oversight of Cell, Tissue, and Gene Therapy Products in Singapore (Adv Exp Med Biol, 2023;1430:197-210)
sources.scope: Chapter by an HSA Advanced Therapy Products Branch author. HSA implemented a risk-based CTGTP framework on 1 March 2021, with 11 pieces of subsidiary legislation gazetted under the Health Products Act as the Health Products (CTGTP) Regulations 2021. Class 1 (lower-risk) and Class 2 (moderate- to higher-risk) are stratified by degree of manipulation, intended use, and combination with therapeutic products or devices.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier; metadata and abstract retrieved via PubMed. Abstract-level only, with no CMC detail.

sources.title: Regulatory Oversight of Cell- and Tissue-Based Therapeutic Products and Gene Therapy Products in Singapore (Adv Exp Med Biol, 2015;871:195-212)
sources.scope: HSA-authored review of the regime before 2021. High-risk cell- and tissue-based therapeutic products and gene therapy products were regulated as medicinal products under the Medicines Act, with clinical trials under a Clinical Trial Certificate. Historical context for the 2021 move to the Health Products Act.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. It describes a superseded regime (pre-2021) and is historical only.

sources.title: Compromised quality of medicines: a regulatory failure (Indian J Med Ethics, 2026;XI(2):93-97)
sources.scope: States that from 1 January 2026 all Indian manufacturers, small and large, must comply with the December 2023 amendments to Schedule M of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, covering GMP and quality risk management and intended to upgrade Indian manufacturing to WHO GMP standards.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. This is a commentary by a journalist and an advocate, not a regulatory-science study. It corroborates the compliance date only.

sources.title: Addressing varenicline adherence through repackaging in a dose administration aid (Integr Pharm Res Pract, 2017;6:131-135)
sources.scope: Stability study that applies WHO zone IVB storage as 30 ± 2 °C and 75 ± 5% RH, citing the WHO guidelines on pharmaceutical stability testing. Corroborates the zone IVb condition in WHO TRS 1010 Annex 10.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. It corroborates only the zone IVb condition, and it predates TRS 1010 (it cites the earlier WHO stability guideline, whose IVb condition is the same).

sources.title: From Clinical Trials to Commercialization: Perspectives in Human Vaccine (Pharm Res, 2025;43(1):1-8)
sources.scope: Stakeholder study of how India's NDCT Rules 2019 work in practice for vaccines. It reports prolonged approval timelines, ambiguous legal mechanisms, fragmented oversight, and inconsistent documentation practices.
sources.uncertainty: Added by the verifier. Abstract level only; it corroborates that the NDCT Rules 2019 are the operative framework, not specific CMC items.

sources.title: The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004
sources.scope: The main UK law for clinical trials of investigational medicinal products (CTIMPs), in force as amended. It requires a clinical trial authorisation (CTA) from MHRA before a trial starts. It also covers the ethics committee opinion, substantial amendments, IMP manufacture and import (manufacturing authorisation for IMPs, Qualified Person certification) and IMP labelling. Under the pre-2026 text, MHRA's statutory timelines are: first review of an initial application within 30 days; sponsor reply to grounds for non-acceptance within 14 days; decision within 60 days where grounds for non-acceptance are raised; and substantial amendments decided within 35 days. It transposed Directive 2001/20/EC. Amended many times, including by SI 2006/1928, the 2019 EU-exit clinical trials amendments, and the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (full effect 2026-04-28).
sources.uncertainty: An MHRA-authored peer-reviewed article confirms the identifier, the title, the CTA-before-start requirement and the statutory timelines quoted above: Manfrin et al. 2025, 'Evaluation of the MHRA's introduction of a risk-proportionate approach for clinical trials', Br J Clin Pharmacol, PMID 41047928, PMC12930005. The made date (2004-04-01) and in-force date (2004-05-01) are model knowledge and were not verified, because legislation.gov.uk is blocked. Also unverified: the Part/regulation numbering of the MIA(IMP) and QP provisions, and the consolidated text as amended from 2026-04-28, including whether the 2025 Regulations changed the 30/35/60-day timelines.

sources.title: The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Amendment Regulations 2006
sources.scope: Amended SI 2004/1031 to implement Commission Directive 2005/28/EC: GCP principles, the trial master file, and requirements on IMP manufacturing and import authorisations.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified; no literature or official snippet could be retrieved. The made date is given to the month only. The 2006-08-29 in-force date is model knowledge.

sources.title: The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019
sources.scope: EU-exit amendments to SI 2004/1031, applying from the end of the transition period (2020-12-31). They include the arrangements for importing IMPs into Great Britain from listed approved countries under QP oversight. (The parallel EU-exit amendments to the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 are believed to be in a separate instrument, SI 2019/775, The Human Medicines (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, which is not included here.)
sources.uncertainty: VERIFIER CORRECTION, based on model knowledge only. The researcher titled SI 2019/744 'The Human Medicines (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019'. The verifier believes that title belongs to SI 2019/775, and that SI 2019/744 is the clinical-trials EU-exit instrument; this also matches the scope the researcher described. Neither attribution could be checked because legislation.gov.uk is blocked, so confirm the number–title pairing before citing it. Also unverified: the made date (month only), the commencement mechanics (amended to apply at IP completion day), and which IMP-import provisions sit here rather than in later EU-exit SIs.

sources.code: The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (UK statutory instrument; SI number not verified)
sources.title: The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025
sources.scope: The new UK clinical trials framework, amending SI 2004/1031 and in full effect from 2026-04-28. It codifies combined MHRA/REC review in law and introduces a risk-proportionate approach: notifiable lower-risk trials and expedited handling of lower-risk modifications (amendments). It requires trial registration and results publication. Sponsors may extend the reply to a request for information from 14 to up to 60 days. ICH E6(R3) is implemented alongside it. It also has transitional arrangements for trials authorised under the earlier text. It was signed into law in 2025.
sources.uncertainty: The title (made as '2025', not '2024'), the 2026-04-28 full-effect date, codified combined review, the risk-proportionate routes, the transparency duties and the E6(R3) alignment come from Alghabban 2026, 'The UK's 2026 Clinical Trial Regulations: A Strategic Analysis for Global Pharmaceutical Sponsors', Ther Innov Regul Sci, PMID 41758490 (abstract only). Manfrin et al. 2025 (MHRA authors; PMID 41047928, PMC12930005) independently confirms that the regulations are signed into law, take effect in 2026, introduce notifiable trials, and allow the 14-to-60-day RFI extension. The exact day 2026-04-28 rests on one source. Not verified: the SI number, the made date (believed April 2025), the laying date in draft (believed 2024-12-12), any staggered commencement, the detail of the transitional provisions, and the CMC-specific changes (IMP and auxiliary-product labelling, manufacturing and assembly exemptions). No official URL could be confirmed.

sources.title: The Human Medicines Regulations 2012
sources.scope: The main UK law for medicines placed on the market. It covers marketing authorisations (Part 5) and the material that must accompany an MA application (Schedule 8, which carries over the Annex I / CTD content requirements). It also covers manufacturer's licences and Qualified Persons, and the legal status of the British Pharmacopoeia. Amended post-Brexit.
sources.uncertainty: Date corrected from 2012-07-24 to 2012-07. The verifier believes the instrument was made on 2012-07-19 and laid on 2012-07-24 (the researcher's date), with entry into force on 2012-08-14. All three dates and the Part/Schedule numbering are model knowledge and were not verified.

sources.code: MHRA guidance: Clinical trials for medicines: apply for authorisation in the UK
sources.title: Clinical trials for medicines: apply for authorisation in the UK
sources.scope: MHRA guidance on the documents a UK CTA needs. These include the IRAS combined-review application, the protocol, the IB, and an IMPD or simplified IMPD (or the SmPC for an unmodified UK-authorised product). Manufacturing and import authorisation information is also required.
sources.uncertainty: Status changed from 'final' to 'unknown'. This page was very probably revised or replaced for the regulations in full effect from 2026-04-28, and its current content, date and URL could not be verified because gov.uk is blocked. The URL slug and content are model knowledge. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: Combined review of clinical trials of investigational medicinal products (MHRA and Research Ethics Committee)
sources.scope: A single IRAS application sent at the same time to MHRA and the HRA-managed Research Ethics Committee, giving one coordinated UK review. It is the standard CTIMP route and is codified in law by the 2025 amending regulations (full effect 2026-04-28).
sources.uncertainty: The single-IRAS-application mechanism is confirmed by PMID 41047928 (MHRA authors), and its codification under the 2025 regulations by PMID 41758490. Not verified (model knowledge): the date it became mandatory for all new CTIMPs (2022-01-01), the 2018 pilot start, and the URL.

sources.code: MHRA risk-proportionate approach: notification scheme for lower-risk clinical trials (administrative, introduced October 2023)
sources.title: MHRA notification scheme for lower-risk clinical trials
sources.scope: Part of the risk-proportionate approach MHRA's Clinical Trials Unit introduced in August 2023. From October 2023, lower-risk phase 3 and 4 trials meeting set criteria are notified rather than fully assessed; trials that do not meet the criteria are assessed in full. The 2025 amending regulations make notifiable lower-risk trials a statutory route.
sources.uncertainty: NEW ENTRY added by the verifier. It rests on PMID 41047928 (MHRA authors) and, for the statutory successor, PMID 41758490. Not retrieved: the official guidance title, URL and eligibility criteria. Not established: whether the administrative scheme has been formally replaced by the statutory notification route since 2026-04-28, so status is 'unknown'.

sources.title: International Recognition Procedure
sources.scope: MHRA reliance route in operation since 2024-01-01. It replaced the European Commission Decision Reliance Procedure (ECDRP) and the Mutual Recognition/Decentralised Reliance Procedure (MRDCRP). MHRA takes into account an approval by one of seven reference regulators: TGA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, HSA, PMDA, FDA, and EMA or EU/EEA member-state competent authorities. Recognition A requires the reference approval to be within the preceding 2 years, Recognition B within the preceding 10 years. MHRA can still refuse an application if the evidence is insufficient. MHRA guidance sets separate timetables for A and B, believed to be 60 and 110 days (not verified).
sources.uncertainty: These points are confirmed by one peer-reviewed source, 'International comparison of medicines approvals in the UK: a retrospective analysis', BMJ Open 2025, PMID 41248376, PMC12587917: the 2024-01-01 start, the replaced routes, the seven reference regulators, the 2-year and 10-year eligibility windows, and MHRA's ability to refuse. Not verified: the 60/110-day timetables, the guidance publication date (believed 2023) and later revisions, how strictly an identical Module 3 is required, and the URL slug.

sources.code: MHRA guidance: 150-day assessment for national applications for medicines
sources.title: Guidance on 150-day assessment for national applications for medicines
sources.scope: MHRA national route, available from 2021-01-01, in which a complete, high-quality MA application is assessed within 150 days, excluding clock-stops.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified. The publication date, URL slug and current procedural details are model knowledge.

sources.code: MHRA guidance: Apply for a licence to market a medicine in the UK
sources.title: Apply for a licence to market a medicine in the UK
sources.scope: MHRA guidance on UK MA applications. It covers CTD/eCTD format with the UK Module 1, submission through the MHRA portal, the QP declaration on active substance GMP, and the ASMF and CEP routes for active substance data.
sources.uncertainty: Status changed from 'final' to 'unknown' because the current revision could not be checked. Content and URL are model knowledge. The UK ASMF procedure may be in a separate MHRA page. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: MHRA guidance: Good manufacturing practice and good distribution practice
sources.title: Good manufacturing practice and good distribution practice
sources.scope: MHRA guidance on UK GMP. It covers manufacturer's licences including MIA(IMP), Qualified Persons, inspections, and the UK GMP guide, which is based on the EU GMP guide as it stood at the end of the transition period.
sources.uncertainty: Status changed from 'final' to 'unknown' because the current revision could not be checked. URL and content are model knowledge. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: MHRA guidance: Importing investigational medicinal products into Great Britain from approved countries
sources.title: Importing investigational medicinal products into Great Britain from approved countries
sources.scope: Explains how IMPs QP-certified in a listed approved country (EU/EEA) are imported into Great Britain. The UK importer holds an MIA(IMP), and its QP checks through an oversight system that each batch was certified, rather than re-certifying it.
sources.uncertainty: Status changed from 'final' to 'unknown': whether the arrangement and page were changed by the 2025 regulations in effect from 2026-04-28 could not be checked. Title, URL and publication date are model knowledge. Northern Ireland / Windsor Framework arrangements are not covered.

sources.code: MHRA guidance: EU guidance documents referred to in the Human Medicines Regulations 2012
sources.title: EU guidance documents referred to in the Human Medicines Regulations 2012
sources.scope: MHRA statement that EU guidance in force at the end of the transition period continues to apply in the UK unless MHRA says otherwise. This is how EMA quality guidelines, including those on IMP quality, keep applying to UK dossiers.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified. Title, URL and date are model knowledge, and MHRA's current policy on EU guidelines issued after 2020 was not checked.

sources.title: British Pharmacopoeia 2026
sources.scope: The UK's legally binding pharmacopoeia, published every year (usually in August) and legally effective from the following 1 January. BP 2026 is the edition in force through 2026-12-31. BP 2027, if published in August 2026, takes effect on 2027-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified. The edition cycle and dates are model knowledge. Whether BP 2027 had been published by 2026-10-04 is not established.

sources.title: Guideline on the requirements for the chemical and pharmaceutical quality documentation concerning investigational medicinal products in clinical trials
sources.scope: Defines the structure and phase-appropriate content of the quality part of the IMPD for chemical IMPs, including placebo and modified comparators. Used here as the IMPD-Q content standard that MHRA and Swissmedic rely on. Predecessor: CHMP/QWP/185401/2004.
sources.uncertainty: The Rev. 2 adoption and effective dates are not verified. Also unconfirmed: whether MHRA applies Rev. 2 or the version in force on 2020-12-31, whether Swissmedic cites this exact revision, and the URL slug. Arsić 2026, 'Analysis of IMPD Deficiencies in the Clinical Trial Approval Process', Ther Innov Regul Sci, PMID 42754766 (abstract only), corroborates generally that specifications, stability data and manufacturing-control descriptions are the most frequently cited IMPD deficiencies. It does not confirm this guideline's identifier or dates. The EU-scope research should be the primary record; deduplicate by code.

sources.title: Guideline on the requirements for quality documentation concerning biological investigational medicinal products in clinical trials
sources.scope: Phase-appropriate quality IMPD content for biological IMPs. It covers characterisation, control of materials, process description, adventitious agents and viral safety, and comparability during development. It replaces Rev. 1.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified. The Rev. 2 date and URL slug are model knowledge. How MHRA and Swissmedic apply it is assumed from their general reliance on EU IMP quality guidelines. Deduplicate against the EU-scope research.

sources.title: EU Guidelines to Good Manufacturing Practice, Annex 13: Investigational Medicinal Products
sources.supersededBy: In the EU: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 and the Commission Guidelines on GMP for IMPs (C(2017) 8179), from 2022-01-31. It remains the IMP text in UK GMP for Great Britain and in the PIC/S GMP Guide.
sources.scope: GMP guidance specific to IMPs. It covers the product specification file, blinding and randomisation, packaging and labelling, QP certification, retention samples, comparators and returns. In the EU it was replaced from 2022-01-31 by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 and the Commission Guidelines on GMP for IMPs. It is still the IMP reference in UK GMP for Great Britain and in the PIC/S GMP Guide (Annex 13), which Switzerland applies.
sources.uncertainty: Status changed from 'final' to 'superseded' (for the EU), with supersededBy recorded; it remains applicable in GB and PIC/S contexts. Not re-verified: the reference number, the 2010 date (in operation 2010-07-31) and the EU supersession date are model knowledge. Whether MHRA has issued a UK-specific IMP GMP text, including under the 2025 regulations, is not established. The URL is the EudraLex Vol. 4 landing page.

sources.title: PIC/S Guide to Good Manufacturing Practice for Medicinal Products (incl. Annex 13)
sources.scope: The PIC/S GMP Guide that Swiss GMP law (MPLO) refers to, including Annex 13 on IMPs. Swissmedic and MHRA are both PIC/S participating authorities.
sources.uncertainty: Status changed from 'final' to 'unknown'. PE 009-17 (in force 2023-08-25) is model knowledge, and a later revision may be current as of 2026-10-04. How the MPLO refers to the PIC/S guide is not verified.

sources.title: ICH Members & Observers
sources.scope: ICH membership list. Swissmedic is a Standing Regulatory Member (an Observer before the 2015 ICH reform). MHRA is a Regulatory Member, admitted after Brexit (believed 2022). Both implement ICH Q-series guidelines.
sources.uncertainty: Not verified, because ich.org and database.ich.org are blocked and no retrieved article states either agency's ICH membership status or year. PMID 41248376 confirms only that MHRA is an IPRP member, which is not the same as ICH membership. Adoption date not established.

sources.title: Agreement on Mutual Recognition in relation to Conformity Assessment between the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Swiss Confederation
sources.scope: Carries over the EU–Switzerland MRA arrangements between the UK and Switzerland. This includes the medicinal-product GMP chapter: mutual recognition of GMP inspections and manufacturer's batch certification. Applied from 2021-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: Not verified: the signature date, the date it applied from, IMP coverage, later amendments, and an official URL.

sources.title: Agreement between the European Community and the Swiss Confederation on mutual recognition in relation to conformity assessment — Chapter 15: Medicinal products GMP inspection and batch certification
sources.scope: Mutual recognition of GMP inspections and manufacturer's batch certification between the EU and Switzerland (in force 2002-06-01). Batches certified on one side can be accepted on the other without re-testing.
sources.uncertainty: Not verified: the dates, IMP coverage, whether Chapter 15 is unaffected by the EU–CH institutional dispute, and an official URL.

sources.code: Access Consortium New Active Substance Work-Sharing Initiative (NASWSI)
sources.title: Access Consortium New Active Substance Work-Sharing Initiative
sources.scope: Work-sharing among the regulators of Australia, Canada, Singapore, Switzerland and the UK for the joint review of new active substance and new indication applications. It was founded in 2007 as ACSS by Australia, Canada, Singapore and Switzerland, and renamed Access when MHRA joined in October 2020. Work-sharing with MHRA began on 2021-01-01. Relevant to UK and Swiss MA quality dossiers prepared for joint assessment.
sources.uncertainty: NEW ENTRY added by the verifier. Membership and the initiative name are confirmed by Geraci et al. 2024, 'Industry Perceptions and Experiences with the Access Consortium New Active Substance Work-Sharing Initiative (NASWSI)', Ther Innov Regul Sci, PMID 38459358, PMC11043105. The 2007 founding, the October 2020 MHRA accession and the 2021-01-01 start rest on one source (PMID 41248376). No official URL or operating procedure was retrieved, so dossier rules (e.g. an identical Module 3 to all partners) are not verified.

sources.title: Federal Act on Medicinal Products and Medical Devices (Therapeutic Products Act, TPA; Heilmittelgesetz, HMG)
sources.scope: Swiss framework law. It requires marketing authorisation (Art. 9) and provides for temporary authorisation (introduced 2019). Swissmedic may take account of authorisations from countries with comparable control (Art. 13). It requires an establishment licence for manufacture (Art. 5), sets the clinical-trial provisions (Art. 53 ff.) and gives the pharmacopoeia its legal status. In force 2002-01-01; ordinary revision in force 2019-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: Two analyses confirm that Swissmedic's expedited routes include fast-track authorisation and temporary authorisation (the latter introduced in 2019): Hediger et al. 2026, JAMA Health Forum, PMID 42496993, PMC13401199; Hwang et al. 2022, JCO Oncol Pract, PMID 35731996, PMC9509186. Model knowledge only, not verified (fedlex.admin.ch is blocked): the article numbers (including Art. 9a for temporary authorisation), the dates and the ELI path. Not established: whether a later TPA amendment widening reliance on foreign approvals is in force by 2026-10.

sources.title: Federal Act on Research involving Human Beings (Human Research Act, HRA; Humanforschungsgesetz, HFG)
sources.scope: Swiss framework act for human research, including clinical trials. It provides for cantonal ethics committee authorisation and risk-based requirements. In force 2014-01-01 and implemented for clinical trials by ClinO.
sources.uncertainty: Cevallos et al. 2015, 'A pilot test of the new Swiss regulatory procedure for categorizing clinical trials by risk', Clin Trials, PMID 26122923, PMC4648234, confirms that the risk-based framework took effect in January 2014. The adoption date (2011-09-30) and ELI path are model knowledge.

sources.title: Ordinance on Clinical Trials in Human Research (Clinical Trials Ordinance, ClinO; KlinV) — original 2013 text
sources.supersededBy: ch-clino-sr-810-305 (revised ClinO, in force 2024-11-01; not verified)
sources.scope: The original ClinO text. It set risk categories A, B and C for trials of medicinal products, based on Swiss authorisation status and on whether the product is used as its product information specifies. It also set the Swissmedic authorisation procedure and the document lists for ethics committees and Swissmedic.
sources.uncertainty: PMID 26122923 confirms: A/B/C categories for drug trials, based on Swiss marketing-authorisation status and use within the product information; a draft ordinance consulted 2012-08-31 to 2012-10-31; application from January 2014. Not verified: the adoption date, the article and annex numbering (Art. 19; Annex 4), and the supersession date, which depends on the revision entering into force on 2024-11-01.

sources.title: Ordinance on Clinical Trials in Human Research (Clinical Trials Ordinance, ClinO; KlinV) — revised text
sources.scope: The current ClinO, revised by Federal Council decision (reported 2024-06-07) and in force 2024-11-01. It keeps the A/B/C risk categories (Swissmedic authorisation for B and C, alongside ethics committee approval) and sets the Swissmedic application documents, including IMP quality documentation and GMP evidence. It also governs substantial changes and adds transparency obligations, with closer alignment to EU CTR procedures.
sources.uncertainty: Three Swiss trial protocols show the framework in current use. A 2026 protocol is classified 'Category A under the Swiss Human Research Act and Clinical Trials Ordinance (ClinO)' with ethics-committee (BASEC) approval only (PMID 42082244, PMC13141127). Medicinal-product trials carry both BASEC and Swissmedic approval numbers (PMID 39578038, PMC11590791; PMID 40601599, PMC12221041). Not verified: the revision's adoption date (2024-06-07), its in-force date (2024-11-01), the content of the changes, and the post-revision article and annex numbering.

sources.title: Ordinance on Medicinal Products (Therapeutic Products Ordinance, TPO; Arzneimittelverordnung, VAM)
sources.scope: Implementing ordinance for marketing authorisation of medicinal products under the TPA. It covers authorisation procedures, fast-track, the procedure with prior notification, and variations. In force 2019-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified. The date and SR number are model knowledge, and no Fedlex ELI URL could be confirmed.

sources.title: Ordinance on Licensing in the Medicinal Products Sector (Medicinal Products Licensing Ordinance, MPLO; Arzneimittel-Bewilligungsverordnung, AMBV)
sources.scope: Covers establishment licences for manufacture, import and wholesale, and the responsible person (fachtechnisch verantwortliche Person). Its GMP rules refer to the PIC/S GMP Guide, including Annex 13 for IMPs. In force 2019-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: Not re-verified. The date, SR number, the way the annexes refer to PIC/S, and the IMP provisions are model knowledge. No URL could be confirmed.

sources.title: Ordinance of the Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products on the Requirements for the Marketing Authorisation of Medicinal Products (Arzneimittel-Zulassungsverordnung, AMZV)
sources.scope: Sets the content requirements for Swiss MA documentation, including the analytical, chemical and pharmaceutical (quality) documentation and the product information. Revised with effect from 2019-01-01.
sources.uncertainty: The English short name and abbreviation are not verified and are left out of the title. The researcher used 'TPLRO'; Swissmedic English texts may use 'TPLRO' or 'MPLRO', so cite as 'AMZV (SR 812.212.22)' until confirmed. The date, SR number and article/annex structure are model knowledge, and no URL could be confirmed.

sources.code: Swissmedic guidance on clinical trials with medicinal products (document identifier not verified)
sources.title: Clinical trials with medicinal products — Swissmedic authorisation requirements (guidance document / information pages)
sources.scope: Swissmedic guidance on applying for Category B and C trials. It covers the application form, protocol and IB, and IMP quality documentation: an IMPD written to the EU IMP quality guidelines, or Swiss product information for an unmodified authorised product. It also covers GMP evidence and substantial changes.
sources.uncertainty: Not verified, because swissmedic.ch is blocked: the identifier, exact title, version date and URL path. Content is inferred from model knowledge and may have been revised for the ClinO revision. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: Swissmedic guidance document — authorisation of human medicinal products with new active pharmaceutical ingredient (identifier not verified)
sources.title: Guidance document Authorisation of human medicinal product with new active pharmaceutical ingredient
sources.scope: Swissmedic requirements and procedure for new active substance MA applications. It covers dossier content, the standard procedure, and the expedited routes: fast-track, temporary authorisation and the procedure with prior notification.
sources.uncertainty: Fast-track and temporary-authorisation routes are confirmed by PMID 42496993 and PMID 35731996. PMID 41921119 (JCO Oncol Pract 2026) reports that Swissmedic completed 49% of priority (fast-track) cancer-drug reviews within the required period. Not verified: the identifier, title, version date and URL, and the 330-day standard and 140-day fast-track targets. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: Swissmedic guidance document — formal requirements (identifier not verified)
sources.title: Guidance document Formal requirements
sources.scope: Swissmedic's formal dossier requirements: CTD structure, the Swiss Module 1 (CH regional) and the accepted electronic formats (eCTD).
sources.uncertainty: Not verified: the identifier, the CH Module 1 specification version, whether eCTD is mandatory, any eCTD v4.0 timelines, and a URL. Adoption date not established.

sources.code: Swissmedic guidance document — authorisation under Art. 13 TPA (identifier not verified)
sources.title: Guidance document Authorisation of human medicinal products under Art. 13 TPA
sources.scope: Procedure in which Swissmedic takes into account a decision by an authority with comparable medicinal-product control. The dossier, including Module 3, must match the one approved abroad, and the foreign assessment reports must be supplied.
sources.uncertainty: Not verified: the identifier, title, date, the list of reference authorities, how strictly an identical Module 3 is required, and a URL. No retrieved literature describes the Art. 13 procedure specifically. Adoption date not established.

requirements.statement: File a Clinical Trial Application with Health Canada, and obtain authorization, before selling or importing a drug for a trial when the drug is not authorized for sale in Canada, or is a marketed drug used outside its authorized parameters (indication or clinical use, target population, route of administration or dosage regimen). This covers Phase I-III trials. No CTA is needed for a drug with a Notice of Compliance used within its authorized parameters (e.g., Phase IV), or for observational studies.

Health Canada reviews a complete CTA within 30 days of receipt. It issues either a No Objection Letter (NOL), after which the trial may proceed subject to REB approval, or a Not Satisfactory Notice (NSN), after which the trial may not proceed. Put the full quality package in the initial filing; quality deficiencies are resolved within the 30-day window or lead to an NSN.
CTA amendments (CTA-A), including quality amendments, also have a 30-day Health Canada review. Build that into the timing of chemistry and manufacturing changes that need an amendment.

Send pharmaceutical (chemical-entity) CTAs to the Pharmaceutical Drugs Directorate (PDD). Send CTAs for biologics, radiopharmaceuticals, and cell and gene therapies to the Biologic and Radiopharmaceutical Drugs Directorate (BRDD). The two directorates use different quality templates and guidance.

During review Health Canada typically sends clarification requests ('Clarifax'). A 2019 report says sponsors were expected to respond within 2 days, and that deficiencies left unresolved, or too serious, led to CTA withdrawal or an NSN. Keep CMC staff available to answer quality questions throughout the 30-day review.

requirements.modality: all (excluding the product types listed in the statement)
requirements.statement: Health Canada has an administrative, non-regulatory 7-day review target for comparative bioavailability trials and Phase I trials in healthy adult volunteers. It does not apply to Phase I trials of somatic cell therapies, xenografts, gene therapies, prophylactic vaccines or reproductive/genetic technologies. The 30-day default remains the legal requirement.

Organize the CTA in three modules. Module 1 is administrative and clinical: HC/SC 3011 form, IB, PSEAT-CTA synopsis, protocol, informed consent, Clinical Trial Site Information, REB and foreign refusals, and letters of access. Module 2 holds the quality summary (QOS). Module 3 holds the supporting quality information, cross-referenced from the QOS.
Include chemistry and manufacturing information for every drug in the trial that has no Canadian DIN or NOC, whether investigational product or unapproved comparator (reported as FDR C.05.005).

For chemical-entity CTAs, provide the Module 2.3 QOS on the phase-appropriate QOS-CE (CTA - Phase I, II or III) template, or as a QOS prepared to ICH M4Q. The level of detail should reflect what is known at that phase and let Health Canada assess the drug substance and drug product.

In the QOS-CE (CTA), the drug substance summary should cover: manufacturer(s) and manufacture (S.2); the specification, with justification of impurity acceptance criteria (S.4); and a stability summary (S.7.1) giving storage conditions and re-test period and confirming that stability data exist in the proposed container closure.

Full long-term stability data need not be available at filing. Provide preliminary data (e.g., accelerated) on representative batches and commit to monitoring clinical trial samples for the duration of the trial.

If batch analysis data for the clinical lot are not available at filing, submit representative batch results and commit to submitting the clinical-lot batch analysis before dosing. A representative batch analysis with a stated sampling rationale may replace a certificate of analysis for every batch.

Quality information may be cross-referenced to a previously authorized CTA of the same or a higher phase; a Phase III CTA cannot be fully cross-referenced to a Phase II CTA. Drug product batch analyses for Phase I/II CTAs cannot be cross-referenced. Third-party quality information may be cross-referenced with a letter of access. Health Canada may still require updated quality information when dose, combination, route, phase or population changes.

When confidential quality data sit in a Master File, the MF (with letter of access and fees) must be filed with and accepted by Health Canada before the CTA is filed. The letter of access must be signed by the MF holder and name the CTA sponsor and the trial exactly as on the application form.

For biologic CTAs, use the QOS-B in Module 2.3; radiopharmaceutical CTAs use a Quality Information Summary (template names reported as QIS-R and QIS-PER, unverified). An IMPD may be submitted instead of the QOS for CTAs and CTA-As. Early in development, Module 3 may not be needed if the summary is detailed enough.

Process validation and analytical method validation data are reportedly not required in biologic CTAs or CTA-As under the 2024 biotherapeutic CTD quality guidance. Safety-relevant controls, such as viral safety and sterility, should still be described.

For a quality amendment (CTA-A), describe each change, give the rationale and supporting data, and submit an updated QOS/QIS containing only the revised sections, with changes clearly identified. Later-phase CTAs should build on the earlier filing and flag what has changed.

Chemistry and manufacturing changes that do not need an amendment must still be notified to Health Canada (CTA-N); sources report a 15-day window after the change. Confirm the applicable Division 5 notification provision and timeline before relying on it.

The sponsor must ensure the trial drug is manufactured, handled and stored under the applicable GMP of Part C, Divisions 2-4, with specified exceptions (reported as FDR C.05.010). Apply GUI-0036 (Annex 13; reported revised edition 2026-02-04, unverified), including its sample retention, labelling and recall expectations. Each batch is certified by the person in charge of the quality control department.

Keep evidence that clinical trial drugs meet GMP: certificates of manufacture, certificates of analysis documenting identity, purity and strength, or approved lot release. Retain clinical trial records for the Division 5 retention period, reported as 15 years (FDR C.05.012).

Prepare cell-therapy CTAs under Health Canada's guidance 'Preparation of Clinical Trial Applications for use of Cell Therapy Products in Humans'. Address TSE risk for starting, ancillary and excipient materials. Early-phase process validation may be minimal but should cover safety-critical steps.

If the product is or contains a micro-organism or living organism within CEPA 1999 and the NSN Regulations (Organisms) - such as viral vectors (including non-replicating vectors) or oncolytic viruses, and possibly genetically modified cells - a New Substances Notification to ECCC may be needed alongside the CTA. As of 2019 the ECCC review had a 120-day statutory timeline that starts once the package is complete and runs independently of Health Canada's 30-day CTA review. Confirm current requirements with ECCC early.

Filing CTAs, CTA-As, CTA-Ns and Pre-CTA packages in eCTD is reportedly optional. Once a dossier is filed in eCTD, every later transaction for it must also be eCTD. CTSI and DSURs are out of scope for eCTD.

File under Part C, Division 5 and current guidance until replacement regulations come into force. Health Canada's modernization proposals include a proportional risk-based approach, single authorization of multi-arm trials, lifecycle terms and conditions, and decentralized-trial provisions. Reported but unverified: pre-publication in Canada Gazette I (2025-12-20), formal authorization letters, reviews of up to 60 days for complex trials, and final publication and coming into force projected for 2027 and 2028.

File NDS, SNDS, ANDS and SANDS in eCTD, reported as mandatory since 2018-01-01. Build the Canadian Module 1 to the Canadian Module 1 schema and place documents according to Health Canada's Module 1 organization table.

For synthetic or semi-synthetic drug substances and products, prepare Module 3 and the Module 2.3 QOS to Health Canada's NDS/ANDS Quality guidance (reported revision 2024-12-18), using the QOS-CE (NDS/ANDS) template. Complete a CPID-CE summarizing the final agreed quality data.

Show that every test batch used in studies supporting the submission was manufactured and controlled in a way representative of market production (reported as FDR C.08.002(2)(m); C.08.002.1(2)(d) for ANDS).

For biotherapeutic and blood products, prepare Module 3 to the merged CTD quality guidance (reported effective 2024-04-29). The Canadian QOS-B is recommended but not mandatory; a global QOS is acceptable but may prompt clarification requests.

Sources report that drug substance stability at NDS/ANDS filing should include long-term data at 25 °C ± 2 °C / 60% RH ± 5% RH: 12 months for a new drug substance and 6 months for an existing drug substance. Verify against the current NDS/ANDS Quality guidance before relying on this.

Health Canada has reportedly announced step-wise implementation of ICH Q12 and Q14. Initial Q12 scope is limited to PACMPs for BRDD-regulated products; Established Conditions and non-BRDD PACMPs are out of initial scope; Q14 is implemented without Established Conditions. The reported dates (notice 2026-01-12; PACMPs accepted from 2026-08-13 after a 90-day coming-into-effect period) are internally inconsistent. Confirm them with Health Canada before relying on them.
Validate analytical procedures to ICH Q2(R2), which ICH adopted at Step 4 on 2023-11-01. Health Canada's implementation date in place of Q2(R1) is reported as 2025-10-17 but is unverified.
Third-party confidential drug substance information may be supplied through a Master File. Health Canada reviews the restricted part only after receiving a letter of access signed by the MF holder.

'Unapproved' therapeutic goods may be supplied in an Australian clinical trial only under the TGA's Clinical Trial Notification (CTN) or Clinical Trial Approval (CTA) scheme. This covers any medicine, biological or device not on the ARTG, and ARTG goods used beyond their marketing conditions. The trial must also comply with the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 and Regulations, the National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research and GCP, and have HREC approval.

Under the CTN scheme, the TGA does not evaluate any data: quality, nonclinical or clinical. The approving HREC reviews the trial, including whether it has the expertise to assess product safety. The sponsor notifies the trial online and pays the fee; notifications are processed in about 5 days, and once notified and paid the trial can start, with HREC approval.

The trial sponsor is responsible for the quality of investigational products, including active comparators and placebo, and must ensure they are made under applicable GMP. The TGA reportedly cannot enforce GMP at overseas IMP manufacturers, so the sponsor must assure GMP compliance of overseas manufacture itself.

Under the CTA scheme, the sponsor applies to the TGA (CTA Part 1) with supporting data. The TGA evaluates the safety aspects of the product before the trial may start; the HREC reviews and approves the other aspects, including the protocol.

Submit the CTA data package as an electronic dossier of searchable PDFs. The TGA reportedly evaluates: quality (manufacturing process, process validation, proposed specifications, release and stability data, transport); adventitious-agent and microbiological safety or sterility; nonclinical safety; and available clinical data. The Part 1 form headings cover raw materials, facilities, manufacturing and packaging, in-process controls, stability and samples.

A CTA-scheme trial cannot start until written TGA approval, HREC approval and institutional approval are all in place. CTA Part 2 is reportedly due to the TGA within 28 days of starting each new trial or adding a site.

The CTA scheme is mandatory for trials of Class 4 biologicals, unless an earlier clinical trial has assessed the safety of the unapproved good, or a regulator with comparable requirements (e.g., FDA) has approved a trial for an equivalent indication. Otherwise the choice between CTN and CTA lies first with the sponsor and then with the approving HREC, depending on whether the HREC has the scientific and technical expertise to assess product safety.

Australian manufacture of goods for initial experimental studies in human volunteers (in practice, first-in-human trials) is reportedly exempt from TGA manufacturing licensing (Therapeutic Goods Regulations 1990, Schedule 7 item 1). GMP principles are still expected, and the TGA evaluates CTA applications on that basis.

Outside the first-in-human exemption, Australian manufacture of investigational medicines and biologicals reportedly needs a TGA manufacturing licence authorizing clinical-trial manufacture at that site. Inspection is against the PIC/S GMP Guide including Annex 13 (reported PE009-17 from 2025-09-01, with Annexes 4, 5 and 14 not adopted; unverified).

For biological IMPs under the CTA scheme, structure the quality documentation to the EMA guideline on quality documentation for biological IMPs in clinical trials, Revision 2, reported as TGA-adopted in round R01/2025 (unverified). It covers cell banks, process description and controls, raw materials, viral safety and stability.

For planning: the TGA's target timeframe for evaluating a CTA-scheme application, and a CTA amendment, is 50 days. CTN notifications are processed in about 5 days with no data evaluation. It was not confirmed whether the 50 days are working or calendar days, or how further-information requests affect the clock, so confirm the current timeframe and fee category with the TGA.
Prepare applications to register a prescription medicine in CTD format. Build the Australian Module 1 to the TGA 'CTD Module 1' guidance, and Module 2.3 and Module 3 to ICH M4Q as adopted by the TGA.

Submit prescription medicine applications, including master files, in eCTD; NeeS has reportedly not been accepted since 2023-05-01. Use the AU Module 1 eCTD specification (v3.2, reported published 2024-09) with ICH eCTD v3.2.2.

Quality data must meet the EU, ICH and other guidelines the TGA has adopted; check both the 'adopted' and 'not adopted' lists. Where an adopted EU guideline cites EU legislation, those legislative requirements reportedly do not apply in Australia.

Validate analytical procedures to ICH Q2(R2), which ICH adopted at Step 4 on 2023-11-01 and which is reported as TGA-adopted in R01/2025. ICH Q14 is reportedly not adopted in Australia: its references in Q2(R2) are general scientific principles, and enhanced-approach elements need sufficient justification and data.

Run stability studies under defined, controlled conditions; 'room temperature' or 'normal warehouse conditions' are reportedly unacceptable. To label a product 'Store below 30 °C', provide long-term data at 30 °C/65% RH. ICH Q1A(R2) is reported as adopted without TGA annotation.

Supply third-party drug substance information by DMF or EDQM CEP. With a CEP, reportedly: a complete copy in Module 3.2.R, a letter of access in Module 1.6.3, and certificates of analysis for at least three production-scale batches.

Each overseas manufacturing site needs a current TGA GMP clearance covering the relevant steps and dosage forms; Australian sites need a TGA manufacturing licence. The clearance must stay valid through evaluation.

Medicines and their ingredients must comply with the applicable default standards (BP, Ph. Eur. or USP-NF monographs) and any applicable Therapeutic Goods Orders, such as TGO 101 for tablets, capsules and pills.
Manufacture to the PIC/S Guide to GMP as adopted by the TGA, reported as PE009-17 from 2025-09-01 excluding Annexes 4, 5 and 14, with phased assessment against revised Annex 1 (unverified).

CDE decides on a clinical trial application within 60 working days of acceptance. If the sponsor receives no objection or questions in that time, the trial is deemed approved and may proceed on the submitted protocol. Plan the IND clock in working days, not calendar days.

Registration time limits under the 2020 Provisions for Drug Registration are counted in working days. Examples: 60 working days for clinical trial applications, 200 for standard marketing-application review, 130 for priority review. Plan CMC deficiency-response and clock-stop windows in working days.

Clinical trial applications for chemical drugs and for therapeutic or preventive biologics follow the ICH M4 CTD structure, with content suited to the development stage. That means a China-regional Module 1, a Quality Overall Summary in 2.3, and quality data in Module 3 (3.2.S/3.2.P).

ICH M4 (CTD) has applied in China since 2018-02-01 to defined new-drug categories: chemical category 1 and 5.1, and therapeutic and preventive biologics category 1. It became the general dossier structure for chemical and biological registration applications from 2020-07-01.

China introduced CTD-format pharmaceutical (Module 3-equivalent) dossiers for chemical drugs in 2010. CTD-format pharmaceutical data was required for the new chemical drug categories in 2016, and the 2020 chemical drug dossier requirements superseded this. Cite the 2020 requirements for current submissions.

A Phase I application gives drug substance information: basic information, manufacturer(s), a manufacturing process description, characterization (structure, impurities), quality control (specification, analytical methods, batch analyses) and stability data.

A Phase I application gives drug product information: dosage form and composition (including any placebo), manufacturer(s), a manufacturing process description, quality control (specification, analytical methods, batch analyses) and stability data covering use during the planned trial.

Phase I CMC information should focus on factors that affect subject safety, such as the impurity profile, sterility and endotoxin control for parenterals, and stability over the trial period. Present these explicitly in 2.3 and Module 3.

Before pivotal Phase III, innovative chemical drug sponsors are expected to provide expanded CMC information under CDE's Phase III pharmaceutical research information guide: process and controls, specification justification, impurities and stability. The guide's identifier and current status are unverified; confirm on cde.org.cn before citing.

During a clinical trial, the sponsor assesses each pharmaceutical (CMC) change for its effect on subject safety, following CDE technical guidelines. A change judged not to affect safety may be implemented and reported in the DSUR. A change that may increase subject risk needs a supplementary application (补充申请) before implementation.
CDE decides a supplementary application for a change during a clinical trial within 60 working days of acceptance. If CDE does not notify the sponsor in that time, the change is deemed approved.

Sponsors submit a development safety update report (研发期间安全性更新报告, DSUR) to CDE annually during the clinical trial. The DSUR is also the vehicle for reporting CMC changes that do not need a supplementary application.
Clinical trial approval lapses if no subject has signed informed consent within 3 years of approval. CMC information may then have to be resubmitted in a new application.

Sponsors can request communication meetings with CDE at key milestones: pre-IND, end of Phase II / pre-Phase III, and pre-NDA. Use the pre-IND meeting for phase-appropriate CMC questions such as specifications, starting materials, or comparability between toxicology and clinical batches.

Manufacturers of chemical APIs, pharmaceutical excipients and direct-contact packaging materials or containers register product information and data on the CDE registration platform. CDE reviews them together with the drug product application (关联审评审批). The drug product application cites the platform registration number with the supplier's authorization.

The CDE platform shows a public status for each registered API, excipient or packaging material, recollected as 'A' (associated with an approved product, or independently approved for an API) and 'I' (otherwise). Check the supplier's status when selecting suppliers and planning the marketing application; the status convention itself is unverified.

Excipients and direct-contact packaging materials are no longer approved separately in China. They are reviewed with the drug product application that uses them, and the drug product MAH is responsible for their suitability and supplier quality.

A chemical API may be reviewed and approved with a drug product or on its own. Approval issues an API approval notice with an approved standard and manufacturing process, and changes the API's platform status to 'A'.

The Chinese Pharmacopoeia is a statutory technical standard that must be applied in drug development, production, use and regulation in China. Apply ChP monographs and general chapters (or justify alternatives) in drug substance, drug product and excipient specifications. The rule that registered standards may not be lower than the ChP comes from the Drug Standards Measures and is unverified here.

ChP 2025 has replaced ChP 2020 and is the edition in force. Current dossiers should cite ChP 2025 monographs and general chapters, including the revised bacterial endotoxin test chapter. The 2025-10-01 effective date and the transition rules for approved products are unverified; confirm them from the NMPA/NHC implementation announcement.

ChP general chapters implement ICH quality guidance: 9001 stability (ICH Q1A), 9101 analytical method validation (ICH Q2), 9102 impurities (ICH Q3A/Q3B thresholds), 0861 residual solvents (ICH Q3C) and 9306 genotoxic impurities (ICH M7). Cite the ChP chapter alongside the ICH guideline in the relevant Module 3 sections. Chapter numbers are confirmed for ChP 2020; check them in ChP 2025.

Design stability studies to ChP general chapter 9001 (stability testing of drug substances and preparations, aligned with ICH Q1A) and the CDE chemical drug stability guideline. Provide long-term, accelerated and stress/photostability data, plus post-approval stability commitments.

Since 2022-07-01, investigational drugs for clinical trials in China (test articles, comparators and placebos) must be prepared under China GMP and its Clinical Trial Drug Annex. This covers preparation, packaging, labelling and blinding.

The Clinical Trial Drug Annex requires a quality system for investigational drugs: product documentation, batch records, QC testing, retention samples, and documented release before supply to trial sites. The sponsor remains responsible for release, shipment, recall, return and destruction.

Under the 2020 GCP, the sponsor supplies investigational products made under GMP, suitably packaged and labelled (including blinding), with defined storage and transport conditions and accountability records.
Commercial manufacture must comply with China GMP (2010 revision) and its annexes, under a manufacturing licence issued under the 2020 Drug Manufacturing Supervision Measures.

Under the 2019 Drug Administration Law, the marketing authorization holder holds the authorization separately from manufacturing and is responsible for drug quality and risk control across the lifecycle, including when manufacturing is contracted out. Specific supplier-oversight duties for API, excipient and packaging suppliers (NMPA 2019 No. 56) are unverified.

Marketing applications undergo registration testing (注册检验): NIFDC or a provincial drug control institute tests samples and reviews the proposed quality standard. Testing may start before the application is accepted.

The 2020 Provisions provide for risk-based on-site inspection of development and manufacturing sites in parallel with technical review. Batch records and data in Module 3 must be traceable to site records. Coordination with the pre-approval GMP compliance inspection is unverified.

At marketing approval, NMPA approves the quality standard and manufacturing process together with the label and package insert. These approved documents become the registered baseline for post-approval change control.

The standard review time limit for a marketing application is 200 working days, and 130 working days under priority review. Urgently needed rare-disease drugs already marketed overseas are reported to have a 70-working-day limit (single source). Published analyses show actual median review times often exceed these limits.
Chemical drug and biologic marketing applications contain a complete ICH M4Q Module 3 and a Quality Overall Summary (2.3), together with the China-regional Module 1.
Dossiers are submitted in Chinese. Foreign-language source documents need Chinese translations, and the Module 1 administrative documents and drug information must be in Chinese.

NMPA has been an ICH Regulatory Member since 2017 and has implemented most ICH guidelines, and the ChP general chapters are being harmonized with ICH Q-series and Q4B texts. Do not assume a particular Q guideline is in force in China: check NMPA's implementation status for that guideline in the ICH implementation tables before citing it.

NMPA accepts eCTD submissions built to its eCTD technical specification and CN regional Module 1 backbone, for a defined scope of applications introduced in 2021. Confirm the current eCTD scope, and any mandatory requirement, with CDE before choosing a submission format.

Post-approval CMC changes are classed as major (prior-approval supplementary application), moderate (filing with NMPA or the provincial authority) or minor (annual report). Classify them using the post-approval change measures and the CDE pharmaceutical change guidelines; major changes to biologics need a comparability exercise.

Every vaccine lot must pass lot release (批签发) before sale or import: lot-by-lot examination of the lot-release documents plus NIFDC (or designated institute) sample testing, with test items and frequency adjusted by risk. Lot-release documents must reflect production and testing data, including deviations. Lot release for other biologics such as blood products comes from the 2020 lot-release measures and is unverified here.

For cell therapy products, a July 2025 CDE draft guideline proposes a three-tier risk classification of CMC changes, with comparability expectations benchmarked to ICH Q5E. Check whether it has been finalized before relying on it.

In an EU/EEA CTA, present IMPD quality data in a logical structure such as ICH CTD Module 3. Keep the IMPD concise, preferably as tables with a brief narrative of the salient points, and preface each section with a detailed table of contents and a glossary (CTR Annex I, points 38-40).

The IMPD must cover the quality, manufacture and control of each IMP, plus non-clinical and clinical data.
