Where the sponsor and the IMP manufacturer are different entities, Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 requires a technical agreement between them. Its exact required content, such as sharing inspection reports and quality information, should be checked against the verbatim text.

A CTIMP in the UK needs a clinical trial authorisation from MHRA and a favourable Research Ethics Committee opinion before it starts. Make the application once, through IRAS, as a combined review sent to both MHRA and the HRA/REC. The 2025 amending regulations codify combined review in law.

Support each IMP in the CTA with quality data: a full IMPD quality section, or a simplified IMPD where the quality data have already been assessed. For a UK-authorised product used unmodified in the trial, the SmPC can replace the quality part of the IMPD.

Structure the quality IMPD with CTD-style headings: 2.1.S drug substance, 2.1.P investigational medicinal product, and 2.1.A appendices (facilities and equipment, adventitious agents safety evaluation, novel excipients, solvents for reconstitution and diluents).

Give quality data for the placebo: composition, manufacture, release specification, and evidence that it matches the active IMP. For a comparator modified for the trial (e.g. over-encapsulated), show that performance is unchanged (e.g. comparative dissolution) and provide stability data.

At phase 1, specifications may be provisional, with limits justified by batch data and safety. Confirm that the analytical methods are suitable and tabulate their validation parameters and acceptance limits; full validation reports are not normally expected. Give batch analyses for the nonclinical and clinical batches, and relate the clinical impurity profile to the toxicology batches.

IMPD stability data must support the proposed shelf life or retest period for the length of the trial. A stability protocol plus a commitment to extend shelf life on ongoing real-time data may be used.

For biological IMPs, include characterisation, a process description with control of materials, and an adventitious agents and viral safety evaluation, with viral clearance data scaled to the development phase.

After authorisation, submit to MHRA any change to IMP quality data likely to affect participant safety or the trial's scientific value (e.g. new manufacturing site, changed specifications). These are substantial amendments under the 2004 text and modifications under the 2025 amending regulations. Get approval before implementing them.

The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 amend SI 2004/1031 and take full effect on 2026-04-28. They codify combined review, add risk-proportionate routes for lower-risk trials and modifications, and require trial registration and results publication. Check current MHRA guidance for transitional arrangements for trials authorised under the earlier text.

IMP labels must carry the particulars required by the UK clinical trials regulations and UK GMP (Annex 13). Check current MHRA labelling guidance before finalising label text: the 2025 amending regulations are reported to revise IMP labelling provisions, but this is not verified.

Plan IMPD questions and responses around MHRA's statutory clock. Under the 2004 text, MHRA gives its first review within 30 days, the sponsor must answer grounds for non-acceptance within 14 days, MHRA decides within 60 days, and substantial amendments are decided within 35 days. The 2025 amending regulations let the sponsor extend the reply to a request for information from 14 to up to 60 days.

Since October 2023, lower-risk phase 3 and 4 trials that meet MHRA's notification criteria have been notified rather than fully assessed; a trial that does not meet the criteria is assessed in full. The 2025 amending regulations make notifiable lower-risk trials a statutory route. Check eligibility against MHRA's current criteria.

Manufacturing, assembling or importing IMPs in the UK requires a manufacturing authorisation for IMPs (MIA(IMP)), unless a statutory exemption applies (e.g. assembly in a hospital or health centre by or under a pharmacist for trial use there).
A Qualified Person named on the MIA(IMP) must certify each IMP batch before it is released for use in the trial.

Manufacture IMPs to UK GMP, including the IMP guidance in Annex 13 (product specification file, blinding and randomisation controls, labelling, retention samples). Annex 13 remains part of UK GMP although the EU replaced it on 2022-01-31.

IMPs from countries on MHRA's approved list (EU/EEA) must be imported into Great Britain by a UK MIA(IMP) holder whose QP has a system to verify that each batch was QP-certified in the approved country. GB re-certification of the batch is not required.
IMPs imported from countries not on the approved list must be QP-certified in the UK, with the QP confirming that manufacture met GMP standards at least equivalent to UK GMP.

A UK marketing authorisation application must contain quality data in CTD Module 3 (ICH M4Q structure) and a Module 2.3 Quality Overall Summary, with the UK Module 1, submitted electronically to MHRA.
Module 1 must include a Qualified Person declaration that the active substance is manufactured in accordance with GMP.

Active substance information can be supplied in full in 3.2.S, by an EDQM Certificate of Suitability (CEP), or by an Active Substance Master File lodged with MHRA under the UK ASMF procedure, with the applicant's part given to the MA applicant.

Substances and products with a British Pharmacopoeia or European Pharmacopoeia monograph must comply with it. BP monographs are legally binding in the UK; cite the edition in effect (BP 2026 from 2026-01-01).
Write UK quality dossiers to ICH quality guidelines and to the EU scientific guidelines in force on 2020-12-31, which continue to apply in the UK unless MHRA has said otherwise.
Full-dossier national applications can be assessed under MHRA's 150-day route (excluding clock-stops), which expects a complete, high-quality Module 3 at submission.

The International Recognition Procedure, in place since 2024-01-01, lets MHRA take into account an approval by one of seven reference regulators: TGA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, HSA, PMDA, FDA, and EMA or EU/EEA member-state authorities. Recognition A requires the reference approval to be within the preceding 2 years, Recognition B within the preceding 10 years. MHRA can still refuse an application if the evidence is insufficient. The IRP replaced the EC Decision Reliance Procedure and the MRDC reliance procedure.

For an IRP application, submit evidence of the reference regulator's approval, including its assessment reports. The UK product and Module 3 are expected to match what the reference regulator approved (sites, process, specifications, shelf life). Declare and justify any differences, which can move the application from Recognition A to B.

A QP named on a UK manufacturer's licence must certify each batch released to the GB market. Whether batch testing done in approved countries (EU/EEA) is accepted depends on MHRA's current approved-country policy; confirm it before relying on it.

Under ClinO, Swiss clinical trials of medicinal products fall into risk categories A, B or C, set by whether the product is authorised in Switzerland and whether it is used as its product information specifies. Category A: authorised and used per the product information. Category B: authorised but used otherwise, subject to ClinO's exceptions. Category C: not authorised in Switzerland. The category determines the approval route and documentation.
Category B and C trials of medicinal products need Swissmedic authorisation as well as cantonal ethics committee approval. Category A trials need ethics committee approval only.
Submit to the competent cantonal ethics committee through BASEC and, for Category B and C trials, to Swissmedic. The two submissions can be made in parallel.

For Category B and C trials, the Swissmedic application must include IMP quality documentation (an IMPD quality section, or Swiss product information where the authorised product is used unmodified) and evidence of GMP-compliant manufacture, as ClinO's Swissmedic document annex lists.

Swissmedic accepts IMP quality documentation written to the EU IMP quality guidelines, so an IMPD-Q prepared for an EU or UK CTA can generally be reused. Swiss-specific items go in the application form and cover documents.
Submit substantial changes to IMP quality documentation during the trial to Swissmedic, and get authorisation before implementing them.
The revised ClinO, in force 2024-11-01, governs applications from that date and replaced the 2014 text. Check its transitional provisions for trials authorised under the earlier version.
Manufacturing IMPs in Switzerland requires a Swissmedic manufacturing licence. IMPs must be produced to GMP as the MPLO sets out; the MPLO refers to the PIC/S GMP Guide, including Annex 13 on IMPs.

Batches made in Switzerland are released by the licence holder's responsible person (fachtechnisch verantwortliche Person). For IMPs made abroad, the sponsor must document GMP-compliant manufacture and release, e.g. with the manufacturing authorisation or GMP certificate and the QP certification.

GMP inspections and manufacturer batch certification are mutually recognised between Switzerland and the EU (MRA Chapter 15) and between Switzerland and the UK (2019 MRA). Confirm each agreement's scope, including whether IMPs are covered, before relying on a foreign QP certification without re-testing.

Swiss marketing authorisation applications use the CTD format: quality data in Module 3 (ICH M4Q) and Module 2.3, with the Swiss Module 1. Swissmedic's formal-requirements guidance sets the accepted electronic format (eCTD).

The analytical, chemical and pharmaceutical documentation must meet AMZV (SR 812.212.22) requirements and the current state of science. Swissmedic applies the latter through the ICH quality guidelines it implements as an ICH member.

Products and substances must comply with the European Pharmacopoeia and the Swiss Pharmacopoeia (Ph. Helv.), both legally binding in Switzerland. Reference the applicable monographs in the specifications.
Document the GMP status of every manufacturing site in the Swiss Module 1: Swissmedic licences, or foreign authority GMP certificates and MRA evidence.

Under Art. 13 TPA, Swissmedic takes into account the assessment of a product already authorised by an authority with comparable control. The dossier, including Module 3, must match the version that authority approved, and the foreign assessment reports must be provided.

New active substance applications follow Swissmedic's NAS authorisation guidance. The expedited routes (fast-track; temporary authorisation, introduced 2019; procedure with prior notification) shorten or front-load review but do not reduce what Module 3 must contain.
Swissmedic is one of the seven reference regulators under MHRA's International Recognition Procedure, so a Swiss approval and its approved Module 3 can support a UK IRP application.

MHRA and Swissmedic are both members of the Access Consortium, with TGA, Health Canada and HSA, which work-shares the assessment of new active substance and new indication applications. Both are also Project Orbis partners for concurrent oncology review.

pathways.applicationName: CTA - Clinical Trial Application (with CTA-A amendments and CTA-N notifications)
pathways.legalBasis: Food and Drugs Act; Food and Drug Regulations Part C, Division 5, corroborated as the governing regulation for drug and biologic trials (PMID 40303377). Section mapping reported by the researcher, not re-verified: C.05.005 (application content, including chemistry and manufacturing information for drugs without a DIN or NOC), C.05.006 (30-day default authorization), C.05.008 and related sections (amendments and notifications), C.05.010 (sponsor obligations including GMP), C.05.012 (records). Proposed Clinical Trials Regulations (reported Canada Gazette I, 2025-12-20; not re-verified) would replace Division 5.
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Reported (not re-verified): a CTD-style CTA in three modules. Module 1 is Canadian administrative and clinical: HC/SC 3011, IB, PSEAT-CTA, protocol, ICF, CTSI, letters of access. Module 2.3 is the QOS: for chemical entities, the phase-specific QOS-CE (CTA - Phase I/II/III; CTA-BA) or an ICH M4Q QOS; for biologics, QOS-B; for radiopharmaceuticals, a Quality Information Summary; an IMPD reportedly accepted in place of the QOS for biologic CTAs. Module 3 holds supporting quality data. eCTD is optional for CTAs, but once used it is required for all later transactions on that dossier.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Corroborated: a CTA is required for clinical and quality review of Phase I-III trials. Reported but not re-verified: quality detail should reflect what is known at each phase, with separate Phase I, II and III QOS-CE templates. Preliminary stability data plus a commitment to monitor clinical lots, and representative batch analyses with a commitment to provide clinical-lot data before dosing, are acceptable. Cross-referencing is allowed only to authorized CTAs of the same or a higher phase. Process and method validation are not required for biologic CTAs. Updated quality data may be required for changes in dose, route, combination, phase or population.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Reported, not re-verified: the sponsor must ensure manufacture, handling and storage under the applicable GMP of Part C, Divisions 2-4 (C.05.010). GUI-0036 (Annex 13; revised edition reported dated 2026-02-04, unverified) covers sample retention, labelling, recall, and batch certification by the person in charge of the quality control department. The sponsor keeps GMP evidence such as certificates of manufacture, certificates of analysis and lot release.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Corroborated (PMIDs 40303377, 30984761): review by PDD for pharmaceuticals or BRDD for biologics, radiopharmaceuticals and cell and gene therapies; 30-day review of CTAs and CTA-As from receipt of a complete application; No Objection Letter or Not Satisfactory Notice; clarification requests ('Clarifax'), with a 2-day response expectation reported in 2019; possible parallel CEPA/NSNR(O) notification to ECCC for viral vectors and oncolytic viruses, with a 120-day statutory review as of 2019. Reported but not re-verified: PSEAT-CTA synopsis; Master Files filed and accepted before the CTA, with a letter of access naming the sponsor and trial; a 7-day administrative target for comparative BA and Phase I healthy-volunteer trials, excluding cell and gene therapies, xenografts and prophylactic vaccines; a 2026-09-14 interim policy on REB, qualified-investigator and consent processes, with no CMC changes found.
pathways.language: English or French (Canada's official languages); not verified in either the research or the verification pass.

pathways.applicationName: NDS / ANDS (New Drug Submission / Abbreviated New Drug Submission), including SNDS/SANDS
pathways.legalBasis: Food and Drugs Act; Food and Drug Regulations Part C, Division 8 (reported C.08.002, including C.08.002(2)(m), and C.08.002.1), as amended by the Agile Licensing regulations (reported SOR/2024-238). Not re-verified.
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Reported, not re-verified: eCTD mandatory since 2018-01-01, with a Canadian Module 1 built to the Canadian Module 1 schema and the Module 1 document-placement table. Module 2.3 QOS uses QOS-CE (NDS/ANDS) for chemical entities or QOS-B (recommended) for biologics. Module 3 follows ICH M4Q and the Health Canada NDS/ANDS Quality guidance (reported revision 2024-12-18) or the biotherapeutic and blood products CTD quality guidance (reported 2024-04-29). A CPID-CE summarizes the final agreed quality data for chemical entities.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Full commercial-stage Module 3, with test batches representative of market production. Stability follows ICH Q1A(R2) as applied by Health Canada; the 25 °C/60% RH long-term condition and the 12-month/6-month data expectations were not confirmed.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to the marketing application itself. Commercial manufacture is subject to Part C Division 2 GMP and establishment licensing, which were not reviewed in this scope.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Reported, not re-verified: Canadian Module 1, with transactions rejected if the placement table is not followed; CPID-CE; Master Files with letters of access. ICH Q2(R2) was adopted by ICH on 2023-11-01 (corroborated); Health Canada's reported implementation date of 2025-10-17 is unverified. An ICH Q12/Q14 notice reported dated 2026-01-12 limits initial Q12 scope to BRDD PACMPs, with Q14 implemented without Established Conditions; its PACMP acceptance date (2026-08-13) is internally inconsistent with the notice date and is unverified.
pathways.language: English or French; not verified.

pathways.applicationName: CTN - Clinical Trial Notification scheme
pathways.legalBasis: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 and Therapeutic Goods Regulations 1990; the TGA administers the CTN scheme under this legislation (corroborated, PMIDs 40303377 and 40007583). Provision mapping reported by the researcher, not re-verified: Act ss18/19 for medicines and s32CK for biologicals; Regulations Schedule 5A item 3 (CTN).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: No quality dossier is submitted to or evaluated by the TGA (corroborated, PMID 40303377). The HREC reviews the trial and decides whether it has the expertise to assess product safety, and may require the CTA scheme instead. The route by which product quality information reaches the HREC (e.g., the Investigator's Brochure) was not verified.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Any phase may use CTN when the HREC has the scientific and technical expertise to assess product safety and the product is not subject to mandatory CTA. Class 4 biologicals must use CTA unless an earlier clinical trial has assessed the safety of the unapproved good, or a comparable regulator (e.g., FDA) has approved a trial for an equivalent indication (PMID 40303377).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Reported, not re-verified: the sponsor is responsible for IMP quality and for manufacture under applicable GMP, including comparators and placebo, and must assure GMP at overseas manufacturers. Australian manufacture for first-in-human studies is exempt from licensing (Regulations Schedule 7 item 1), but GMP principles are expected. Other Australian IMP manufacture needs a TGA licence and is inspected against PIC/S GMP including Annex 13 (reported PE009-17 from 2025-09-01).
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Corroborated (PMID 40303377): online notification with a fee, processed in about 5 days; the trial may start once notified and paid, with HREC approval; the TGA inspects clinical trial sites; a National One Stop Shop is under development (also PMID 40007583). Reported, not re-verified: CTN form user guide v1.4 (May 2024). GMO products also need separate gene-technology (OGTR) authorization under the Gene Technology Act 2000; this rests on literature only (PMIDs 32129035, 34222122), with no official source retrieved.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: CTA - Clinical Trial Approval scheme (formerly CTX)
pathways.legalBasis: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 and Therapeutic Goods Regulations 1990 (corroborated as the governing legislation). Reported, not re-verified: approval to supply unapproved goods in a clinical trial (s19(1)(b); s32CK for biologicals) and Regulations 12AA-12AD (conditions, including GCP).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Corroborated: an application to the TGA with supporting data; the TGA evaluates the safety aspects of the product (PMID 40303377). Reported, not re-verified: CTA Part 1 form plus an electronic dossier of searchable PDFs with drug substance and drug product quality data (raw materials, facility, manufacturing and packaging, in-process controls, specifications, release and stability, transport, adventitious agents and sterility). Biological IMPs are reported to follow the TGA-adopted EMA biological IMP quality guideline (Rev. 2). The form does not mandate a CTD layout. CTA Part 2 is due within 28 days of starting each trial or adding a site.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: The TGA evaluates safety aspects before the trial starts, with a 50-day target timeframe for applications and amendments (PMID 40303377; working versus calendar days unconfirmed). The scheme is mandatory for Class 4 biologicals unless an earlier trial assessed safety or a comparable regulator approved a trial for an equivalent indication. It is otherwise used when the HREC lacks the expertise to assess product safety.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: As for CTN; reported, not re-verified. The Schedule 7 item 1 licensing exemption covers first-in-human manufacture, with GMP principles expected and evaluated. Other Australian IMP manufacture needs a TGA licence and is inspected to PIC/S GMP including Annex 13. The sponsor assures overseas GMP.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: The HREC reviews and approves the protocol and other aspects (corroborated). TGA approval, HREC approval and institutional approval are all reportedly required before the trial starts. A TGA review of the CTA scheme (HREC consultation May 2024) is ongoing, with its outcome unknown. ICH Q14 is reportedly not adopted in Australia.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: Registration of a prescription medicine on the ARTG (e.g., new chemical entity, new biological entity, biosimilar)
pathways.legalBasis: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989. Reported, not re-verified: s23 (registration), s9D (variations), ss25(1)(g) and 26A(3) (overseas manufacture evidence), s3 (default standards), and the Therapeutic Goods (Manufacturing Principles) Determination adopting PIC/S PE009-17.
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Reported, not re-verified: eCTD only since 2023-05-01, using the AU Module 1 specification (v3.2, published 2024-09) with ICH eCTD v3.2.2. The Australian Module 1 follows the TGA 'CTD Module 1' guidance; Module 2.3 and Module 3 follow ICH M4Q as adopted by the TGA.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Full commercial Module 3 to the TGA-adopted EU/ICH guidelines. Reported, not re-verified: ICH Q2(R2) adopted and ICH Q14 not adopted; ICH Q1A(R2) adopted without annotation; long-term stability at 30 °C/65% RH for 'Store below 30 °C' labelling.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable. For commercial supply, Australian sites need a TGA licence and overseas sites a TGA GMP clearance (MRA, PIC/S, US FDA or compliance-verification evidence) valid through evaluation, against PIC/S GMP (reported PE009-17, Annexes 4, 5 and 14 not adopted). Not re-verified.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Reported, not re-verified: DMF or CEP routes for third-party APIs (CEP copy in 3.2.R, letter of access in 1.6.3, CoAs for three production batches); default standards (BP, Ph. Eur., USP-NF) and TGOs (e.g., TGO 101); annotated adoption of EU/ICH guidelines with a separate list of guidelines not adopted.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: Drug Clinical Trial Application (药物临床试验申请; called 'IND' in CDE usage)
pathways.legalBasis: Drug Administration Law, 2019 revision (in force 2019-12-01): 60-working-day silent approval and communication mechanisms. Provisions for Drug Registration, SAMR Order No. 27 (promulgated 2020-01-22, in force 2020-07-01). NMPA 2020 No. 44 (chemical) and No. 43 (biologics) dossier requirements (identifiers unverified). GCP 2020 (identifier unverified).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: ICH M4 CTD structure with stage-appropriate content: China-regional Module 1 (administrative documents and drug information, in Chinese), Module 2.3 Quality Overall Summary, and Module 3 (3.2.S/3.2.P, plus 3.2.A/3.2.R for biologics). For first-in-human applications, CDE's Phase I application technical guide (新药I期临床试验申请技术指南) sets the expected pharmaceutical information (identifier unverified). eCTD has been accepted for a defined scope since 2021; current scope unverified.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Phase I: CMC content focused on subject safety (impurity profile, sterility and endotoxin for parenterals, stability over the trial). Phase III (innovative chemical drugs): expanded CMC per CDE's Phase III pharmaceutical research information guide (identifier and status unverified). During the trial, each CMC change is assessed for safety impact. Changes with no safety impact are implemented and reported in the annual DSUR. Changes that may add risk need a supplementary application (60-working-day implied approval; unverified). Approval lapses if no subject consents within 3 years (unverified). Cell therapy: CDE July 2025 draft on CMC changes (three-tier risk classes); finalization not established.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: China GMP (2010 revision) plus the GMP Annex for Clinical Trial Drugs (recollected as NMPA 2022 No. 43, effective 2022-07-01; unverified), covering test articles, comparators and placebos: preparation, blinding, labelling, retention samples, release, distribution and returns. GCP 2020 places investigational product obligations on the sponsor. China has no EU-style QP declaration; release follows the Annex's documented release procedure (clause detail unverified). For CGT, data from investigator-initiated trials run outside the NMPA IND track may need bridging, because the product may not have been made under GMP (single secondary source).
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Associated review (关联审评): suppliers may register APIs, excipients and direct-contact packaging on the CDE platform (status flags recollected as A/I), and the sponsor cites them by registration number with a letter of authorization. Whether a clinical trial application may instead carry these data directly is NOT established; confirm with CDE. ChP 2025 is the pharmacopoeia in force (effective date reported as 2025-10-01, unverified). ChP general chapters 9001/9101/9102/0861/9306 implement ICH Q1A/Q2/Q3A-B/Q3C/M7. Communication meetings are available at pre-IND, end of Phase II / pre-Phase III and pre-NDA. Dossier in Chinese, with translations of foreign source documents.
pathways.language: Simplified Chinese (foreign-language source documents with Chinese translation; unverified)

pathways.applicationName: Drug Marketing Authorization Application (药品上市许可申请; NDA/BLA equivalent)
pathways.legalBasis: Drug Administration Law, 2019 revision (in force 2019-12-01): nationwide MAH system. Recollected but unverified: review of APIs with the drug product, joint review of excipients and packaging, and approval of the quality standard, process and labelling. Provisions for Drug Registration, SAMR Order No. 27 (in force 2020-07-01): marketing authorization, associated review, registration testing, risk-based on-site inspection in parallel with review, expedited pathways. NMPA 2020 No. 44 / No. 43 dossier requirements (unverified). Drug Manufacturing Supervision Measures, SAMR Order No. 28 (unverified).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Full ICH M4Q CTD: China-regional Module 1, Module 2.3 QOS, and complete Module 3 (3.2.S, 3.2.P, 3.2.A, 3.2.R). eCTD per the NMPA eCTD specification for the scope introduced in 2021; current mandatory scope unverified.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Not phase-based: a complete commercial-stage quality dossier is required. Standard review limit is 200 working days; priority review 130 working days; urgently needed rare-disease drugs already marketed overseas reportedly 70 working days (single source). Actual median times often exceed the limits. Post-approval CMC changes follow the major/moderate/minor classes of the 2021 post-approval change measures (unverified).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to investigational product. Commercial manufacture is under China GMP (2010 revision) and its annexes. The 2020 Provisions provide risk-based on-site inspection of development and manufacturing sites in parallel with technical review; coordination with the pre-approval GMP compliance inspection is unverified.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Registration testing (注册检验) of samples and the quality standard by NIFDC or a provincial institute; may start before acceptance (unverified). APIs, excipients and packaging on the CDE associated-review platform with letters of authorization (unverified). The approved quality standard and manufacturing process are issued with the approval and form the registered baseline (unverified). Specifications must comply with ChP 2025, the edition in force. Every vaccine lot needs lot release under the Vaccine Administration Law (passed 2019-06-29, in force 2019-12-01). Lot release for other biologics under SAMR Order No. 33 is unverified. The MAH is responsible for quality across the lifecycle.
pathways.language: Simplified Chinese (foreign-language source documents with Chinese translation; unverified)

pathways.applicationName: CTA under EU CTR (Regulation (EU) No 536/2014) via CTIS - IMPD quality part (full IMPD-Q or simplified IMPD)
pathways.legalBasis: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 (Articles 5, 25, 61-63; Annex I IMPD and GMP documentation; Annex VI labelling); Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569; Detailed Commission guidelines on GMP for IMPs C(2017) 8179
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: IMPD quality part structured on ICH CTD Module 3 (S drug substance, P investigational medicinal product, A appendices). Concise and tabular, with each section prefaced by a table of contents and glossary. A simplified IMPD (Annex I Table 1) can be used for products authorised in the EU or an ICH country: the SmPC substitutes for quality data when the product is unmodified; P and A data are needed when it is modified (e.g. blinded). A placebo may be limited to quality data. Modality guidelines: EMA/CHMP/QWP/545525/2017 Rev. 2 (chemical, including radiopharmaceuticals), EMA/CHMP/BWP/534898/2008 Rev. 2 (biological), EMA/CAT/22473/2025 (ATMP). Quality data sit in Part I, which the Member States assess jointly through the reporting Member State.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: The EMA IMP guidelines scale quality data with development stage. Phase 1 centres on safety-relevant quality: impurity profile versus toxicology batches, sterility and viral/adventitious agent safety, and stability over the trial. Analytical methods need only be shown suitable, with validation parameters tabulated. Phase 2-3 adds more process detail, tabulated validation results, specifications justified by accumulated batch data, comparability for process changes (biologics) and updated stability. ATMP data may be risk-adapted under EMA/CAT/22473/2025. Phase-scaling details are unverified against the guideline PDFs (low confidence); frequent IMPD deficiencies are unjustified specifications, missing stability data and incomplete manufacturing-control descriptions (Ther Innov Regul Sci 2026, DOI 10.1007/s43441-026-01046-3).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: IMPs must be made under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 and the detailed GMP-IMP guideline C(2017) 8179. The 2010 Annex 13 has no application to EU/EEA trials since 30 January 2025. Investigational ATMPs follow EudraLex Vol. 4 Part IV, which is under revision (EMA/INS/GMP/48771/2025). Manufacture or import needs an Article 61 MIA with a QP; Article 61(5) exempts certain hospital processes, e.g. diagnostic radiopharmaceutical preparation. Each batch is QP-certified (Article 62), then released by the sponsor before shipment. IMPs made in a third country and not authorised in the EU or an ICH country need a QP declaration of GMP equivalence (EudraLex Vol. 10 template). Unauthorised or modified auxiliary medicinal products must be made under GMP or an equivalent standard.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: GMP compliance documentation in Part I: none for authorised, unmodified IMPs. Otherwise, a copy of the Article 61 MIA, plus a QP declaration of GMP equivalence for non-EU manufacture of products not authorised in the EU or an ICH country. CTIS has been mandatory for new CTAs since 31 January 2023 and for all trials since the transition ended (30 January 2025). Quality changes with substantial impact go through Part I substantial modifications. IMP labelling follows CTR Annex VI. The Commission/CTCG CTR Q&A (EudraLex Vol. 10) is the implementation reference; cite its current version, which is not confirmed here.
pathways.language: Part I quality documents (IMPD) are generally accepted in English by most Member States. Part II documents and labelling follow each Member State's national language requirements, as published in EudraLex Vol. 10. Not verified per Member State.

pathways.applicationName: Marketing Authorisation Application (MAA) - centralised procedure under Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, or MRP/DCP/national under Directive 2001/83/EC
pathways.legalBasis: Directive 2001/83/EC Article 8(3) (and other legal bases, e.g. Article 10a) and Annex I (Module 3; Part IV for ATMPs); Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Regulation (EU) 2017/745 Article 117 for integral drug-device combinations. The pharmaceutical reform (COM(2023) 192/193) is pending; its adoption was not confirmed as of 2026-10.
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Full CTD Module 3 (3.2.S, 3.2.P, 3.2.A, 3.2.R) and a Module 2.3 QOS in eCTD with EU Module 1. The active substance may be supported by an EDQM CEP or an ASMF (Applicant's Part, plus a Restricted Part sent directly to the authorities, with a letter of access).
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Commercial-stage expectations: process validation data (or, for standard processes, an EU 3.2.R process validation scheme completed before commercial release); specifications justified on clinical and commercial batches; formal ICH stability data; and a nitrosamine risk evaluation for the active substance and finished product.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to the MAA itself. Commercial manufacture follows EU GMP (EudraLex Vol. 4 Parts I-IV and Annexes, including the 2022 Annex 1 for sterile products). Commission Directive (EU) 2017/1572 on GMP principles was not verified. QP batch certification follows Annex 16. A QP declaration on active substance GMP (EMA template) goes in Module 1.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: EU 3.2.R contains the drug product process validation scheme, medical device information (MDR Article 117 conformity evidence or notified body opinion), CEPs, and TSE information for materials of animal/human origin. Module 1 holds the QP declaration(s) on active substance GMP, the ASMF letter of access and CEP copies. Nitrosamine expectations follow the EMA nitrosamine Q&A (CPCA for NDSRIs).
pathways.language: Centralised procedure: dossier, including Module 3, in English; product information in all official EU languages. National/MRP/DCP: per Member State; an English Module 3 is widely accepted. Not verified.

pathways.applicationName: Variations to marketing authorisations (Type IA/IAIN, IB, II, extensions) under Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008 as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701
pathways.legalBasis: Commission Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008 as amended (including Regulation (EU) No 712/2012 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1701); the revised Commission variations classification guidelines replacing 2013/C 223/01. Application dates of the 2024/2025 instruments not verified.
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Variation application form (Module 1) plus updated Module 3 sections, and Module 2.3 where affected, as the classification category requires.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Post-approval only. Documentation and procedure depend on the variation category, including grouping/worksharing and post-approval change management protocols.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable. Changes to manufacturing sites need valid MIA/GMP status and, for active substance sites, an updated QP declaration.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Nitrosamine-driven changes are implemented through variations. Switching an approved manufacturer from an ASMF to a CEP can take several variations: in a 2025 case study across 38 EEA MAs it took four, one authority asked for a fifth, and the same change was classified IA, IB or II in different countries. Classification codes must follow the guidelines in force on the submission date.
pathways.language: Centralised: English. National/MRP/DCP: per Member State.

pathways.applicationName: IND - Investigational New Drug Application (CMC section per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)); covers drugs and PHS Act biologics, including cell and gene therapies
pathways.legalBasis: FD&C Act section 505(i) and 21 CFR Part 312: 312.23(a)(7) CMC, 312.23(c) translations, 312.6 labeling, 312.31 information amendments, 312.33 annual reports. CGMP: FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B) and 21 CFR 210.2(c), which exempts most Phase 1 products from Part 211. Environmental: 21 CFR 25.31(e). DMF referencing: 21 CFR 314.420 and the 2024 BLA/Master Files final rule. eCTD: FD&C Act 745A(a) for commercial INDs.
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: There is no separate IMPD-style quality dossier. Commercial INDs must be eCTD, with CMC under ICH M4Q Module 3 headings: 3.2.S, 3.2.P (placebo usually as its own 3.2.P), 3.2.A appendices (facilities, adventitious agents) and 3.2.R. A Module 2.3 QOS is recommended but not required. Content is phase-graded, and not every CTD section must be completed in the original IND. Noncommercial INDs (investigator-sponsored, expanded access) are exempt from eCTD. Labeling and the environmental claim go in Module 1. M4Q(R2) is a draft and does not yet change the format.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Phase 1: focus on identifying and controlling raw materials and drug substance, with no final specifications expected (312.23). The 1995 guidance asks for a statement of CMC risk signals and a link between clinical and toxicology material, accepts preliminary tabular stability data, and does not expect validation data or established specifications. FDA's 2026 FIH clarifications, for CDER small molecules and recombinant biologics, set at least 1 month of representative-lot stability (no degradation), no clinical-lot or full-duration stability, no method validation, and no non-safety process controls; for recombinant products, no full orthogonal characterization, no product-specific viral clearance study, and a potency assay only where warranted. Phase 2/3 (small molecules, 2003 guidance): CMC safety information goes in information amendments before each phase, and corroborating information is generated during the phase and summarized in annual reports. Scale-up and other changes are reported through 'Information Amendment: CMC'. Cell and gene therapies follow CBER's 2020 gene therapy guidance, 2008 somatic cell therapy guidance and the May 2026 flexibilities guidance (permissive early release criteria; defined acceptance criteria before Phase 2/3; risk-based comparability).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Phase 1: most investigational drugs, including biological drugs, are exempt from 21 CFR Part 211 under 210.2(c) but must meet statutory CGMP per FDA's July 2008 Phase 1 CGMP guidance (not applicable to section-361-only HCT/Ps). Phase 2/3: full Part 211 applies, plus Parts 600-680 for biologics as applicable. A product already supplied for Phase 2/3 or lawfully marketed must meet Part 211 even in a later Phase 1 study. There is no QP certification or GMP-certificate requirement for IND supply; FDA oversees compliance through inspection.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: No EU-style QP declaration. Letters of authorization are needed to reference Type II, III or V DMFs; DMFs and all DMF correspondence must be eCTD since 2018-05-05. INDs for PHS Act biologics may reference any master file information. The immediate package must carry the 312.6 caution statement. Include a claim of categorical exclusion under 25.31(e) or an EA. Nitrosamine and M7 risk should be addressed during development so they are resolved before the NDA. eCTD v4.0 is accepted for new INDs since 2024-09-16. Optional programs include the CDRP pilot (through FY2027) and Phase 1 IND Navigator resources (Operation TrialBlazer, 2026).
pathways.language: English. Non-English parts need accurate and complete English translations, with copies of the original publications (21 CFR 312.23(c)).

pathways.applicationName: NDA (FD&C Act 505(b)(1)/(b)(2); 21 CFR 314.50) and BLA (PHS Act 351(a); 21 CFR 601.2) - CTD Module 2.3 and Module 3
pathways.legalBasis: FD&C Act section 505(b) and 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1) (CMC) and 314.50(e) (samples); PHS Act section 351(a) and 21 CFR 601.2. Master files: 21 CFR 314.420 and the 2024 BLA/Master Files final rule (89 FR 9743). Post-approval protocols: 21 CFR 314.70(e) and 601.12(e). CGMP: 21 CFR 210/211, plus 600, 606 and 820 as applicable. eCTD: FD&C Act 745A(a).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Full ICH M4Q CTD in eCTD, mandatory since 2017-05-05 (v3.2.2, or v4.0 for new applications since 2024-09-16): Module 2.3 QOS plus Module 3 (3.2.S, 3.2.P, 3.2.A, 3.2.R). The US 3.2.R regional section holds executed batch records (3.2.R.1.S/3.2.R.1.P.1), comparability protocols (3.2.R.2.S/3.2.R.2.P) and the methods validation package (3.2.R.3.S/3.2.R.3.P). Q12 established conditions, PACMPs and the PLCM document may be included. M4Q(R2) is a draft (January 2026) and not yet in force.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Marketing-stage expectations: commercial specifications justified per Q6A/Q6B; impurity thresholds per Q3A(R2)/Q3B(R2), Q3C(R8), Q3D(R2) and M7(R2); nitrosamine risk assessment and confirmatory testing; analytical procedures validated per Q2(R2) and developed per Q14; methods validation package, with samples on FDA request; registration stability per Q1A(R2) (consolidated Q1 pending); pharmaceutical and process development per Q8(R2)/Q11/Q9(R1); continuous manufacturing per Q13; viral safety per Q5A(R2) and comparability per Q5E for biologics; lifecycle process validation with PPQ before commercial distribution. For cell and gene therapy BLAs, the May 2026 flexibilities allow a scientifically justified number of PPQ batches and flexible commercial specifications.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to the marketing pathway itself. Commercial manufacture must comply fully with 21 CFR Parts 210/211, plus Parts 600/606/820 as applicable for biologics and combination products, as stated in 601.2 for BLAs. Clinical supplies under the IND remain subject to the IND CGMP regime above.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: NDAs may reference Type II DMFs for drug substance via LOA. BLAs may not reference master files for drug substance, drug substance intermediate or drug product information, apart from transition products. The US-specific 3.2.R content is listed above. A claim of categorical exclusion or an environmental assessment is required under 21 CFR Part 25. FDA may request samples for methods verification (314.50(e)). Comparability protocols may be included at filing to support future post-approval changes (2022 guidance). Nitrosamine and NDSRI acceptable intakes follow FDA's live webpage. Drafts to monitor: Q1 (Step 4 projected November 2026), Q3E (projected June 2027), the August 2026 container closure draft, M4Q(R2), and the AI credibility framework.
pathways.language: English (US regulatory submissions are made in English; translation provisions for NDAs were not verified in this research).

pathways.applicationName: Clinical Trial Notification (治験計画届, CTN)
pathways.legalBasis: PMD Act (Act No. 145 of 1960, as amended; in force in its PMD Act form since November 2014) Art. 80-2, including the 30-day waiting period after a first CTN. The 30-day period is corroborated by PMC12771677; the article number is not verified. PMD Act Enforcement Regulations (MHW Ordinance No. 1 of 1961), CTN provisions (article numbers not verified). J-GCP (MHW Ordinance No. 28 of 1997) Arts. 5, 8, 16 and 17 (article numbers not verified). CTN handling notification, recalled as 薬生薬審発0831第10号 of 2020-08-31 (identifier and current revision not verified). Cell and gene therapy products fall under the PMD Act's regenerative-medical-product provisions (corroborated).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: There is no CTD Module 3 or IMPD-style quality dossier. The CTN form carries the IMP particulars: code or name, ingredients and quantities, dosage form, route, manufacturing site(s) and planned supply quantity. Quality information is presented in the investigator's brochure (治験薬概要書, J-GCP Art. 8) and in the document stating why the trial is scientifically justified. PMDA completes its review of a first CTN, including any document amendments, within 30 calendar days. Which quality data PMDA typically asks for in that review was not verified.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: A notification, not an approval. Before the trial, the sponsor must have finished the quality, toxicity and pharmacology studies needed to request it (J-GCP Art. 5). Under 治験薬GMP, process and analytical-method validation is built up stepwise as development proceeds. The first CTN for a drug carries a 30-day wait, during which PMDA completes its review; sites can be contracted from day 31, and about half of first-in-Japan studies at one site started within 70 days of CTN submission (PMC12771677). That later CTNs and change notifications have no 30-day wait was not independently verified. PMDA consultations (e.g. pre-Phase 1, quality) are available, and early use is associated with shorter later reviews (PMID 29714577).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Investigational Product GMP (治験薬GMP): notification 薬食発第0709002号 of 2008-07-09, superseding 薬発第480号 of 1997 (identifiers recalled, not verified). IMPs made outside Japan must meet an equivalent standard. Not established as of 2026-10-04: whether a revision aligning with PIC/S Annex 13 or the newer EU IMP GMP has been issued. The GMP-equivalent standard for investigational regenerative medical products was not researched.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: IMP labels must be in Japanese, say the product is for clinical trial use, and must not show the planned brand name, indications or dosage (J-GCP Art. 16; not verified). Human- and animal-derived materials are subject to the Standard for Biological Ingredients (生物由来原料基準); how it is applied at CTN was not verified. Gene therapy and other LMO IMPs need Cartagena Act clearance (Type 1 or Type 2). Cell and gene therapy products are regenerative medical products (再生医療等製品), not drugs (corroborated). Gene therapy quality and safety expectations are in the notification cited as No. 0709-2 (identifier not verified). Changes to notified items, including IMP manufacturing sites, need a CTN change notification. Japan has no QP-declaration equivalent.
pathways.language: Japanese for the CTN form and its required entries. Not verified: whether the IB or protocol may be filed in English, possibly with a Japanese summary, under recent drug-loss measures.

pathways.applicationName: Marketing approval application (製造販売承認申請, J-NDA) and post-approval changes (一部変更承認申請 / 軽微変更届 / change-plan confirmation)
pathways.legalBasis: PMD Act Art. 14 (approval, partial change approval, minor change notification, GMP conformity inspection); Art. 14-7-2 (change-plan confirmation, the statutory PACMP, recalled as added by Act No. 63 of 2019); Art. 13-3 (foreign manufacturer accreditation); Arts. 41 and 56 (Japanese Pharmacopoeia); Art. 80-6 (Master File). No article number is verified. Enforcement Regulations Art. 47 (minor change scope; role corroborated by PMID 40839206). MHLW notifications: 薬食審査発第0210001号 (2005-02-10, application form entries and change-category annotations; corroborated by PMID 40839206); 薬食発1121第2号 (2014-11-21); 医薬審発第899号 (2001-06-21, CTD); 薬食審査発1117第3号 (2014-11-17, MF); and a 2021-07-30 notification on the specifications and test methods column (identifier not verified). ICH Q12 has applied in Japan since 2021 (PMID 40839206).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: ICH CTD: Japanese Module 1 plus Modules 2–5, with Module 3 following ICH M4Q and 2.3 as the QOS. Separately, the approval application form (承認申請書) carries legally binding 製造方法 and 規格及び試験方法 entries. Since 2005 each entry has been annotated with symbols fixing whether a later change needs partial change approval or minor change notification, and MHLW treats these annotated approved matters as equivalent to ICH Q12 established conditions (PMID 40839206). Electronic submission is via Japanese eCTD; whether eCTD v4.0 is now mandatory was not verified.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Marketing stage. A full commercial-scale quality package is needed: data category ロ (manufacturing, specifications and test methods) and data category ハ (stability: long-term, stress and accelerated). There is a GMP conformity inspection at approval and periodic re-inspection, recalled as five-yearly. Post-approval routes: partial change approval before implementation; minor change notification after implementation, within the Art. 47 scope (30-day timing recalled); or notification under a confirmed change plan (PACMP). Japan has had no separate risk-based post-approval change classification guideline like those of the US and EU. A notification of 2024-09-30 allowing risk-based changes was reported, but its identifier and implementing guidelines were not established (PMID 40839206).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to the marketing application. Commercial drug manufacture must meet the GMP Ministerial Ordinance (MHLW Ordinance No. 179 of 2004), recalled as amended by Ordinance No. 90 of 2021 effective 2021-08-01 (PQS, QA unit, data reliability); not verified. Japan applied to PIC/S in March 2012 (corroborated); the 2014-07-01 accession is recalled, not verified. Regenerative medical products are under a separate GCTP standard (not verified).
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Japanese Module 1 includes: a copy of the application form, certificates, patent status, development history, foreign use status, a list of similar drugs, a draft package insert, nonproprietary-name documents, data for poisonous or powerful drug designation, a draft RMP and a list of attachments. Foreign manufacturers must be accredited (外国製造業者認定). The Master File (原薬等登録原簿) system exists (PMID 27518176): the MF number is cited in the application, the applicant contracts with the holder, and a foreign holder appoints an in-country caretaker (details not verified). JP-listed drugs must conform to the current Japanese Pharmacopoeia; JP18 was still cited as current in literature through mid-2026, and whether JP19 had been promulgated by 2026-10-04 was not established. Biological-origin materials must meet the Standard for Biological Ingredients. Cell and gene therapy products follow the regenerative-medical-product route, which offers conditional, time-limited approval.
pathways.language: Japanese for the application form, Module 1 and Module 2 (including the 2.3 QOS). Modules 3–5 may be in English (not verified).

pathways.applicationName: Clinical Trial Plan Approval (임상시험계획 승인, Korean IND)
pathways.legalBasis: Pharmaceutical Affairs Act (약사법), recalled as Art. 34 (not verified). Regulations on Safety of Pharmaceuticals, etc. (의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙), recalled as Art. 24 with KGCP/KGMP annexes (not verified). MFDS notification 의약품 임상시험 계획 승인에 관한 규정, cited in PMC7921003 as the 'Guideline for Approving Clinical Study Plans on Drugs' and in force by 2009; current revision not established. Korean IND system introduced December 2002. Advanced biopharmaceuticals are also governed by the Advanced Regenerative Bio Act (enacted 2019-08, implemented 2020).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Manufacturing and quality data for the investigational product: active ingredient and amount, manufacturing method, manufacturer, standard test methods and QC results. GMP compliance documents are also required (PMC7921003). Not verified: whether the data must follow CTD/IMPD structure, what stability data are expected, and any phase-dependent reductions.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Prior approval, trial by trial. MFDS described 30 working days from submission to the first supplementary-data notice (2020), and IND and IRB review may run in parallel. Trials of approved drugs within their approved indication are exempt from IND approval but need IRB approval. Investigator-initiated INDs for previously approved drugs may omit the IB, nonclinical data, prior clinical data and development plan if supporting literature is provided. Changes to approved plans, including CMC changes, need change approval or, for minor items, a change report (not verified).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: GMP compliance documents for the IMP must be submitted with the IND (PMC7921003). Not verified: the specific KGMP standard for IMPs (an annex to the Regulations on Safety and/or the MFDS Regulation on Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Quality Control) and the evidence accepted for IMPs made abroad. MFDS PIC/S membership is recalled as from 2014-07-01 and is not verified.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: IRB approval is required in addition to MFDS approval. Trials must be run under KGCP at MFDS-designated clinical trial institutions. IMP labels are in Korean and state 임상시험용 (not verified). For advanced biopharmaceuticals (cell therapy, gene therapy, tissue-engineered and advanced bio-convergence products), the Advanced Regenerative Bio Act adds MFDS manufacturer/importer licensing, human-cell management licensing with donor suitability assessment, and long-term follow-up. The trial itself follows the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act IND route (PMC9597240). Unlike Japan's CTN, prior approval is needed for each trial.
pathways.language: Korean for the application and the Korean-specific documents. How far English technical attachments are accepted was not verified.

pathways.applicationName: Product approval (품목허가) — new drug marketing application
pathways.legalBasis: Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, recalled as Art. 31 (not verified). Regulations on Safety of Pharmaceuticals, etc. MFDS notification 의약품의 품목허가·신고·심사 규정 (Regulation on Approval, Notification and Review of Pharmaceuticals). Advanced biopharmaceuticals: also the Advanced Regenerative Bio Act, including expedited review (customised review, priority review, conditional approval on Phase 2 data).
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: ICH CTD: Korea-specific Module 1 plus Modules 2–5, with Module 3 per ICH M4Q (not verified). MFDS has been an ICH Regulatory Member since November 2016 (one secondary source). The date CTD became mandatory for new drugs and the eCTD status were not verified.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Marketing stage: a full commercial quality package, plus a KGMP compliance evaluation of all domestic and overseas sites before approval (not verified). Post-approval CMC changes go through change approval or change notification under MFDS rules, which were not researched.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to the marketing application. Commercial manufacture must meet KGMP, understood to be aligned with PIC/S (not verified). Advanced biopharmaceutical manufacturers and importers need an ARMAB licence with step-by-step quality control from cell collection onward (PMC9597240).
pathways.regionalSpecifics: MFDS operates an ASMF/DMF (원료의약품 등록) procedure (PMID 27518176); its legal basis and link to product approval were not verified. Korean Pharmacopoeia (대한민국약전) compliance applies where monographs exist; the current edition was not verified.
pathways.language: Korean for the application and Module 1. Acceptance of English Module 3 data was not verified.

pathways.applicationName: DDCM (Dossiê de Desenvolvimento Clínico de Medicamento) + DEEC (Dossiê Específico de Ensaio Clínico)
pathways.legalBasis: RDC nº 945/2024 (reported in force 2025-01-01; replaced RDC 9/2015); IN nº 338/2024 as amended by IN nº 345/2025 (reliance / optimized review)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: DPI (Dossiê do Produto sob Investigação) or IMPD within the DDCM, covering the active substance and the investigational medicine (RDC 945 Art. 28, item list known only from summaries). The RDC 945/IN 338 Q&A recommends the CTD Module 3 structure (ICH M4). Under reliance, the DPI/IMPD must be identical to the version approved by an AREE.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: One DDCM covers the clinical development plan, with one DEEC per trial. Partial data may be submitted continuously before the definitive DDCM. Phase IV and non-interventional trials are reported to be exempt from Anvisa review (ethics only). IN 338 allows lighter review through reliance or risk/complexity assessment; for registered or AREE-approved products, modified products and FDCs, only the modification data are reviewed. The sources found do not detail phase-specific quality data expectations under RDC 945, and the promised complementary quality act is still pending.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: RDC 658/2022 (general GMP, covering investigational medicines) plus IN 136/2022, which adopts the PIC/S IMP GMP guideline. ANVISA has been a PIC/S Participating Authority since 2021-01-01. The sponsor must ensure the investigational medicine, comparators and placebo are made under GMP, and coded and labelled to protect blinding.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Reported (secondary sources only, low confidence): primary petitions are reviewed in 90 working days, with release by lapse of time (Resolução-RE in the DOU) if Anvisa does not act. The DEEC is due within 15 working days of DDCM issuance. AREE list in IN 338/2024 as amended; read the consolidated text. Substantial modifications to the investigational product are secondary petitions. ANVISA has been an ICH regulatory member since November 2016.
pathways.language: Portuguese for Anvisa forms and petitions. Whether English technical documents such as the IMPD are accepted under RDC 945/2024 was not verified; check the DDCM/DEEC manual.

pathways.applicationName: Registro de medicamento (marketing registration) – synthetic/semisynthetic (RDC 753/2022) or biological (RDC 55/2010)
pathways.legalBasis: RDC nº 948/2024 (general regularization requirements, in force 2025-01-01); RDC nº 753/2022 (synthetic/semisynthetic; revoked RDC 200/2017); RDC nº 55/2010 (biologicals, amended 2024; current consolidated status unverified); RDC nº 359/2020 (DIFA/CADIFA for APIs)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: CTD format recommended per Guia nº 24. Version 1 (2019) made it optional. Version 2 (2026-04-25, published 2026-05-04, open for comment until 2026-11-04) is reported to fold in the CADIFA flow. API data go through DIFA/CADIFA.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Full commercial-scale quality dossier (Module 3 content) at registration. Post-registration changes follow the post-registration rules (not mapped here).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to registration. Commercial GMP is under RDC 658/2022 and its INs, and GMP certification is required.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: CADIFA for APIs of new, innovative, generic and similar medicines. Electronic filing is reported (unverified) as part of Guia 24 v2. The long-term stability condition Anvisa requires was not verified in this corpus.
pathways.language: Portuguese (administrative). Rules on the language of technical documents were not verified.

pathways.applicationName: Clinical trial permission – Form CT-04 (application) / Form CT-06 (permission); manufacture for trials CT-10/CT-11; import for trials CT-16
pathways.legalBasis: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 (G.S.R. 227(E), 2019-03-19), under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; as amended by the NDCT (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 46(E), 2026-01-20)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Second Schedule data, including chemical and pharmaceutical information: identity and structure, physicochemical properties, composition, specifications with pharmacopoeial references, API source, identification, assay and impurity methods with reference standards, and accelerated and real-time stability. The sources found do not mandate the IMPD or CTD Module 3 format for trial applications.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: The Second Schedule sets data by trial type and phase; the phase-specific CMC table was not read verbatim. Decision within 90 working days, or 30 for drugs discovered or developed in India and to be made and marketed there. Deemed approval on silence applies only to that 30-working-day route. CT-06 is reported valid for 2 years (secondary sources).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E), 2023-12-28) includes a part on investigational pharmaceutical products for human trials. It has applied to large manufacturers since 2024-06-28 and to all manufacturers since 2026-01-01. Since 2026, manufacture solely for analytical or non-clinical testing can proceed on prior intimation, except for high-risk categories.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Zone IVb stability conditions are cited as 30 °C/75% RH long-term and 40 °C/75% RH accelerated; check the Gazette text. Test-licence timelines (rules 53 and 60) are reported as 45 working days since 2026. Submissions go through CDSCO's SUGAM online portal. India is not a PIC/S participant. CDSCO's ICH observer status rests only on ICH Assembly minutes (low confidence).
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: New drug permission – Form CT-18 (import application) / Form CT-21 (manufacture application); permissions CT-19/CT-20 (import of API/formulation) and CT-23 (manufacture of formulation)
pathways.legalBasis: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 (new-drug approval chapters and Second Schedule); CDSCO CTD Guidance (28.10.2010)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: CTD (five modules, quality in Module 3) per CDSCO's 2010 CTD guidance. For biologics, also CDSCO's 2008 Guidance for Industry on quality information (current status unconfirmed).
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Full quality dossier at marketing application. A local clinical-trial waiver is possible for drugs approved in countries the CLA specifies (rule 101, per secondary sources).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable. Commercial manufacture must comply with revised Schedule M (all manufacturers since 2026-01-01).
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Zone IVb stability conditions. Permission decisions within 90 working days per secondary sources. Form numbers for API manufacture permission were not mapped.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: Clinical Trial Authorisation (CTA) / Clinical Trial Notification (CTN) / Clinical Trial Certificate (CTC)
pathways.legalBasis: Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2016 (S 331/2016, in operation 2016-11-01); Health Products (Clinical Research Materials) Regulations 2016 (S 332/2016); Health Products (CTGTP) Regulations 2021 (CTGTP framework, from 2021-03-01); Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2016 (S 335/2016, CTC route)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: No full IMPD is routinely required for therapeutic-product CTAs. Required: the GMP certificate of the finished-product manufacturer (and of the drug-substance manufacturer for biologics and Class 2 CTGTPs), or a GMP declaration; certificates of analysis for study batches; the investigator's brochure for unregistered products; and CMC information when HSA requests it. Class 2 CTGTPs need a full CMC dossier per GN-ATPB-1-4.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: CTA review 30 working days (15 for phase 1 BA/BE, food-effect or DDI trials; 60 for Class 2 CTGTP trials); CTN 5 working days (per GN-IOCTB-04 as summarised). The quality package is largely the same across phases; HSA asks for CMC data case by case.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: GMP evidence is required for all unregistered investigational and auxiliary products. HSA has participated in PIC/S since 2000. That HSA applies PIC/S Annex 13 as the IMP GMP reference is assumed, not confirmed by an HSA document in this research. Labelling follows HSA's IP/AP labelling guidance (GN-IOCTB-07).
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Filed on PRISM. A CRM notification is required before importing unregistered clinical research materials (valid one year). CTGTPs are classed Class 1 or Class 2 since 2021-03-01; before that, high-risk cell, tissue and gene therapy products were trialled under a CTC under the Medicines Act. HSA has been an ICH regulatory member since November 2017.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: Therapeutic product registration (NDA / GDA); Class 2 CTGTP registration
pathways.legalBasis: Health Products Act and Health Products (Therapeutic Products) Regulations 2016; Health Products (CTGTP) Regulations 2021 for CTGTPs; HSA Guidance on Therapeutic Product Registration in Singapore (updated 2026-04-01)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: ICH CTD (quality in Module 3, QOS in Module 2.3) or ASEAN CTD (quality in Part II). eCTD accepted voluntarily since 2026-04-01 (ICH v3.2.2, SG-HSA v1.1). CTGTP CMC follows GN-ATPB-1-4.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Full commercial quality dossier at registration.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable. For NCE/NBE applications, applicants may ask HSA to inspect overseas drug-substance sites that lack GMP evidence (since 2026-01-16).
pathways.regionalSpecifics: A declaration that the CMC dossier contains no known quality defects requiring update is reported to be required from 2026-06-01 (secondary sources, low confidence). The CTD format cannot be changed after submission.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: WHO Prequalification of medicines – product dossier (FPP)
pathways.legalBasis: Procedure for prequalification of pharmaceutical products, WHO TRS 1067 Annex 4 (2026), presumed successor of the TRS 961 (2011) procedure; quality-part guideline TRS 970 Annex 4 (2012); stability guideline TRS 1010 Annex 10 (2018)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: CTD-Quality per ICH M4Q: Quality Overall Summary (Module 2.3) and Module 3, using WHO terms (API, FPP, product dossier). TRS 986 Annex 6 is the counterpart for national regulators.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Marketing stage (prequalification) only. WHO has no clinical-trial application route; the national CTA applies. WHO GMP for investigational products (TRS 1044 Annex 7; the IAEA/WHO investigational radiopharmaceutical guideline for radiopharmaceuticals) is the normative GMP reference.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: WHO GMP for investigational products, TRS 1044 Annex 7 (2022), which replaced TRS 863 Annex 7 (1996). IAEA/WHO GMP for investigational radiopharmaceutical products, reported as TRS 1044 Annex 3 (2022); confirm the annex title.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Stability per TRS 1010 Annex 10. Long-term conditions follow the target market's climatic zone, e.g. zone IVb (30 °C/75% RH) for hot and very humid markets.
pathways.language: English (assumed for WHO PQ submissions; not verified in this research)

pathways.applicationName: UK Clinical Trial Authorisation (CTA) via combined MHRA/REC review (IRAS)
pathways.legalBasis: The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 (SI 2004/1031), as amended, including by SI 2006/1928, the 2019 EU-exit clinical trials amendments (SI 2019/744; title attribution unverified) and the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (full effect 2026-04-28; SI number not verified)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: An IMPD quality section using the EU IMPD-Q headings (2.1.S drug substance, 2.1.P IMP, 2.1.A appendices), or a simplified IMPD. For an unmodified UK-authorised product the SmPC can replace the quality IMPD. Not a full CTD Module 3.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: MHRA applies the EU IMP quality guidelines. At early phase, acceptable content includes provisional specifications, confirmation of analytical suitability with tabulated validation parameters, batch analyses linked to the toxicology batches, and stability covering the trial duration with a shelf-life extension protocol. Detail grows towards phase 3: tighter specifications justified by batch data, validated methods, and a process closer to commercial. Biologics need adventitious agents and viral safety data scaled to the phase. Specifications, stability data and manufacturing-control descriptions are the most frequently cited IMPD deficiencies (PMID 42754766).
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: UK GMP, including Annex 13 (the 2010 text, retained in Great Britain). An MIA(IMP) is needed to manufacture, assemble or import, with limited exemptions such as hospital assembly. A QP certifies each batch. IMPs from listed approved countries (EU/EEA) are imported under QP oversight without re-certification. IMPs from other third countries are QP-certified in the UK against GMP equivalent to UK GMP.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: A single IRAS combined review goes to MHRA and the HRA/REC. Statutory clock under the 2004 text: first review within 30 days; sponsor reply to grounds for non-acceptance within 14 days; decision within 60 days; substantial amendments within 35 days. Under the 2025 regulations the reply to a request for information can be extended to up to 60 days (PMID 41047928, MHRA authors). An administrative notification scheme for lower-risk phase 3/4 trials has run since October 2023, and the 2025 regulations make notifiable lower-risk trials statutory. The 2025 regulations also add registration and results-publication duties and are implemented alongside ICH E6(R3) (PMID 41758490). Quality changes are substantial amendments (modifications under the 2025 regulations). MHRA continues to apply EU guidelines in force on 2020-12-31 unless it says otherwise. Not verified: Northern Ireland/Windsor Framework specifics, the 2025 SI number, and the 2025 changes to IMP labelling and manufacturing exemptions.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: UK national Marketing Authorisation (150-day national route; International Recognition Procedure; Access work-sharing)
pathways.legalBasis: The Human Medicines Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/1916), Part 5 and Schedule 8; MHRA International Recognition Procedure guidance (in operation since 2024-01-01)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: Full ICH CTD: Module 2.3 QOS and Module 3 (3.2.S, 3.2.P, 3.2.A, 3.2.R) to ICH M4Q(R1), with the UK Module 1, submitted electronically (eCTD) to MHRA. M4Q(R2) is in development.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Marketing standard: validated analytical procedures, process validation or a validation scheme, ICH Q1A(R2) stability for the proposed shelf life, and full justification of the control strategy. Phase scaling does not apply.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to the MA itself. For commercial supply, UK manufacturer's licence (MIA) holders and QP certification of batches for the GB market are required, and a QP declaration on active substance GMP goes in Module 1.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: The QP declaration on active substance GMP goes in Module 1. Active substance data may come from the UK ASMF procedure or a CEP. BP and Ph. Eur. monographs must be complied with. The IRP (since 2024-01-01; replaced the ECDRP and the MRDC reliance procedure) relies on approvals by seven reference regulators: TGA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, HSA, PMDA, FDA, and EMA or EU/EEA member-state authorities. Recognition A requires a reference approval within 2 years and Recognition B within 10 years (PMID 41248376). The A and B timetables (believed 60 and 110 days) are not verified. MHRA has been an Access Consortium member since October 2020 and is a Project Orbis partner. ICH membership (believed Regulatory Member since 2022) is not verified. Acceptance of EU/EEA batch testing under approved-country rules must be confirmed.
pathways.language: English

pathways.applicationName: Swissmedic clinical trial authorisation (Category B/C), with cantonal ethics committee approval via BASEC
pathways.legalBasis: Therapeutic Products Act (TPA, SR 812.21); Human Research Act (HRA, SR 810.30); Clinical Trials Ordinance (ClinO, SR 810.305), revised text in force 2024-11-01 (not verified). Risk-based categorisation has applied since January 2014.
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: An IMP quality dossier (an IMPD quality section in the EU IMPD-Q structure is accepted), or Swiss product information for an authorised product used unmodified. GMP evidence for the IMP is required, as ClinO's Swissmedic document annex lists.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Swissmedic follows the EU IMP quality guidelines (chemical and biological), so the same phase scaling applies: provisional specifications and method-suitability summaries early, fuller validation and justified specifications in later phases.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Swiss manufacture needs a Swissmedic manufacturing licence. GMP under the MPLO follows the PIC/S GMP Guide, including Annex 13. The licence holder's responsible person (fachtechnisch verantwortliche Person) releases batches. For foreign-made IMPs the sponsor documents GMP compliance and QP release. Mutual recognition applies under EU–CH MRA Chapter 15 and the UK–CH MRA; IMP coverage is to be confirmed.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Risk categories A, B and C are set by Swiss authorisation status and use per the product information (PMID 26122923). Category A needs ethics approval only; B and C also need Swissmedic authorisation. In practice, published protocols for Swiss medicinal-product trials cite both a BASEC (ethics) number and a Swissmedic authorisation number (PMID 39578038; PMID 40601599). Not verified: parallel submission to Swissmedic and the ethics committee, Swissmedic approval of substantial quality changes before implementation, the 2024 ClinO transparency obligations, Swissmedic guidance identifiers and current annex numbering.
pathways.language: German, French, Italian or English; English is generally accepted for scientific documents (IMPD, IB, protocol), and participant-facing documents are in the local language. Not verified.

pathways.applicationName: Swiss Marketing Authorisation (standard, fast-track, temporary authorisation, procedure with prior notification, Art. 13 TPA, Access work-sharing)
pathways.legalBasis: TPA (SR 812.21) Art. 9 ff. and Art. 13; Therapeutic Products Ordinance (TPO/VAM, SR 812.212.21); Swissmedic Ordinance on the Requirements for the Marketing Authorisation of Medicinal Products (AMZV, SR 812.212.22)
pathways.qualityDossierFormat: ICH CTD: Module 2.3 and Module 3 to ICH M4Q, with the Swiss Module 1. The electronic format (eCTD) is set by Swissmedic's formal-requirements guidance.
pathways.phaseAppropriate: Marketing standard. AMZV quality requirements apply, together with the ICH Q guidelines Swissmedic implements as an ICH member. Phase scaling does not apply.
pathways.gmpForInvestigationalProduct: Not applicable to the MA itself. Module 1 must document the GMP status of every manufacturing site (Swissmedic licences, or foreign GMP certificates and MRA evidence). Batch release is by the responsible person under the MPLO.
pathways.regionalSpecifics: Ph. Eur. and Ph. Helv. must be complied with. Under Art. 13 TPA, Swissmedic considers decisions by authorities with comparable control; this needs a dossier identical to the one approved abroad plus the foreign assessment reports (not verified). Peer-reviewed analyses confirm the fast-track procedure and temporary authorisation (introduced 2019) as expedited routes (PMID 42496993; PMID 35731996). Swissmedic met the required review period for 49% of fast-track cancer-drug reviews in 2010–2024 (PMID 41921119). Not verified: the procedure with prior notification, and the ~140-day fast-track and ~330-day standard targets. Swissmedic belongs to the Access Consortium (PMID 38459358) and Project Orbis (PMID 37072651; PMID 41248376), and is an IRP reference regulator for the UK (PMID 41248376).
pathways.language: Module 1 and product information in German, French and/or Italian; English generally accepted for Modules 2–5. Not verified.

notes.topic: Which ICH analytical-procedure guidelines are current, and what did Q2(R2) and Q14 replace?
notes.phase: all (full Q2(R2) validation expected at marketing; phase-appropriate earlier)
notes.summary: ICH adopted the revised Q2(R2) (Validation of Analytical Procedures) and the new Q14 (Analytical Procedure Development) as Step 4 harmonised guidelines on 1 November 2023. Q2(R2) replaces Q2(R1) (2005). Q14 is the first ICH guidance on how analytical procedures are developed. The two are written to be used together: Q14 development knowledge, including robustness, feeds the Q2(R2) validation. Write new validation protocols and Module 3 validation summaries in Q2(R2) terms. Do not repeat legacy Q2(R1) validations by default; gap-assess them. Where each region's effective date matters for a filing, confirm it on that regulator's site.
keyPoints: Q2(R2) and Q14 were adopted as ICH harmonised guidelines on 2023-11-01 [PMID:40154788; PMID:41299187].

Q2(R2) supersedes Q2(R1). Cassidy et al. list 56 specific omissions, expansions and additions between the two. Use the list as a gap-assessment checklist for SOPs and legacy validation reports [PMID:40154788].
Q14 introduces ICH guidance on analytical procedure development for the first time. It describes minimal and enhanced approaches, with a continuum between them [PMID:40154788; PMID:39111548].
Many Q14 concepts are carried into Q2(R2), so the two should be applied as a pair [PMID:40154788].
Analytical procedures go in 3.2.S.4.2 and 3.2.P.5.2, and their validation in 3.2.S.4.3 and 3.2.P.5.3, under the existing CTD quality structure (ICH M4Q(R1)). Q2(R2)/Q14 do not change these locations.

Cassidy et al. (2025) report that multiple regulators have officially incorporated Q2(R2)/Q14 and others are in process. Exact effective dates at FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, Health Canada and TGA were NOT verified in this research [PMID:40154788].
commonDeficiencies: When the toolkit was published, no official list of Q2(R1)-to-Q2(R2) differences existed. Companies therefore risk keeping SOPs and validation templates on Q2(R1) logic [PMID:40154788].
No regulator-published deficiency statistics specific to Q2(R2)/Q14 were found.
